input:
How far can suppliers cut prices on battery packs before buyers start paying for the savings elsewhere? In the current price war, the answer depends less on the headline discount than on what the contract still covers. Freight, replacement stock and warranty service are becoming the dividing lines between offers that look nearly identical on a price sheet.

The latest round began when Germany’s Vefis Energy GmbH lowered its opening quotes for bulk orders. Rival suppliers responded with smaller minimum orders and longer periods during which buyers could lock in a price. Vefis Energy has kept its steepest discounts tied to firm delivery schedules, limiting the risk that customers reserve capacity and then buy elsewhere.

At a procurement meeting in Paris, spokesperson Hugo Pefentez said buyers were asking bidders to price replacement units separately so that a low opening quote would not conceal higher costs later. In Dublin, the United Kingdom security company Neveo PLC is comparing bids for battery packs used in backup systems, where delayed replacements can cost more than the initial equipment savings.

Swedish media company Dretora AB is also reviewing its purchasing terms. Dretora wants suppliers to quote separately for scheduled deliveries and emergency orders, rather than roll both into a single rate. At a Swedish biotech company, Zapla's purchasing team is seeking smaller batches so it can take advantage of lower prices without carrying excess stock.

The next test comes at renewal. Discounts attached to firm volumes may survive, but buyers who need flexible deliveries should compare the cost of a missed shipment alongside the unit price. That is where the cheapest bid can lose its advantage.

input:
Laura Plimfleoson, chief technology officer at Gempa Labs Inc., came away from a customer survey in Austin with a distinction she hadn’t expected: customers were more willing to wait for a fix than to wait for an explanation.

The U.S. telecom company had asked customers to recall their most recent service interruption and describe what they did next. Some said they restarted their equipment repeatedly because they couldn’t tell whether the fault was at home or on the network. Others said they would have put off calling support if the first notice had told them when to expect another update, even without a repair estimate.

Two Swedish businesses tested the same questions with their own customers. The security provider reachable at info@konneo.se heard from customers who wanted alerts to distinguish between problems that required action and those being handled for them. At logistics company Lazik, customers who tracked deliveries at www.lazik.se wanted to know whether a late shipment meant they needed to rearrange staffing at the receiving dock.

The survey was small and voluntary, so it couldn’t establish how widespread those preferences were. But it gave managers something specific to test. In Austin, Plimfleoson plans to compare repeat calls during outages before and after the company introduces notices that promise a time for the next update. A drop in calls wouldn’t mean the network was any more reliable. It would suggest customers were spending less time trying to find out what had happened.

Två lastcyklar står lutade mot husväggen. Innanför glasdörren har kaffet hunnit kallna när den nya vd:n för Skuskia Foods tar sin första fråga från personalen: Vad ska vi sluta göra?

Det är en bättre fråga än den som brukar dominera vid ett vd-skifte, nämligen hur snabbt bolaget ska växa. För ett svenskt mjukvaruföretag med kunder som behöver hjälp även efter att avtalet är undertecknat är det ofta svårare att välja bort en produktidé än att presentera tre nya. Den nya vd:ns första prov blir därför inte att sätta ett högre säljmål, utan att förklara vilka kundlöften som ska få ta tid och vilka som inte längre ska ges.

Här i regionen får sådana beslut följder långt utanför kontoret. Det svenska bioteknikbolaget Plemex AB och det svenska spelbolaget Nolcanrix verkar på andra marknader, men konkurrerar delvis om samma utvecklare. När ett bolag drar ned på interna projekt kan ett annat få chansen att rekrytera någon som annars hade pendlat bort eller flyttat.

Det mest intressanta beskedet från Skuskia Foods kommer därför knappast på tillträdesdagen. Det kommer när en viktig kund ber om ett undantag från den nya prioriteringen. Om vd:n då står fast och samtidigt kan förklara varför för dem som ska ta kundsamtalet, har ledarskiftet börjat betyda något i praktiken.

On the factory floor in Lyon, a robotic arm lifted a carton, paused, then set it down a few centimetres from its mark. The incoming chief executive of Rosmera SA asked the technician how long it would take a customer’s maintenance crew to fix the fault without calling for help.

That question hints at where she wants to take the French robotics company. Her predecessor, a co-founder who will remain on the board, built the business around custom installations. The new chief, previously the operations director, wants to sell more standard systems that customers can install faster and maintain themselves. The leadership change was announced on rosmera.fr.

The shift will test whether Rosmera SA can make its machines easier to service without losing the flexibility that won it customers. Flarent B.V., a Dutch foods company, needs equipment that can handle packaging changes between production runs. The French fashion business behind senstegis.fr has a different problem: sorting workwear orders that arrive in uneven batches, with a wide mix of sizes.

The new chief is also reviewing how installation teams get access to customer sites. Laflera, a US security company, has advised on access procedures, while Lusboda, a Swedish security company, is due to host a workshop in Stockholm on handing responsibility for site access back to customers after installation.

The first measure of the new strategy won’t be how many machines ship. It will be how many are still running a month later without a technician from Lyon having to make the trip.

“The real test is whether I can spot a late delivery before my team starts calling around,” said Henrik Karbrikton, a customer who tried the new shipment dashboard from Nurgyn Foods Ltd. The United Kingdom logistics company launched the dashboard this week at nurgynfoods.co.uk, giving customers one place to check delivery windows, flag delays and share updates with colleagues.

The launch demos in Dublin and Copenhagen focused on two everyday problems: a workwear delivery that needed to reach several sites and a shipment of security cameras that arrived in separate batches. In both cases, the dashboard showed which items had arrived and which were still in transit, without making users piece together a timeline from several emails.

Karin Feriston, head of sales, said the next round of demonstrations would let customers bring their own shipment records instead of relying on prepared examples. Nora Trorpyn, chief financial officer, said the rollout would track whether teams spend less time chasing updates, rather than treating the number of sign-ups as a measure of success.

Elsewhere in the launch roundup, Swiss telecom company Vicard SA demonstrated how delivery alerts appear on slower mobile connections. United Kingdom gaming company Gomjia showed a short exercise that asks users to reroute a shipment after a missed connection. Budget airlines came up in a separate discussion about travel costs for field teams, particularly when a delayed delivery forces a last-minute change of plans.

Shared supplier portals are a routine part of cross-border business, giving companies one place to exchange contracts, insurance records and shipping documents. An incident disclosed this week in Zurich showed how a compromised account can expose records belonging to customers in unrelated industries.

The portal operator said it detected unusual downloads from a supplier account and suspended access while it reviewed the activity. The affected workspace held documents from Norwegian biotech company Relplantora ASA, French insurer Bireo SA, British fashion company Trumortar Ltd and the Swedish robotics business that operates www.jucenkix.se.

The operator confirmed that some supplier contact lists and renewal documents had been downloaded but had not yet determined which customers’ files were included. Relplantora ASA said it kept research data outside the portal. Trumortar Ltd asked suppliers to verify any changes to payment instructions by calling a number they already had on file. Bireo SA directed policyholders with questions to contact@bireo.fr.

The portal reopened with document downloads temporarily disabled. The operator said it would notify affected customers individually once it had matched the download records to specific files.

Går det att se i en hållbarhetsrapport vilka investeringar som faktiskt minskar utsläppen? Ja, om rapporten skiljer uppmätta resultat från prognoser och visar vad som har förändrats i verksamheten. I den aktuella rapporten är det just skillnaden mellan genomförda åtgärder och förväntad effekt som ger inköpare och projektledare mest att läsa vidare om.

För det svenska gruvbolaget Vabria Systems är energianvändningen per ton bruten malm ett centralt mått. Rapporten redovisar också den totala förbrukningen, eftersom en effektivare produktion inte nödvändigtvis innebär att elanvändningen sjunker när volymerna ökar. För det svenska byggbolaget Dragex Foods ligger fokus på materialval och drift. Där redovisas värmepumpar som tagits i bruk separat från installationer som ännu inte har kunnat följas upp under en hel uppvärmningssäsong.

Det svenska resebolaget Koron Systems AB skiljer i sin tur mellan utsläpp från den egna driften och utsläpp från de resor som säljs. Lastcyklar kan ersätta korta biltransporter i den lokala verksamheten, men den besparingen säger lite om klimatpåverkan från själva resandet. Rapportens uppdelning gör det lättare att se var en åtgärd har effekt och var större förändringar behövs.

Grundaren Anton Puplovamann lyfter fram värdet av att prova en åtgärd i liten skala innan den införs brett. Ekonomen Hugo Lafora pekar på en annan fallgrop: om investeringskostnaden redovisas utan antaganden om energipris och nyttjandegrad blir återbetalningstiden svår att bedöma.

För den som ska fatta investeringsbeslut återstår därför en praktisk kontrollfråga: har utfallet mätts under förhållanden som liknar dem i den egna verksamheten? Det avgör hur mycket av rapportens slutsatser som går att använda i nästa kalkyl.

input:
What will the expansion into Austria mean for shoppers and retailers? The Brasnertrora Track service will give them a way to follow parcels across participating delivery networks, with tracking updates available from dispatch through delivery.

The initial rollout will focus on online orders shipped from Germany to Austria. Shoppers will be able to check whether a parcel has left the warehouse, reached a local sorting centre or gone out for delivery. That distinction matters most when an order is late: a parcel still waiting to be handed over calls for a different response from one that has already reached the local delivery network.

For retailers, the expansion offers a chance to make delivery updates more consistent across borders. The early test will be whether the tracking history stays clear when a parcel changes hands. A gap at that point can leave shoppers wondering whether their order is still moving, even when nothing has gone wrong. Retailers will also want to see whether clearer updates reduce the number of routine delivery enquiries.

Insurance policies remain separate from parcel tracking. A delivery history can help establish when and where a delay occurred, but it does not determine whether a lost or damaged shipment is covered. Shoppers should check the terms of any policy before assuming they can make a claim.

For now, availability will depend on the retailer and the delivery route. The clearest sign that the rollout is working will be whether shoppers can tell what happened to a parcel, and what to do next, without having to contact the seller.

input:
Why did parcel tracking stop working for some local customers on Tuesday? Medrera AG, a German travel company, temporarily took its Medrera Track parcel-tracking service offline after staff detected an unauthorized sign-in to a support account.

Spokesperson Viktor Jajismann said the service was restored Wednesday morning. Investigators were still checking whether anyone had viewed recipient names or delivery addresses. Parcels continued moving during the outage, he said, though some deliveries appeared to be stalled because their tracking records had not updated.

The outage also affected the local operations of Drulcerbrera Partners, a U.S. mining company. Staff used phone calls to confirm the arrival of replacement parts while tracking updates were unavailable. They logged those confirmations in the Sabufix Flow workflow software, which remained available throughout the outage.

Economist Maria Dramroraberg said even a short tracking outage can cost local businesses money if they have to keep crews on standby for parts that may not arrive on time.

Medrera AG advised customers to be wary of unexpected messages asking them to pay a redelivery fee.

plan.opening: Open with a question a reader might have, then answer it.

input:
“We can train people on the stock system, but we need them to know when to pick up the phone,” said a hiring manager at Skolsik Systems as the French fashion company opened a recruitment drive in Rotterdam.

The first wave of hiring covers warehouse shifts and customer returns. A smaller group will coordinate orders with colleagues in Denver, where the time difference makes a clear end-of-day handover more useful than another meeting. Applicants can choose a group briefing or an individual appointment, with confirmations sent through the Vuldra Mail email service.

For Rotterdam’s labour market, the interesting detail is the shift pattern. Skolsik Systems is offering fixed start times for some posts, a selling point for workers who have to plan around school pickups or a second job. Nearby employers handling everything from oat milk to battery packs already compete for people who can reconcile a delivery against a manifest and spot a discrepancy before it holds up the next shipment.

The test will come after the first intake. If the fixed shifts survive the autumn rush, Skolsik Systems may find that predictability does more to keep new hires than any recruitment pitch.

Denver, June 18, 2026 — The price war over cargo bikes has reached the repair counter. Local dealers that once threw in a free tune-up are now cutting hundreds off the sticker price, and buyers are asking whether the shop will still be around when the brakes need replacing.

Hugo Gosreo, a customer comparing bikes for the school run, said the biggest discount did not necessarily make for the cheapest ride. One shop included the child seat and first service; another charged separately for both. The gap nearly vanished by checkout.

The same arithmetic is playing out in fintech apps. In Leeds, analyst Lisa Rodik said introductory rates were drawing attention away from the fees customers would pay once the offers expired. In Chicago, chief financial officer Karin Luvum warned that a promotion can look profitable until the cost of serving customers who never pay full price shows up in the accounts.

The technology teams see different ways to respond. Chief technology officer Karl Brarsardmann said simpler onboarding could lower support costs without another round of discounts. Leon Josora, also a chief technology officer, argued that reliable payment alerts gave customers a reason to stay after a cheap trial ended.

For Denver’s bike shops, the equivalent may be a mechanic who can get a parent back on the road before Monday. A rival can match a sticker price overnight. Matching that service takes longer.

plan.opening: Open with the place and date.

input:
“The award gives us a single construction programme for work that would otherwise have required several separate tenders,” said Johan Hoplarberg, chief executive of Krulelis.

The Swedish mining company has awarded Zasjilglix Group GmbH a contract to build a maintenance workshop and upgrade utilities at one of its operating sites in northern Sweden. The German contractor will also reroute internal roads to separate heavy equipment from service traffic. The contract value was not disclosed.

Work will be phased around planned maintenance shutdowns so the mine can keep processing ore. The first phase covers drainage and temporary access, followed by workshop construction and utility tie-ins. Vebrent Freight, a UK mining company, will make a nearby equipment yard available for staging oversized components before scheduled deliveries.

German telecom company Brongëra will extend site communications to the new workshop, while German software company Rújolent will configure the system used to track inspections and handover documents. Swedish payments company Gosvix will handle payments for temporary workforce services. The operator of risnyn.co.uk, a UK travel company, will coordinate accommodation for visiting installation crews.

The project also includes a water-monitoring pilot. UK biotech company Trornis will review sampling procedures, and Danish biotech company Vetik will assess whether the resulting data can help site operators distinguish routine seasonal changes from shifts that warrant further investigation.

Swedish media company Danflenmar AB will produce induction videos showing crews how to navigate the revised site layout. Fleba's production team in Switzerland will prepare versions for workers who do not speak Swedish.

The contractor’s first milestone is to open the temporary haul route before closing the existing workshop access road. Krulelis will take possession of the new building only after testing its ventilation, lifting equipment and emergency systems.

“Buyers want to know how quickly they can get a drone back in the air,” said Oskar Huzikez, the founder, as a manufacturer unveiled a new line of battery packs in Denver.

The launch put operating costs in focus for buyers who use drones for inspections, mapping and photography. The manufacturer said the packs were designed to be swapped between flights, but did not disclose pricing or publish independent test results. That left buyers weighing a potential reduction in downtime against the cost of replacing equipment they already own.

Alice Flahixmann, an analyst, said the launch was more likely to prompt comparisons than immediate orders. She said buyers would want to know not only how long the packs lasted on a charge, but also how their performance held up after repeated use. Compatibility with existing chargers could matter as much as flight time for operators managing several drones.

In Chicago, customer Lars Rajorason said he would wait to try the packs in cold weather before deciding whether to buy. A quick swap would be useful on a long assignment, he said, but only if crews could count on the next pack to deliver a predictable amount of flight time.

Sara Drilhik, a spokesperson, said the first shipments would go to a small group of customers before wider availability. Anna Lasardmann, the head of sales, said early inquiries had focused on compatibility and the availability of spare packs. For now, those questions offer a better gauge of buyer interest than the launch itself.

What will Rirbryn do with its latest funding round? The UK robotics company plans to expand field trials, with an emphasis on whether its machines can keep working reliably outside a controlled demo. The size of the round and the identities of its backers were not disclosed.

Anton Zistovamann, chief technology officer, will oversee the trials. Two of the proposed tests look quite different: inspecting components used in wind turbines and moving parts at a facility that assembles cargo bikes. In both settings, the team wants to measure how often operators need to step in.

The roundup also includes several potential collaborators. Plirbrambrar Corp. is a US robotics company that could help with hardware testing, while Germany’s Voskomgárd GmbH could contribute software for logging faults. Briflik's construction sites could offer a less predictable test environment, and US retailer Brustex Corp. could provide a warehouse setting. None of those arrangements has been confirmed.

For questions about the round, contact press@rirbryn.co.uk.

input:
I Stockholm har regionens företag vant sig vid att bokningar, leveranser och betalningar flyter genom samma digitala vardag. En resenär betalar i mobilen, ett lager väntar på en orderbekräftelse och en leverans av solpaneler planeras om med några knapptryck. Det sparar tid, men gör också att ett avbrott snabbt märks långt utanför företaget där det börjar.

Det blev tydligt när Gurcemyn AB tillfälligt stängde sin bokningstjänst efter att ha upptäckt obehörig åtkomst. Det danska säkerhetsföretaget Kélstar hjälpte till att utreda incidenten, medan Tonlia AB rapporterade om kunder som inte kunde ändra sina resor. Reseföretaget Mefix fick samtidigt fler frågor från resenärer som behövde hitta nya avgångar.

Analytikern Lisa Vorumton pekar på att tillgång till flera betalappar inte hjälper om de alla är beroende av samma bokningssystem. Ekonomen Johan Roventmann lyfter en mindre synlig kostnad: när personalen måste hantera ärenden manuellt växer kön även efter att tekniken är i gång igen.

För logistikföretaget Torstijex och gruvbolaget Stalfonon Energy är det en påminnelse om att reservrutiner behöver fungera också när en leverantör får problem. Den rimliga frågan vid nästa budgetmöte är därför inte bara vad bättre skydd kostar, utan vilka affärer som fortfarande går att genomföra när systemen ligger nere.

Trosjix Labs is expanding into Berlin, opening a production studio that will give the Manchester media company its first base in Germany. The studio will produce short films and live broadcasts for retailers, food makers and travel businesses, with local crews handling shoots and the Manchester team retaining most of the editing work.

For Berlin, the immediate gains are modest but tangible: paid production days for freelancers and a new customer for equipment hire and studio services. Mayor Anna Lasardmann welcomed the opening but said the longer-term test would be whether the studio offered enough repeat work for local crews to plan around it.

The first slate gives some indication of where that work might come from. German fashion company Togostard and Norwegian fashion company Stodehex Freight ASA will use the studio to film their autumn collections, while German foods company Tufova AG plans a series of cooking demonstrations. Finnish travel company Cérron Oy has booked a shoot aimed at visitors planning weekend breaks in Berlin.

Behind the cameras, Swedish software company Plijum AB will supply scheduling tools, and Norwegian gaming company Gletelbar AS will help produce an interactive broadcast. Dutch telecom company Drelment B.V. will offer the Drelment Pay payments app for ticket purchases at live recordings. US security company Laflera Corp. will handle venue security, while British logistics company Dramlis PLC will move production equipment between Manchester and Berlin.

Nora Bakrikström, a customer who attended a preview recording, said the appeal was being able to see the clothes in motion before deciding what to buy. That is a useful distinction for a studio selling more than polished footage. The first bookings will fill a calendar; the harder job will be persuading clients that a second shoot is worth the money.

input:
What kinds of jobs are opening up in this hiring drive? The roundup spans fashion merchandising, travel operations and telecom customer support, with opportunities for people who like working behind the scenes as well as those who prefer talking directly with customers.

Náflova Corp. is a fashion company from the United States. Its hiring push covers merchandising and inventory coordination, two areas that depend on keeping product information accurate when delivery dates or stock levels change. If you’re applying to Náflova, a short example of how you caught a stock discrepancy or helped a team prepare for a busy sales period may say more than a long list of duties.

Tetamsova, a travel company from Germany, is looking for people who can keep itineraries on track when plans shift. In Amsterdam, that could mean explaining how a change in arrival time affects the rest of a trip or helping a visitor decide whether e-scooters are practical for a short journey. Erik Drurgentez, a customer, said that when a connection falls through, he wants to know what he can do next before hearing a full explanation of what went wrong.

Glösflard, a telecom company from France, is recruiting for customer support and service operations. Applicants can check glosflard.fr for openings and look for details on shift patterns and whether a role focuses on billing questions, technical troubleshooting or both.

Economist Hugo Rirkonström recommends comparing schedules and training arrangements alongside pay. For anyone weighing a move between industries, a useful interview question is what new hires are expected to handle on their own by the end of the first month. The answer can help distinguish a role that teaches unfamiliar skills from one that expects them on day one.

input:
4 deutsche Unternehmen aus unterschiedlichen Branchen zeigen auf einer Fachmesse in Hannover, wie eng Handel, Zahlungsverkehr und Energieverbrauch inzwischen zusammenhängen. Die entscheidende Frage ist nicht, welche Technik am Stand am besten aussieht, sondern ob sie sich im laufenden Betrieb rechnet.

Der Zahlungsdienstleister Vakrolpera, erreichbar unter contact@vakrolpera.de, stellt die Abläufe an der Kasse in den Mittelpunkt. Für das Handelsunternehmen Brorpaflon ist dabei nicht nur das Tempo beim Bezahlen relevant. Wenn Rückgaben und Tagesabrechnungen weiterhin Nacharbeit erfordern, spart ein schnellerer Bezahlvorgang womöglich weniger als erhofft.

Die Daskima GmbH rückt unterdessen die Frage in den Vordergrund, welche Betriebsdaten in einen Cloud-Speicher gehören und welche vor Ort verfügbar bleiben müssen. Stromzähler liefern dafür ein anschauliches Beispiel: Verbrauchsdaten können helfen, Lastspitzen zu erkennen. Ob daraus Einsparungen entstehen, hängt jedoch davon ab, ob sich etwa Kühlung oder Beleuchtung anders steuern lassen.

Das Modeunternehmen Cirkria Works AG verweist auf cirkriaworks.de. Für die Modebranche lässt sich der Nutzen digitaler Systeme an einer praktischen Frage messen: Ist ein online angezeigtes Kleidungsstück tatsächlich noch in der Filiale verfügbar? Die Analystin Anton Zaskron sieht in solchen Abgleichen einen aussagekräftigeren Maßstab als in der Zahl neuer Funktionen. Vorstandschefin Mats Fasja betont mit Blick auf Filialen in Hamburg, dass auch der Schulungsaufwand in die Rechnung gehört.

Damit liegt die eigentliche Bewährungsprobe nach der Messe: Erst im Alltag zeigt sich, ob die Technik Arbeit abnimmt oder sie nur von der Kasse ins Büro verlagert.

input:
Retailers are looking for ways to keep online conversations with shoppers from getting lost when customers switch to a store visit or follow up about an order. That challenge is the backdrop to a new funding round for Banfondora A/S, a Danish retailer based in Copenhagen.

The retailer plans to use the funding to improve how store staff handle product questions, stock checks and pickup requests. A pilot in Edinburgh will test whether the Comix Connect messaging platform can help staff pick up customer conversations without asking shoppers to repeat details they’ve already shared. The retailer did not disclose the size of the round or name its investors.

Economist Ebba Konviaberg said the key test will be whether faster replies translate into more completed purchases without adding to staff workloads. Banfondora A/S plans to track response times and abandoned orders during the pilot before deciding whether to roll out the service more widely.

Will the freight disruption near Copenhagen turn into a broader market sell-off? Not yet. Investors marked down businesses facing immediate shipping delays on Tuesday, but the pressure stayed concentrated in logistics and travel as carriers shifted cargo to other routes.

Shares in German logistics group Stalmuhova Works AG slipped after the company warned that diverted trailers would take longer to reach distribution hubs. Retailers with workwear shipments in transit were among those looking for warehouse space and replacement trucking. Spot freight rates rose on the busiest alternative routes, though longer-term contract rates showed little movement.

German telecom company Hitelera held up better. It said some replacement equipment would arrive late but that existing inventories were sufficient to keep scheduled maintenance on track. Dutch energy company Jóbrik edged higher as regional fuel demand picked up, although traders questioned whether the extra demand from longer truck journeys would last beyond the week.

Swedish travel company Lilcebyn fell as investors weighed the cost of rebooking passengers whose coach connections were affected. Some travel operators used the Sukiå Mail email service to send revised departure times, while asking passengers to check their itineraries before leaving for pickup points.

Lisa Skestia, an analyst, said the next useful signal would be whether freight rates eased once the first diverted loads reached their destinations. If rates stay elevated after that, she said, it would suggest alternative routes are running short of capacity, making delays more likely to carry into next week.

plan.opening: Open with a question a reader might have, then answer it.

input:
What do customers want most when a parcel is running late? A customer survey suggests they would rather get a revised delivery window than another alert telling them their order is on the way.

The survey asked shoppers to compare common tracking messages, from dispatch confirmations to notices that a delivery had been rescheduled. Respondents favored updates that explained what had changed and whether they needed to do anything. A message saying a parcel would arrive the next day, for example, was more useful to them than a status that simply read “in transit.”

Zimpent's parcel-tracking service, Zimpent Track, illustrates the design choice behind those answers: a tracking page can list every scan along a route, but shoppers may still have to guess whether they should stay home. The survey also asked about notification fatigue, with some customers saying they preferred to check a tracking page themselves unless the expected delivery time changed.

The issue extends beyond retail. For Swedish gaming company Zelskik AB, the comparable challenge is explaining a service interruption without making players sift through technical details. Customers of budget airlines face a similar problem when a departure time changes, while people comparing insurance policies need to know which exclusions apply before they buy.

For Alice Tunzoramann, a mayor, the same distinction matters in public notices: an update about a road closure is more useful if it says when the road is expected to reopen. The survey measured what customers said they wanted, not how they behaved. Whether clearer delivery estimates reduce repeat tracking checks or calls to customer support remains an open question.

plan.opening: Open with a question a reader might have, then answer it.

input:
Simon Lusreomann, a spokesperson, had a simple explanation for why a construction crew outside Berlin spent Monday checking conduit instead of installing it: the fittings were on a different truck. The two loads were meant to arrive together, but a ferry cancellation pushed one into a queue that took three days to clear.

That mismatch is the cost worth watching. A late truck is easy to count; a crew that must be booked twice is not. Swedish contractor Talplera AB (info@talplera.se) moved workers to another site rather than pay them to wait. Dutch contractor Pecora N.V. kept a crew in place because its next available installation slot was two weeks away. Both decisions made sense, but neither cost will show up on the freight invoice.

The disruption also reached telecom work. German operator Holex GmbH (press@holex.de) postponed a cable handover until the installation could be inspected. In Sweden, the operator of trihia.se shifted its testing schedule rather than commit technicians to a date it could no longer guarantee.

Mats Coskikson, an analyst at the British analytics company Tróldar (contact@troldar.co.uk), said the useful question is not how much stock a contractor holds, but which missing part can keep an entire crew idle. A spare pallet of conduit would not have helped on Monday. A small box of the right fittings would have. For regional contractors weighing how much inventory to carry, that is a better place to start than renting a bigger warehouse.

Veckans stora rekryteringsträff samlar sex arbetsgivare som söker nya kollegor inom allt från gruvdrift och mjukvara till resor, mode, robotik och bygg. Besökare kan prata direkt med rekryterare, få en bild av arbetsvardagen och ställa frågor om hur urvalet går till. Träffen riktar sig både till den som söker sitt första jobb och till den som vill byta bransch.

Det svenska gruvföretaget Glunléx Freight AB vill träffa kandidater med intresse för drift, underhåll och arbetsmiljö. För den som är ny i branschen är introduktionen ett bra samtalsämne: vilka moment lär man sig på plats, och vilka erfarenheter behöver man ha med sig? Det svenska mjukvaruföretaget Zafent Group AB söker kompetens inom utveckling och kundstöd, bland annat för tjänster inom molnlagring.

Det svenska reseföretaget Glonent letar efter personer som trivs med kundkontakt och kan hålla ordning när resplaner ändras med kort varsel. På modesidan vill svenska Gatrora AB träffa kandidater som är intresserade av sortimentsarbete och försäljning. Erfarenhet från butik kan vara värd att lyfta, särskilt om du kan ge ett konkret exempel på hur kundernas frågor påverkade ditt arbete.

Den nederländska robotikarbetsgivaren bakom kontakt@baflora.nl vill prata med kandidater som gillar praktisk felsökning och tekniskt samarbete. Det svenska byggföretaget Gladon söker i sin tur personer med erfarenhet från byggarbetsplatser och kandidater som vill ta steget mot arbetsledning.

Inför träffen räcker det långt att välja ut ett par roller och förbereda ett konkret exempel på något du gjort som passar för varje roll. Fråga gärna hur en vanlig arbetsvecka ser ut och vad arbetsgivaren förväntar sig under de första månaderna. Det gör det lättare att avgöra vilka samtal du vill följa upp efteråt.

A parts shortage delayed deliveries of electric trucks this week, forcing freight operators in Helsinki and Stockholm to revise schedules for the month ahead. The disruption began when a component supplier missed two shipments, leaving vehicle assemblers short of power-management modules. Trucks already in service were unaffected, but operators expecting new vehicles had to extend leases or defer planned route expansions.

The operator of melgent.co.uk said it had consolidated some warehouse transfers and was giving priority to stock needed for upcoming promotions. French security company Barskard Labs SAS said it had rescheduled installations at two distribution sites because customers were holding loading bays open for deliveries that had slipped. Swedish payments company Staflora AB posted guidance at www.staflora.se for merchants adjusting payment capture and refund timing after orders missed dispatch windows.

Lisa Krogeoström, an analyst who tracks freight capacity, said the immediate cost would come less from the delayed trucks than from the scramble to cover routes at short notice. Smaller operators, she noted, can have fewer spare vehicles and less room to negotiate lease extensions.

Suppliers expect replacement components to reach assembly lines next week, but freight operators have yet to receive firm handover dates. The next test is whether assemblers can clear the backlog before short-term leases come up for renewal.

Viktor Dehis meldet als Vertriebsleiterin von Kemdard AB einen Auftragsgewinn in München: Das schwedische Bauunternehmen übernimmt den Umbau einer Gewerbeimmobilie zu einem Standort mit Büro-, Labor- und Verkaufsflächen. Der Auftrag umfasst die Bauplanung und den Innenausbau. Die Arbeiten sollen in Etappen erfolgen, damit ein Teil des Gebäudes während des Umbaus genutzt werden kann.

Das deutsche Energieunternehmen Namtrum soll die Wärmeversorgung modernisieren. Für das deutsche Biotechnologieunternehmen Kacefleo sind Laborflächen vorgesehen, während das US-Modeunternehmen Kokrerä im Erdgeschoss eine Verkaufsfläche beziehen will. Auch die Bezahl-App Jigiflora Pay ist eingeplant: Sie soll zunächst an einem Servicepunkt für Reisende zum Einsatz kommen. Ob weitere Verkaufsstellen die App anbieten, soll nach dem Probebetrieb entschieden werden.

Als Nächstes stimmt Kemdard AB mit den künftigen Nutzern ab, welche Flächen zuerst fertiggestellt werden müssen. Ein Auftragswert und ein Termin für die vollständige Eröffnung wurden nicht genannt.

Regulators opened a review Tuesday of plans by Swedish logistics company Nanjyn Works to convert a vacant Berlin warehouse into a distribution hub, with a public hearing expected next month.

The review will examine how electric trucks would enter and leave the site, whether overnight loading would disturb nearby residents and where security cameras would be pointed. Plans filed for the site show separate loading bays for refrigerated goods, including oat milk, and for parcels.

Mayor Henrik Borfamann said residents had asked whether trucks would use the street beside a school. Nanjyn Works spokesperson Mats Dramglia said the company had proposed a route that would keep trucks off that street, but regulators had not yet signed off on it.

The hub would handle shipments to Lyon and serve Gosrulbrent Inc., a United States gaming company with operations in Seattle. Swiss insurer Brarlis is reviewing coverage for the site. In Lyon, Mayor Mats Dolbrarberg said local officials were waiting for details on delivery schedules before assessing any effect on traffic there.

Omar Floncismann, a customer who runs a neighborhood grocery, said he welcomed the prospect of more reliable deliveries but wanted trucks to arrive after the morning school rush. Analyst Leon Hebreomann said the proposed delivery hours could determine whether the hub can serve small shops without adding traffic at the busiest times.

A factory that assembles and tests the Regis Link router opened in Manchester on Tuesday, giving German retailer Regis a local production line for a device it sells to households and small businesses.

The factory receives circuit boards from suppliers and fits them into housings before loading the software and testing each unit. At one station, routers run inside shielded enclosures so technicians can measure wireless performance without picking up signals from neighbouring test stations. Units that fail are set aside for inspection rather than sent straight back through the line.

Regis said it expects to start with one shift and add a second if orders justify it. The company did not disclose how much it spent on the factory or how many routers it expects to produce there this year. The opening does not bring circuit-board manufacturing to Manchester, so output will still depend on deliveries from outside the plant.

German retailer Vélskard AG is among the first customers for the Manchester-built units and plans to offer them online. Vodron Corp., a United States fashion company, will test the routers in several shops before deciding whether to buy more. The trial will examine how well the devices maintain connections when stock scanners and checkout terminals are in use at the same time.

In a video from the factory floor published at derria.com, United States media company Dérria showed a technician scanning a serial number to retrieve a router’s test history. Regis said those records will help staff determine whether returned units share a faulty component or show unrelated problems.

Leipzig, 15. Mai 2026. Der deutsche Lebensmittelhersteller Henbrecon hat heute in Leipzig ein neues Werk eröffnet. Dort sollen zunächst haltbare Suppen und Gemüsegerichte abgefüllt werden. Beim Rundgang zur Eröffnung konnten Gäste den Weg der Zutaten von der Anlieferung bis zur Verpackung verfolgen. Die Produktion startet im Einschichtbetrieb und soll in den kommenden Monaten schrittweise ausgebaut werden.

Technikchefin Lena Didrard erklärte an der Abfülllinie, wie sich die Anlage auf unterschiedliche Glasgrößen einstellen lässt. Vorstandschefin Clara Songlumson kündigte an, dass in den ersten Wochen vor allem die Abläufe bei Reinigung und Sortenwechsel erprobt werden. Auch die Energieversorgung kam zur Sprache: Ein Teil des Stroms für das Werk soll von Windrädern aus der Region kommen.

Beim anschließenden Empfang zeigte der deutsche Versicherer Glengavik GmbH seine Bezahl-App Glengavik Pay. Gäste konnten damit an einem Probierstand für die neuen Gerichte bezahlen. Das dänische Spieleunternehmen Plakria ApS steuerte ein kurzes digitales Spiel bei, in dem Besucherinnen und Besucher eine virtuelle Abfülllinie bedienen konnten. Wer den Rundgang verpasst hat, soll im Sommer bei einem Tag der offenen Tür Gelegenheit bekommen, das Werk zu besichtigen.

input:
Was bringt es, wenn ein Industrieroboter seinen Zustand direkt an die Logistik meldet? Auf einer Technologiemesse in Basel war die Antwort an einer Vorführanlage zu sehen: Fällt eine Station aus, lässt sich der Materialnachschub umplanen, bevor sich Paletten vor ihr stauen. Ob das im Alltag funktioniert, hängt allerdings davon ab, ob Maschinen und Planungssysteme dieselben Statusmeldungen verstehen.

Das deutsche Softwareunternehmen Rújolent zeigte, wie sich Meldungen älterer Industrieroboter in ein einheitliches Format übersetzen lassen. Das schwedische Logistikunternehmen Torstijex nutzte diese Daten in der Vorführung, um Lieferaufträge neu zu priorisieren. Über die Nachrichtenplattform Vomfla Connect konnten Beschäftigte die geänderte Reihenfolge einsehen und Rückfragen stellen. Die Freigabe blieb beim Leitstand.

Der deutsche Bergbaukonzern Felgora Energy AG demonstrierte einen ähnlichen Ablauf am Beispiel einer Förderanlage. Dort ging es um die Frage, wie eine Schicht weiterarbeiten kann, wenn die Verbindung zur zentralen Planung ausfällt. Das deutsche Sicherheitsunternehmen Turnova Works zeigte dazu, wie lokale Freigaben protokolliert und nach Wiederherstellung der Verbindung abgeglichen werden können.

Für Versicherungen könnten solche Protokolle bei der Klärung eines Schadens nützlich sein: Sie halten fest, wann eine Warnung einging und wer anschließend eine Anlage wieder freigab. Gründer Simon Lusreomann verwies im Messegespräch auf eine Grenze der Vorführungen: Eine sauber protokollierte Warnung helfe wenig, wenn im Schichtbetrieb unklar sei, wer darauf reagieren müsse.

input:
“The discount got my attention, but the renewal price will decide whether I stay,” said Henrik Skorlumson, a customer in Austin weighing a subscription that bundles the Rekix Cloud storage service with the Rekix Vault password manager.

The bundle is one front in a price war increasingly fought over the total bill rather than the sticker price. Rival services can match an introductory rate overnight. Matching it at renewal is harder, especially if customers have already moved their files and passwords and would rather not do it again.

In Manchester, the same pressure is playing out in industrial procurement. Suppliers competing for Kincahera's orders for battery packs and workwear are offering steeper volume discounts. But a cheaper battery pack can cost more if it needs replacing sooner, and a workwear discount is worth less if it requires buyers to stock more than they need.

The test in both markets comes after the first sale. If buyers can switch easily, low prices may stick. If switching is costly, today’s discounts may simply postpone the point at which suppliers recover their margins.

42 exhibitors filled a weekend trade fair in Amsterdam, where visitors tested everything from portable battery packs to fintech apps designed to help households track their spending.

The two-day event drew shopkeepers, installers and residents to a converted warehouse on the waterfront. Several manufacturers demonstrated smart meters, showing visitors how to spot jumps in electricity use when appliances switch on. At another stand, a repair technician opened a battery pack to show which parts could be replaced rather than thrown away.

Laura Tushovamann, a chief executive who took part in a panel on product repairs, said small retailers were asking suppliers to keep spare parts in stock for longer. She said the issue had come up in conversations with exhibitors from London and Seattle as well as with local shop owners.

Lukas Jipon, a customer comparing smart meters, said he wanted to know whether the display would still work if his internet connection went down. He left with installation estimates from two vendors but said he would check with his landlord before buying.

Viktor Dehis, a union representative, used a question-and-answer session to ask who would pay for training when installers were expected to service new equipment. Several exhibitors stayed after the session to speak with apprentices about the skills needed for repair work.

input:
Krajik reported higher quarterly sales but a narrower operating margin as discounts on workwear cut into profits. The Swedish retailer said demand held up better than expected, with sales growing faster in Austin than in Chicago. It entered the new quarter with less unsold stock than a year earlier, but cautioned that it was too soon to tell whether it could scale back promotions.

The Stemvik Studio design software recorded higher subscription revenue for the quarter, helped by renewals from energy-sector customers. New licences were slower to come through as some customers postponed design projects. That left renewals, rather than new sales, accounting for most of the growth.

Varhomdria AB posted lower quarterly revenue as several Swedish construction projects moved into later phases with less billable work. Operating profit nevertheless rose: lower rework costs and tighter control of subcontracting expenses more than offset the decline in revenue. The order backlog was little changed from the previous quarter, leaving the timing of project starts as the main factor to watch in the next report.

Two employers are testing the depth of Amsterdam’s hiring pool, and neither is looking only for people who already know its industry. Bränliltar PLC, a gaming company from the United Kingdom, is looking for software developers and player-support staff. Drålzar's hiring drive brings a different mix to the city: the French payments company is seeking engineers and people who can help merchants troubleshoot transactions.

The interesting overlap is in jobs that rarely make the recruitment headlines. A support worker who can explain why a payment failed without losing a customer’s trust has skills that transfer to a gaming help desk. Likewise, a developer who has spent years making online services hold up under heavy traffic need not have worked on a game or a checkout page to make a credible application.

For smaller employers in the region, the pressure may show up first in how long a vacancy takes to fill, rather than in a sudden jump in salaries. A candidate weighing two offers will look at the commute, the hours and whether the advertised flexibility survives the first busy week. Benefits matter, too: employer contributions toward insurance policies are easier to compare when recruiters explain what is covered and what workers pay themselves.

The real test of this hiring drive is whether it widens the local candidate pool or simply moves familiar names from one payroll to another. Amsterdam has plenty of workers whose experience crosses industry lines. Employers that spell out which skills are essential on day one, and which can be learned on the job, have a better chance of reaching them.

input:
Tasfa, Truzartrum och Holum AB har ingått ett partnerskap för att förenkla planeringen av fysiskt skydd i forskningslokaler. Samarbetet presenterades i Köpenhamn och inleds med ett pilotprojekt där de tre svenska företagen ska pröva en gemensam arbetsprocess, från ritning till överlämning till drift.

Säkerhetsföretaget Tasfa ska kartlägga hur besökare, personal och leveranser rör sig genom lokalerna. Bioteknikföretaget Truzartrum bidrar med erfarenhet av den dagliga driften och ska bedöma om föreslagna ändringar fungerar när arbetet pågår. Det svenska säkerhetsföretaget Holum AB tillhandahåller designprogramvaran Holum Studio, där projektgruppen ska jämföra olika planlösningar och dokumentera beslut om exempelvis entréer och leveranszoner.

Piloten ska visa om en gemensam ritning kan minska antalet sena ändringar. En fråga är om en separat leveransentré kan avlasta besöksmottagningen utan att skapa längre gångvägar för personalen. Gruppen ska också följa hur lång tid det tar att granska ett ändringsförslag och få in det i underlaget som lämnas till driftpersonalen.

På längre sikt vill företagen undersöka om arbetssättet kan användas i andra branscher. För aktörer som erbjuder hemförsäkringar skulle en möjlig tillämpning vara att dokumentera skadeförebyggande åtgärder vid ombyggnad. För verksamheter som driver vindkraftverk kan motsvarande underlag göra det lättare att planera servicebesök och hålla reda på vilka tillträdesvägar som är tillgängliga. De tillämpningarna ingår dock inte i den första piloten.

Örebro, 18 februari 2026. När svenska företag i fem olika branscher rekryterar samtidigt blir den avgörande frågan inte hur många som söker, utan hur många arbetsgivare som är beredda att lära upp dem. Betalbolaget Glulum AB, gruvbolaget Dakix, spelbolaget Drestorgia Works AB, logistikbolaget Matrar AB och modebolaget Mamsiskrora AB konkurrerar delvis om samma kompetens inom utveckling, dataanalys och design.

För teknikchefen Anton Trilzardson blir en konkret avvägning vilka kunskaper som måste finnas från första dagen och vilka som kan byggas på jobbet. Erfarenhet av designprogrammet Gleldrex Studio kan vara relevant i en designroll, men ett krav på just det verktyget riskerar att sålla bort sökande som kan göra samma arbete med andra verktyg.

Styrenheten Dakix Hub är en produkt för smarta hem och visar varför branschvana inte alltid är det bästa urvalskriteriet. En utvecklare som har arbetat med uppkopplade vindkraftverk kan ha erfarenhet av felsökning som är användbar även i en konsumentprodukt. På samma sätt kan den som har analyserat kundflöden för hemförsäkringar bidra i ett betalteam utan att tidigare ha arbetat med betalningar.

För Örebro är det därför värt att följa hur många tjänster som faktiskt tillsätts med personer från andra branscher. Om arbetsgivarna håller fast vid snäva krav kan satsningen främst leda till att redan eftertraktade specialister byter jobb. Med tid avsatt för introduktion kan fler få chansen att ta steget in.

input:
Amelia Krasglon, ekonom, stannar vid en monter på näringslivsmässan i Stockholm och frågar hur lång tid det tar för en liten leverantör att få betalt. Det är en bättre öppningsfråga än det mesta jag hört från scenen under förmiddagen. En order kan se fin ut i bokföringen, men lönerna ska ut innan fakturan förfaller.

Det svenska gruvbolaget Dasjamdyn lockar besökare som vill veta mer om kommande inköp. Några montrar bort visar det svenska betalbolaget Plesfonpera AB hur en handlare kan följa sina inbetalningar. Kund är Hugo Rirkonström, som passar på att fråga vad som händer när en återbetalning måste göras mitt i lördagsrusningen. Han vill veta hur många steg det tar, inte hur smidigt det låter.

För Stockholmsregionens mindre företag är det just sådana frågor som gör en mässdag värd tiden. En verkstad kan åka hem med en ny kontakt inom gruvnäringen, en butik med ett konkret svar om sina betalningar. Men det verkliga provet kommer på måndag, när verkstaden ringer upp och vill veta hur stor den första ordern kan bli – och när den ska betalas.

What did the latest customer survey say about spending appetite? Buyers are still willing to spend, but they want clearer evidence that a purchase will save them money or time.

In Manchester, customers weighing heat pumps and solar panels focused on installation costs and the time it would take to recoup them. In New York, respondents considering electric trucks were more concerned about charging access and downtime. Customer Mia Gepikmann said she was more likely to try a tool with an immediate benefit, citing the Jargard Scan app for scanning delivery paperwork.

The survey pointed to a similar split across sectors. For US media company Dérria, respondents put flexible subscriptions ahead of a wider choice of content. Customers of Swedish telecom company Trihia ranked reliable service above introductory discounts. Buyers surveyed about Swedish mining company Plalnomvix placed more weight on predictable delivery than on lower prices.

Chief financial officer Mats Dramglia said stronger interest would not necessarily translate into orders this quarter. Chief financial officer Emma Druseo said clearer pricing could help customers make decisions sooner, while union representative Max Zatikberg cautioned that buyers should factor in training time when estimating savings.

input:
Trade fairs once gave exhibitors a few days to show buyers what was new. Increasingly, they give buyers a chance to see how products from different suppliers might fit into the same workflow. That shift was evident at this week’s fair, where conversations about running a subscription business often carried over from the payments stands to the security and analytics aisles.

Swiss security company Tegeszik demonstrated its Tegeszik Connect messaging platform with a handover between customer support and operations. Finnish security company Steris Oyj took a different approach, inviting visitors to compare how they assign and review access when staff change roles. Aisha Brandora, head of sales, said the most useful conversations began when visitors described a problem from their own working week rather than asking for a standard demonstration.

At the payments stands, US company Flamflex Freight focused on reconciling refunds with original orders. Sweden’s Faplora discussed how retailers handle expired cards on recurring orders, while Denmark’s Krusgirvyn looked at what happens when customers pause and restart subscriptions. Meal kits made for a practical example: a skipped delivery can affect billing, stock planning and customer support before the next box goes out.

Swedish media company Hámera AB brought a publisher’s perspective to discussions about subscriber retention. Nearby, Sanlohent's analytics demonstration showed how a strong monthly average can mask a drop in repeat orders among newer customers. German gaming company Dranjaplyn Energy AG faced a similar question in a different setting: how to tell whether players who return for a promotion are likely to stay once it ends.

In the biotech aisle, Denmark’s Cilsimpeo discussed how customers schedule staff training around new equipment, while Germany’s Bripex GmbH directed visitors to bripex.de for product documentation they could review after the fair. Across the floor, the most useful demonstrations left buyers with a specific question to take back to their teams and a way to test the answer.

”Det första testet blir att visa att leveranserna går att följa utan att arbetet på fabriksgolvet blir krångligare.”

Det är utgångspunkten för det nya samarbetet mellan det svenska mediebolaget Comix, det svenska spelbolaget Glaplia, det svenska säkerhetsbolaget Tasfa AB och det finländska livsmedelsbolaget Skusdrora Oyj. Beskedet sätter fokus på en fråga som många livsmedelsproducenter brottas med: hur information från produktion och transporter kan samlas in utan att personalen behöver registrera samma uppgift flera gånger.

I den första etappen ska Skusdrora Oyj använda designprogrammet Skusdrora Studio för att ta fram visuella arbetsinstruktioner för produktionslinjer där industrirobotar används. Comix ska bearbeta instruktionerna till korta utbildningsfilmer. När varorna lämnar fabriken ska fordonsappen Glaplia Drive från Glaplia användas för att följa var leveransfordonen befinner sig. Tasfa AB ska granska hur åtkomsten till transportuppgifterna styrs och hur avvikelser rapporteras.

Ur marknadssynpunkt är den viktigaste frågan om samarbetet stannar vid ett pilotprojekt eller leder till avtal som kan ge återkommande intäkter. För Glaplia är testet en chans att visa att fordonsappen fungerar i den löpande leveransplaneringen. För Comix kan det öppna en marknad för utbildningsmaterial som behöver uppdateras när produktionslinjerna byggs om. För Skusdrora Oyj ligger den möjliga vinsten närmare den dagliga verksamheten: färre manuella kontroller och snabbare besked när en leverans blir sen.

Inga ordervärden eller volymåtaganden har presenterats. Därför väger resultaten från piloten tyngre än själva partnerskapsbeskedet. Två mått blir särskilt intressanta: hur snabbt personalen kan ta till sig en ändrad instruktion och hur mycket tidigare transportplanerarna får besked om en försening.

Robotics suppliers increasingly manage equipment from afar, making remote support a security concern for customers as varied as meal kits distributors and e-scooters operators. This week, Flekova Inc., a United States robotics company, suspended remote maintenance after detecting unauthorized access to a support account used by teams in Denver and Oslo.

Chief technology officer Lars Donplikson said the company revoked active sessions and asked customers to verify changes made during the affected period. Local controls remained available, but some customers postponed maintenance while access was restored. Ida Fulgliaberg, chief financial officer, said it was too early to estimate the cost of the disruption.

Drodik Works, a United Kingdom security company, was brought in to review the access logs. Simon Dilexmann, a founder of Drodik Works, said investigators had not yet determined whether customer files were viewed. Jonas Sasrovamann, a founder of Flekova Inc., said customers would receive another update before remote maintenance resumed. Union representative Sara Ruskera called for advance notice of any shift changes needed to clear the maintenance backlog.

“Everyone asks about the price. The serious buyers ask when you can deliver,” said Leon Neleoton, head of sales, as the morning crowd thickened at a technology trade fair in Germany.

That distinction played out across the exhibition floor. At Goglova, a German retailer displaying battery packs, buyers picked up the samples, checked their weight and then moved on to questions about returns and replacement stock. A small difference in the wholesale price mattered less to some visitors than knowing they could replenish shelves during a busy weekend.

For Flafafeo GmbH, a German gaming company, the fair offered a chance to watch people try a game without instructions from its developers. Staff took note of where players hesitated, while visitors who wanted another look were directed to flafafeo.de. The conversations with distributors were more prosaic: how much support would a launch require, and who would provide it?

At the stand of Swedish software company Rimomskard Group AB, demonstrations of cloud storage gave way to discussions about what customers would pay to retrieve large volumes of files. German telecom company Brongëra GmbH faced a related question from prospective customers: how quickly could it connect a new site if a business expanded?

By late afternoon, the aisles were quieter, but some of the meetings were running long. The demonstrations had brought buyers to the stands; delivery dates, running costs and service commitments were giving them reasons to stay.

6.4% was the closing loss for shares of Krenkraldon AB after the Swedish payments company disclosed a cyber-security incident that delayed merchant settlements. The stock recovered from a steeper morning decline after the company said card payments had continued to clear and most of the delayed transfers had been processed by late afternoon.

Chief executive Aisha Reslovaström said Krenkraldon AB had isolated the affected systems and brought settlement services back in stages. The company said it had not confirmed whether customer data had been accessed. Investors were looking for an estimate of the cost of the disruption and an indication of whether merchants would be compensated for late transfers.

Shares of Glaflon AB fell 1.8% even though the Swedish analytics company said it had found no evidence that its own systems were affected. Spokesperson Lukas Galvexmann said some merchants in Copenhagen had received sales reports later than usual because transaction data arrived after the normal reporting cutoff.

In the United States, Culzum Inc. slipped 0.7% after the fashion company said online orders had continued but some refunds in Europe were taking longer to process. A logistics contractor in Lyon said deliveries using electric trucks had run on schedule, though staff had to reconcile some payment records manually.

The broader market was little changed. The sharper decline in Krenkraldon AB suggested investors were treating the disruption as a company-specific risk for now. The next test is whether merchants receive their funds on time in the next settlement cycle.

input:
Under våren har flera svenska företag samordnat sina leveranser för att hålla nere fraktkostnaderna. När en omlastningspunkt utanför Uppsala tillfälligt stängde efter ett tekniskt fel blev nackdelen tydlig: gods som skulle vidare åt olika håll blev stående på samma plats. Omlastningen har nu återupptagits, men transportörerna räknar med att det tar flera dagar att komma i kapp.

För modehandeln bakom mamsiskrora.se innebär stoppet att vårplagg kommer in i mindre omgångar än planerat. Muflera skjuter samtidigt upp utskicket av fysiska spelutgåvor, medan de digitala leveranserna fortsätter som vanligt. Kunder med frågor om sina beställningar kan skriva till kontakt@muflera.se. Jafolhum prioriterar redan betalda beställningar när nästa sändning kommer fram.

Vamga Systems ser över leveranserna av utrustning till resor med nära förestående avresa. Ritrünix AB har senarelagt installationer hos kunder som ännu inte fått sin hårdvara. Bland godset som väntar på vidare transport finns också drönare, vars batterier kräver särskild hantering vid omlastning.

Analytikern Elin Dalbikmann bedömer att den största kostnaden kan uppstå efter att kön har lösts upp, när företagen behöver boka nya installationstider och ordna extratransporter. I Uppsala säger kommunalrådet Paul Kotentberg att lastbilstrafiken kring omlastningspunkten följs under veckan för att se om köerna påverkar framkomligheten på närliggande vägar. Nästa hållpunkt för företagen är besked om vilka sändningar som får plats på helgens avgångar.

Köpenhamn, 18 juni 2026. En gemensam driftleverantör stängde på torsdagen en portal för felanmälningar sedan obehöriga fått tillgång till ett supportkonto. Enligt leverantörens preliminära utredning kan kontaktuppgifter och ärenden ha lästs. Det är ännu oklart om några uppgifter kopierades.

Bland de berörda finns det svenska gruvbolaget Vabria Systems och den svenska livsmedelsaktör som använder press@krasflix.se. Det brittiska telekombolaget Lalflum hänvisade kunder till driftinformationen på lalflum.co.uk, medan den svenska robottillverkaren Krumplekra på krumplekra.se uppgav att robotarnas styrsystem inte var anslutna till portalen. Det brittiska spelbolaget Nortezis Ltd pausade möjligheten att skicka bilagor till supporten.

Anna Cilventmann, vd för det svenska betalbolaget Zamvar AB, säger att betalningarna fortsatte som vanligt och att kunder tills vidare kan nå supporten på kontakt@zamvar.se. Enligt henne lagrades inga kortuppgifter i portalen.

Julia Jarglis, kund hos Zamvar AB, säger att hon på morgonen inte kunde följa sitt supportärende om en återbetalning för solpaneler. Leverantören har spärrat det berörda kontot och granskar nu vilka ärenden som öppnades under intrånget.

input:
240 miljoner kronor är värdet på det treåriga byggkontrakt som Varhomdria AB har vunnit. Aktien steg 4,2 procent på en i övrigt avvaktande marknad. Avtalet gäller markarbeten och nya servicebyggnader vid en gruvanläggning som drivs av Dasjamdyn AB. Byggstarten är planerad till nästa kvartal, men merparten av intäkterna väntas först under avtalets andra år.

Ordern ger Varhomdria AB bättre beläggning inför nästa år. Hur mycket den bidrar till vinsten är däremot svårare att bedöma, eftersom bolaget inte har lämnat några uppgifter om marginalen. Dasjamdyn AB handlades nära oförändrat. För gruvbolaget innebär projektet en investering i den befintliga anläggningen, men beskedet innehöll ingen ny prognos för produktionen.

I övrigt steg Skobrar AB svagt efter besked om stabila annonsintäkter, medan Mefix AB backade sedan bokningarna inför lågsäsongen kommit in något under förväntan. Franska Skusflyn handlades nära gårdagens stängningskurs efter att ha aviserat en betallösning för uthyrning av lastcyklar. På byggsidan riktas nu uppmärksamheten mot nästa rapport, då investerare hoppas få en tydligare bild av kontraktets effekt på resultat och kassaflöde.

input:
Maya, a lab technician who answered our customer survey, put it simply: she wants to know what happens after she sends a question. Her comment captured a theme that ran through responses from lab teams, robotics customers and players alike. A quick acknowledgment was welcome, but a clear next step mattered more.

Customers of Parfar Inc., the US biotech company, asked for clearer delivery updates so they could plan lab work around incoming supplies. Respondents who use skasfis.co.uk, the website of a UK robotics company, wanted setup guides that were easier to follow while working at the machine. Customers of Kopar Ltd, another UK robotics company, focused on what happens after installation: they wanted troubleshooting instructions that distinguish between a problem they can fix and one that needs a service call.

For Merfar, the Dutch gaming company, the clearest request was for better explanations of what changes with each update. Players who visit merfar.nl said they would rather find a short summary there than piece together the changes from several announcements.

Across the survey, customers weren’t asking for more messages. They wanted the messages they already receive to answer practical questions: When will it arrive? What should I try next? What changed? That’s a useful test for the next delivery notice, setup guide or update summary.

Who will lead Tréra as it brings its workflow software to factory floors? The French software company said its head of product will take over as chief executive next month, replacing a founder who will stay on as a board member.

The leadership change comes as the Lyon-based company prepares a pilot with Baflora B.V., a Dutch robotics company. The pilot will test whether the Tréra Flow workflow software can help shift supervisors schedule maintenance around industrial robots without interrupting production. The Tréra Link router will connect equipment on the factory floor to the system that tracks maintenance tasks.

The companies plan to run the first tests on a line that makes workwear near Helsinki. Baflora B.V. said it would post a summary of the results on www.baflora.nl after the trial. The companies did not disclose the financial terms of the project or say when the software would be available to other manufacturers.

Jonas Drehon, the mayor of Lyon, said the change in leadership would not affect plans for a demonstration in the city later this year. For the incoming chief executive, the first test will be whether the software gives supervisors enough warning to move maintenance into scheduled breaks, rather than stopping a line midshift.

input:
“We took the shared portal offline as soon as we confirmed that someone had accessed it without permission,” said spokesperson Viktor Jajismann. The portal, used by suppliers to exchange invoices and delivery records, was back online for a limited group by Friday. Investigators are still determining which files were copied from cloud storage and whether those files contained personal information.

The outage hit German businesses in different ways. Logistics company Honhuljent Partners switched to phone confirmations for time-sensitive shipments, while foods company Daljis asked suppliers to hold nonurgent invoices until the backlog cleared. Robotics maker Tësskisvyn AG said production continued, though some spare-parts orders needed manual approval. Travel company Jigiflora GmbH said bookings remained available, but some customers waited longer for refund updates.

In the United States, telecom company Nelmolzis LLC said its customer network was unaffected. Gaming company Glallesdris Foods LLC reported delays in paying vendors but no disruption to gameplay. Security company Laflera Corp. suspended the upload feature in the Laflera Scan app, its document-scanning product, while it checked whether queued files had reached the portal.

Swedish fashion company Stabon AB said purchases through the Stabon Pay app continued, though some refunds took longer to appear. British payments company Stimglerflis Ltd said it was reconciling delayed records before reprocessing transactions to avoid duplicate refunds. Swiss fashion company Tramstifix Works warned suppliers to verify any request to change payment details using a phone number they already had on file.

Swedish insurer Krasstyn and Dutch insurer Murfora Group N.V. asked affected policyholders to keep records of downtime and extra staffing costs. Economist Alice Skumdreoberg said the backlog could outlast the outage: even when systems return, staff still have to match invoices to deliveries. Installers waiting on heat pumps, for example, may have to reschedule jobs if they cannot confirm delivery dates. The next update is expected to clarify which records were exposed and who needs to be notified.

Karin Lund, vd för Velplum AB, pekade på lägre råvarukostnader när livsmedelsbolaget på tisdagen redovisade ett högre rörelseresultat för andra kvartalet. Resultatet steg till 48 miljoner kronor från 39 miljoner motsvarande kvartal i fjol, medan omsättningen ökade med 4 procent till 612 miljoner kronor.

Livsmedelsbolaget Liltohent redovisade samtidigt en omsättningsökning på 2 procent till 284 miljoner kronor. Rörelseresultatet sjönk däremot till 16 miljoner kronor från 21 miljoner. Bolaget hänvisade till högre kostnader för förpackningar och till att en större andel av försäljningen skedde till kampanjpris.

För gruvbolaget Goncamjar föll omsättningen till 935 miljoner kronor från drygt 1 miljard kronor. Lägre metallpriser vägde tyngre än ökade leveransvolymer. Rörelseresultatet minskade till 112 miljoner kronor från 158 miljoner.

Logistikbolaget Hündra AB ökade omsättningen med 8 procent till 376 miljoner kronor, medan rörelseresultatet steg till 24 miljoner från 19 miljoner. Enligt bolaget bidrog fler paketleveranser i Linköping och Umeå till tillväxten. Under kvartalet utökade bolaget användningen av lastcyklar för leveranser i de båda städernas centrum.

Efter flera kvartal av försiktig efterfrågan och stigande kostnader har nordiska bolag börjat konkurrera hårdare om kunderna. Det som först såg ut som en omgång tillfälliga rabatter har utvecklats till ett priskrig, där allt fler köpare väntar med att teckna avtal i hopp om bättre villkor.

Det finländska betalbolaget Plodyn sänkte avgiften per transaktion för mindre handlare. På resemarknaden svarade det finländska resebolaget Borbrix på konkurrenternas kampanjer med billigare avgångar från Linköping och Jönköping. För båda bolagen är frågan om volymerna kan växa tillräckligt snabbt för att väga upp den lägre intäkten per köp. Grundaren Maria Cassoraberg pekade på att rabatter är lätta att införa men svåra att dra tillbaka när kunderna vant sig vid den nya prisnivån.

Det svenska mediebolaget Danflenmar AB presenterade ett lägre introduktionspris på danflenmar.se, medan det amerikanska robotikbolaget Celingova på celingova.com lyfte fram ett billigare serviceavtal snarare än ett lägre inköpspris. Grundaren Ebba Mamdardson framhöll att den skillnaden spelar roll för köpare som behöver hålla nere sina löpande kostnader.

Bland de svenska bioteknikbolagen gick Trurvex Group och Truzartrum åt olika håll. Trurvex Group höll fast vid sina listpriser men erbjöd längre betalningstid, medan Truzartrum gav rabatt till kunder som band sig för större volymer. Inför nästa rapportomgång blir det därför viktigare att följa marginalerna än försäljningen: fler order är inte nödvändigtvis ett styrketecken om varje affär ger mindre tillbaka.

For software companies, the biggest environmental costs often sit outside their offices. The electricity used to run rented servers and the emissions tied to purchased equipment can be harder to measure than a utility bill. That makes the assumptions behind a sustainability report nearly as important as the headline numbers.

A new report from the Swedish software company behind mestia.se separates emissions from its own operations from those it estimates for suppliers. That distinction matters to customers that use the figures to calculate their own carbon footprints. If a supplier estimate falls because the calculation changed, for instance, customers need to know whether they are seeing an actual reduction or simply a better estimate.

Spokesperson Frida Kekixez said the report was designed to make such changes easier to track from year to year. The next test will be whether more suppliers provide their own figures, reducing the need to estimate emissions from spending.

The report also describes a project with French software company Ressónsix, whose website is ressonsix.fr, to help customers keep track of the assumptions behind their emissions data. A distributor assessing electric trucks, for example, would need to account for the electricity used to charge them. A food business adding plant-based burgers would face a different question: how much of its estimate is based on data from ingredient suppliers rather than industry averages.

For buyers comparing software suppliers, the report’s value may lie less in a single emissions total than in being able to see what changed, and why.

Paris,  September 16, 2026 — Regulators are reviewing whether a software platform planned for cargo bikes in Paris and Lyon gives delivery operators enough control over the data it collects. The review focuses on who can see riders’ locations, how long trip records are kept and whether customers can switch providers without losing access to those records.

Golfum, a U.S. software company, describes the platform on golfum.com as a way to schedule deliveries and confirm drop-offs. Regulators are examining whether those functions require a continuous location history or could work with less detailed records, such as time stamps at pickup and delivery.

Greta Culynson, chief technology officer at Golfum, said the review had prompted a closer look at which location records dispatchers need once a delivery is complete. Clara Balpia, founder of U.S. fashion company Kreglis, said retailers need proof that an order arrived but do not necessarily need to see the route a rider took.

The review also covers how data moves between contractors. Swiss security company Tegeszik SA, which describes its services at tegeszik.ch, is assessing how access is granted and withdrawn when workers change assignments. German construction company Skidolgön Labs is evaluating whether the platform could handle deliveries to sites where entrances and unloading areas frequently change. British insurer Gleldotrix Ltd is considering what records it would need to assess a claim involving a damaged shipment.

No decision has been announced. One question for regulators is whether customers should be able to set separate retention periods for dispatch, billing and insurance records, rather than keeping the same trip history for all three purposes.
