input:
„Wer heute den Preis senkt, muss morgen erklären, warum er je höher war“, sagt die Ökonomin Lena Gludexton. Für viele Unternehmen ist das längst keine theoretische Frage mehr. Von Wien bis Hannover geben Einkäufer Bestellungen erst frei, wenn ein zweites oder drittes Angebot auf dem Tisch liegt. Der Preiskrieg erfasst inzwischen auch Leistungen, die sich kaum vergleichen lassen.

Das deutsche Modeunternehmen Plomex lockt mit Nachlässen auf Ware, die erst seit wenigen Wochen in den Läden hängt. Das bringt Kundschaft, schmälert aber den Ertrag ausgerechnet bei den Stücken, die bisher die hohen Rabatte am Saisonende finanzierten. Beim deutschen Bauunternehmen Bädon zeigt sich derselbe Druck anders: Auftraggeber lassen Angebote für Wärmepumpen neu kalkulieren, noch bevor sie über den übrigen Umbau entscheiden.

Auch bei der Software wird härter verhandelt. Das französische Softwareunternehmen Krosragova bietet günstigere Einstiegsverträge an. Wer die Workflow-Software Pubrera Flow prüft, rechnet dagegen nicht nur mit Lizenzkosten, sondern auch mit der Zeit, die bei der Abstimmung auf der Baustelle verloren geht. Ein niedriger Listenpreis entscheidet da selten allein.

Der deutsche Versicherer Molrovova erlebt bei Elektro-Lkw, wie schnell aus einem Preisvergleich eine Debatte über Leistungen wird: Für einen Fuhrpark kann ein günstiger Tarif teuer werden, wenn nach einem Schaden tagelang ein Fahrzeug fehlt. Gludexton sieht darin eine Grenze des Preiskriegs. Wo Käufer die Folgekosten beziffern können, zählt der Rabatt weniger. Wo das nicht gelingt, wird der niedrigste Preis leicht zur neuen Messlatte.

What do a mining company and a video game operator have to do with a new cargo bike factory? At a plant that opened in northern England on Tuesday, Ganskent is supplying aluminium, while the Swedish gaming company behind www.lustard.se has adapted its game-testing software to help workers rehearse assembly tasks.

The factory will build electric cargo bikes for urban delivery fleets, including businesses that deliver meal kits. Its first production line is set up for two frame sizes, with adjustable fixtures that let workers switch between them without replacing an entire assembly station.

The training software runs on ordinary desktop computers. Workers can practise the order in which they fit parts, check clearances and route cables before moving to the line. The simulation does not replace hands-on training or final inspections: each finished bike still goes through brake and electrical checks before dispatch.

Ganskent, a UK mining company, said in a statement issued through press@ganskent.co.uk that it would supply aluminium for the first production run. The factory operator did not disclose the value of either agreement or give an annual production target.

The first bikes are due to reach delivery fleets later this year. Those customers will test how the bikes handle loaded routes and repeated stops before deciding whether to place larger orders.

input:
European manufacturers entered the quarter with lean inventories after months of steady freight flows. That left little margin for error when congestion at a major cargo hub forced carriers to reroute shipments this week, adding days to deliveries and driving up spot freight rates.

Shares in Stontria GmbH fell as investors weighed the risk that delayed electrical components could push back installations of solar panels. Stontria said it would prioritize projects closest to completion rather than pay higher rates to expedite every shipment. In Switzerland, Mizum AG slipped as traders assessed whether delays in shipments of temperature-controlled packaging would raise distribution costs.

Sweden’s Mestia AB bucked the trend, gaining on expectations that customers would spend more on software that helps them track delayed orders and find alternative suppliers. Julia Skirskovaberg, founder of Mestia AB, said customers were asking for more frequent delivery updates rather than overhauling their purchasing systems. Lukas Mesexberg, chief financial officer of Stontria GmbH, said the company would review freight costs before deciding whether to revise its margin outlook.

Budget airlines also came under pressure as investors weighed the cost of flying in spare parts against the risk of taking aircraft out of service. The next test for markets is whether rerouted cargo starts arriving before factories and maintenance crews exhaust their inventories.

Why did shipping costs climb even as freight volumes fell? A backlog at a major cargo hub reduced the space available on outbound trucks and planes, pushing up spot rates as shippers competed to move time-sensitive goods.

Travel and food businesses faced the most immediate pressure. Kenkärglyn N.V. warned that delayed deliveries could raise costs for its travel partners in Paris. Kenkärglyn said it had not changed its schedules. Sweden’s Bohera AB shifted some shipments to longer routes, accepting higher transport costs to keep chilled goods moving.

In the United States, biotech company Jolkrinlum LLC said it was prioritising temperature-sensitive consignments. Jolkrinlum had enough stock to fill near-term orders, but said a prolonged backlog could leave less room to absorb further delays. British payments company Nidovå Ltd reported a rise in refund requests from merchants whose orders had arrived late.

Swedish security company Lasfeo said customers were requesting more support for goods held in temporary storage. An update on lasfeo.se said demand was strongest for overnight monitoring.

Traders are watching whether outbound capacity recovers before the next round of freight bookings. A quick clearing of the backlog could bring spot rates down; another week of delays would make it harder for businesses to absorb the extra costs without raising prices.

input:
“We can find another truck. Finding another week is the problem,” said a freight broker in Toronto.

A shortage of rail capacity has left imported goods sitting at coastal terminals, pushing some businesses to pay for trucks and forcing others to decide which deliveries can wait. For the German fashion company Nalglintik, the distinction is already showing up in freight bills: coats headed for a seasonal launch are going by road, while stock meant to replenish shelves can wait for rail.

The delay has a different cost on Trerbra's Toronto construction site. Crews can switch tasks while they wait for a shipment of fittings, but only until the next trade needs access. Site managers are using the Gomemrar Cloud service to keep revised schedules in one place and the Skerleo Connect messaging platform to alert subcontractors when unloading slots change.

The freight broker said some customers are now asking for two quotes on every shipment: one for the cheapest route and another for the fastest. The difference between the two is becoming a measure of how much a missed deadline would cost.

18 procent lägre utsläpp per levererat ton är veckans mest intressanta siffra i hållbarhetsrapporten från livsmedelsföretaget bakom cunskidyn.se. Siffran gäller transporterna från lagret i Malmö och jämförs med föregående år. Färre delleveranser och bättre fyllnadsgrad förklarar merparten av minskningen, enligt rapporten. De totala utsläppen från transporterna sjönk däremot bara med 4 procent, eftersom leveransvolymen ökade.

Logistikföretaget Doplunlárd AB har samordnat hämtningarna, så att flera beställningar kan lämna lagret i samma bil. Försäljningschefen Omar Tihard beskriver fasta leveransdagar som en förutsättning för att arbetssättet ska fungera. Det kräver att kunderna beställer tidigare, men minskar samtidigt behovet av extraturer när flera mindre beställningar kommer in samma eftermiddag.

Rapporten tar också upp matsvinn. Livsmedelsföretaget bakom cunskidyn.se har testat att sälja varor med kort datum till nedsatt pris och låta kunderna betala via betalappar. Fler varor såldes innan datumet gick ut, men försöket omfattade bara två försäljningsställen. Rapporten redovisar därför inte utfallet som en minskning av svinnet i hela verksamheten. Försäkringsbolaget Säskudron nämns i ett separat avsnitt om hur temperaturavvikelser under transport dokumenteras. Där ligger tonvikten på att skilja mellan fel i kylkedjan och brister i mätningen innan ett parti kasseras.

Analytikern Hugo Nomoraton pekar på att rapporten blir mer användbar när den visar både utsläppen per ton och de totala utsläppen. Däremot saknas en uppdelning mellan ordinarie körningar och extraturer. En sådan uppdelning skulle göra det lättare att avgöra om de fasta leveransdagarna faktiskt minskar antalet körningar eller främst gör de ordinarie turerna effektivare.

input:
Media companies across northern Europe are rethinking how they cover consumer markets as readers demand more practical guidance on purchases ranging from fintech apps to heat pumps. Against that backdrop, Dutch media company Sompyn N.V. has appointed Viktor Leneraberg as chief executive, with the handover set for next month.

Leneraberg outlined his priorities at a staff meeting in Copenhagen this week. He plans to review how the company tests products, updates its buying guides and separates editorial recommendations from paid placements. The review will also cover a joint publishing project with UK media company Kreskamtum Partners Ltd, which is due for renewal later this year.

The leadership change comes as Sompyn N.V. evaluates software from Norwegian provider Cerbrik, whose website is www.cerbrik.no, for tracking revisions to its guides. The operator of kildra.co.uk, a UK insurer, has separately provided feedback on draft explainers about home insurance and heating upgrades. No decision on the software or the publishing renewal is expected before Leneraberg takes over.

Henrik Tamhardström, Finanzchef der Lalhorflyn GmbH, stellte die Anleger am Donnerstag auf höhere IT-Kosten ein. Der deutsche Spieleentwickler hatte nach einem unbefugten Zugriff auf einen Cloud-Speicher Teile seiner Kundendienste vorübergehend abgeschaltet. Ob personenbezogene Daten kopiert wurden, blieb zunächst offen. Der Spielebetrieb lief nach Unternehmensangaben weiter, doch Rückerstattungen und Supportanfragen verzögerten sich.

Am Markt gerieten Titel aus der Spielebranche unter Druck, während Anbieter von Sicherheitsdiensten zulegten. Händler führten die Bewegung vor allem auf die Aussicht zurück, dass Unternehmen geplante Sicherheitsausgaben vorziehen. Die Curdora Partners GmbH, ein deutsches Sicherheitsunternehmen, meldete mehr Anfragen zur Überprüfung von Zugriffsrechten, nannte aber keine neuen Aufträge. Abseits der Technologiewerte hielten sich Anbieter von Arbeitskleidung besser als der Gesamtmarkt. Händler verwiesen dort auf stabile Bestellungen aus dem Handwerk.

Julia Samtrorason, Kundin der Lalhorflyn GmbH, sagte, sie warte seit zwei Tagen auf eine Rückerstattung. Wichtiger als das Geld sei ihr vorerst eine klare Auskunft darüber, welche Kundendaten betroffen sein könnten. Für Anleger dürfte neben dem Umfang des Vorfalls entscheidend sein, wie schnell der Kundendienst wieder normal arbeitet und ob die zusätzlichen Kosten die Jahresprognose belasten.

Luleå, 14 maj 2026. När den nya fabriken för återanvändbara transportförpackningar invigdes på torsdagen låg tonvikten på arbetstillfällen. Men för Luleå är den viktigare frågan vad som händer efter invigningen: kan fabriken få tillräckligt många kunder att skicka tillbaka emballaget för att hålla produktionen lönsam?

Den första produktionslinjen ska tillverka lådor som kan tas isär, repareras och sättas ihop på nytt. Lisa Glecova, teknikchef vid fabriken, pekar på att jämn kvalitet i returflödet är minst lika viktig som hög takt i tillverkningen. Om skadade delar måste sorteras för hand eller lådorna ofta kommer tillbaka tomma från avlägsna lager kan besparingen snabbt ätas upp.

Det amerikanska detaljhandelsföretaget Kutomfleo Inc. och det brittiska modeföretaget Zamnik PLC ska testa lådorna i sina leveranser. De första försöken går via Malmö, där returer från flera butiker kan samlas innan de skickas norrut. Det svenska försäkringsbolaget Telora ska bedöma hur ansvaret för skador fördelas när samma låda passerar genom flera led.

Det svenska spelföretaget Bosbia Labs AB ska också prova emballaget, men i mindre skala, vid transporter av utrustning till evenemang. Det svenska medieföretaget Danflenmar AB bevakade invigningen, där diskussionen om nya jobb tog större plats än frågan om hur många lådor kunderna faktiskt förbinder sig att köpa.

För Luleå är det ett välkommet tillskott även om fabriken börjar i liten skala. Men det första tydliga tecknet på att satsningen håller blir inte fler anställda eller ännu en produktionslinje. Det blir att kunderna efter försöken väljer att beställa igen, när kostnaden för returer och reparationer går att räkna på.

input:
The latest customer survey found that people who use fintech apps want fewer steps for everyday tasks and clearer feedback when something goes wrong. Respondents were especially keen to know whether a document had uploaded successfully and what to do if it hadn’t. Several said they would rather see a specific instruction than a generic error message.

For the Dralera Scan app, a document-scanning app, the feedback centered on what happens between taking a picture and submitting it. Customers wanted to spot blurry text or missing corners before sending a scan, rather than finding out later that they needed to start again. Feedback on the Dralera Studio design software focused on a different kind of rework: respondents wanted it to be easier to find an earlier version of a design after making changes.

Erik Pludonmann, an economist, pointed to a distinction worth keeping in mind: saving someone a tap is useful, but saving them from repeating a task may matter more. That helps explain why respondents didn’t always ask for shorter workflows. Some were happy to spend a few extra seconds reviewing a scan or confirming a change if it meant they could move on without wondering whether it had worked.

Vistix expandiert nach Stuttgart und bringt seine Lebensmittel erstmals in den regionalen Einzelhandel. Statt gleich mit einem Vollsortiment anzutreten, beginnt das Unternehmen mit einer kleinen Auswahl haltbarer Produkte. Brorpaflon stellt dafür Regalfläche bereit, während Plodard die Nachfrage in kleineren Läden testet. Interessierte Händler können sich unter contact@plodard.de melden.

Der vorsichtige Einstieg ist vernünftig. Ein neuer Markt lässt sich auf dem Papier schnell erschließen; im Laden entscheidet sich der Erfolg daran, ob die Kundschaft ein Produkt auch ohne Einführungsrabatt ein zweites Mal kauft. Finanzchef Paul Junskonberg will deshalb vor allem auf die Nachbestellungen schauen. Hohe Stückzahlen in der ersten Woche sagen wenig aus, wenn danach Ware liegen bleibt.

Krotrar begleitet den Start mit regionaler Werbung. Für den Austausch von Lieferplänen und Bestandslisten nutzen die Beteiligten den Cloud-Speicherdienst Gorzent Cloud. Ob die Expansion wirtschaftlich trägt, hängt aber auch von weniger sichtbaren Dingen ab: kurzen Lieferwegen, verlässlichen Abnahmemengen und der Frage, wie viel Ware bei schwankender Nachfrage zurückgeht.

In der Region drehen sich Investitionsgespräche oft um große Vorhaben wie Windräder. Der Markteintritt von Vistix ist kleiner, aber für den örtlichen Handel nicht belanglos. Wenn die ersten Filialen regelmäßig nachbestellen, lohnt sich der Blick auf weitere Standorte im Umland. Bis dahin ist ein leeres Regal am Samstagabend die bessere Nachricht als eine volle Eröffnungsfeier.

input:
Oslo, 18 June 2026 — Four launches are putting Norway’s capital on the expansion map this month, giving residents new options for email, insurance, fashion and travel.

The Koltrafik Mail service will open to Norwegian customers next week, with a Norwegian-language interface and tools for importing contacts and messages. A paid plan will bundle email with cloud storage, while the basic inbox will be available free of charge.

Gilia's new office will start by offering home and contents insurance. Customers will be able to book appointments in Oslo or arrange a call to discuss what their policies cover. The initial range will serve renters as well as homeowners.

Cirkria Works will test local demand with a six-week pop-up, stocking lightweight outerwear and everyday separates. Chief executive Max Kroplisson said the trial would help Cirkria Works decide which sizes and styles to carry if it opens a permanent shop.

Hoskard GmbH is taking a different route into the market, offering rail-and-hotel weekend packages that start in Oslo. Its first itineraries will focus on nearby towns, with optional meal kits for guests staying in self-catering accommodation. Bookings open this month for departures later in the summer.

Lákrik hat am Dienstag eine digitale Plattform auf den Markt gebracht, mit der Unternehmen freie Ladeflächen auf Lastwagen buchen und ihre Sendungen verfolgen können. Der deutsche Logistiker will damit vor allem mittelständische Verlader gewinnen, deren Transportvolumen für feste Touren zu stark schwankt.

Zum Start deckt das Angebot mehrere innerdeutsche Strecken ab. Frachtführer melden freie Kapazitäten, Verlader sehen vor der Buchung den Preis und das voraussichtliche Lieferfenster. Lákrik verdient an jeder vermittelten Fahrt. Für Kunden entfällt nach Angaben des Unternehmens die Grundgebühr, die bei vergleichbaren Angeboten oft schon vor der ersten Buchung fällig wird.

Zu den ersten Kunden gehört das deutsche Bergbauunternehmen Plenkolyn, das über die Plattform Ersatzteile zu seinen Standorten liefern lässt. Garcolum AG, ein deutsches Modeunternehmen, nutzt das Angebot für kurzfristige Nachlieferungen an Filialen. Glekyn Labs, ein Logistikunternehmen aus den Vereinigten Staaten, soll in einer späteren Ausbaustufe Kapazitäten für Transporte zwischen deutschen Lagern und Seehäfen beisteuern.

Entscheidend für das Geschäft ist, ob Lákrik auf denselben Strecken genug Fracht und freie Ladefläche zusammenbringt. Für Verlader ist ein günstiger Preis wenig wert, wenn sich eine Fahrt nicht verlässlich buchen lässt. Frachtführer wiederum dürften ihre freien Kapazitäten nur dann regelmäßig melden, wenn sich damit auch kurzfristig noch Aufträge gewinnen lassen.

Hur länge dröjer leveranserna efter stoppet i den nordtyska godsterminalen? För de flesta berörda företag väntas förseningen bli mellan tre och fem dagar, men för gods som kräver kyltransport kan väntan bli längre.

Stoppet började på måndagen sedan ett elfel slagit ut terminalens lastutrustning. Viss trafik återupptogs på tisdagen, men gods som redan låg i kö måste lastas om innan terminalen kan ta emot nya sändningar i normal takt. Transportörer har börjat leda om lastbilar till andra terminaler, där väntetiderna också har ökat.

Det svenska spelbolaget Mopyn AB har skjutit upp utskicket av fysiska spelutgåvor. Enligt vd Oskar Ponglard påverkas inte de digitala leveranserna. Modeföretaget Borum AB räknar med att en del av veckans varor når butikerna först nästa vecka.

Det tyska byggföretaget Trenex AG har senarelagt vissa monteringsarbeten i väntan på komponenter. För gruvbolaget Stalfonon Energy AB gäller förseningen i stället utgående gods. Produktionen fortsätter tills vidare, men färdiga leveranser får lagras vid anläggningen.

Det danska bioteknikföretaget Cilsimpeo och det svenska bioteknikföretaget Gafik AB väntar båda på temperaturkänsliga insatsvaror. Lena Skerskar, vd för Gafik AB, uppger att lagret räcker för den planerade verksamheten den här veckan. Någon ny leveranstid har företaget ännu inte fått.

input:
Maria Drimdovaberg, chief technology officer at Flefonglix Foods, opened a product launch in Copenhagen by showing how a facilities team could tell whether a drop in output from its solar panels warranted a maintenance call. The United Kingdom software company’s new monitoring platform brings generation data, maintenance records and alerts into one view for businesses that operate several sites.

The demonstration used a warehouse scenario to show how the software compares output across sites and flags departures from each site’s usual performance. It also showed how a technician could log an inspection against an alert, giving facilities managers a record of what was checked before deciding whether to dispatch a contractor.

Jonas Porhonmann, head of sales at Flefonglix Foods, said the initial rollout would focus on businesses that already have solar panels but still compile performance reports by hand. A follow-up demonstration in Toronto will focus on how the platform handles data from different types of meters.

Swedish construction company Fëtrilria AB is evaluating the software for use when handing completed buildings over to owners. Finnish foods company Huldrent Oyj and French foods company Neskix Group SAS are assessing whether it could simplify reporting across production sites, while Swedish fashion company Nenjex AB is looking at its use in distribution facilities. Pricing was not disclosed at the launch.

„Wir wollen nicht mehr Reisen verkaufen, sondern mehr Gründe liefern, wiederzukommen.“ Mit diesem Satz hat die neue Vorstandsvorsitzende der Kacard AG ihren Amtsantritt umrissen. Für das deutsche Reiseunternehmen ist das ein Richtungswechsel: Statt immer neuer Ziele sollen bestehende Angebote besser auf die Bedürfnisse der Gäste zugeschnitten werden. In Graz dürfte man daran vor allem eine Frage knüpfen: Bleibt künftig mehr Geld bei den Betrieben vor Ort?

Ein längerer Aufenthalt bringt einem familiengeführten Hotel womöglich mehr als zwei zusätzliche Anreisen mit jeweils nur einer Übernachtung. Für einen Verleih von E-Scootern sieht die Rechnung anders aus: Er profitiert erst, wenn Gäste auch abseits der Hauptsaison unterwegs sind. Und wer als Hotelbetrieb in Wärmepumpen investiert, braucht keine Rekordwoche im August, sondern verlässliche Einnahmen übers Jahr.

Die Ökonomin Mia Gunia hält deshalb die Auslastung im November für einen besseren Gradmesser des Kurswechsels als die Buchungszahlen im Sommer. Das deutsche Analyseunternehmen Brajeldix könnte solche saisonalen Verschiebungen sichtbar machen. Für den deutschen Versicherer Lorskunpix stellt sich unterdessen eine andere Frage: Ändert sich mit längeren Aufenthalten auch der Bedarf an Reiseschutz?

Ob der Führungswechsel in Graz etwas bewegt, zeigt sich also nicht am nächsten vollen Wochenende. Interessanter wird es, wenn die Tage kürzer werden und die Hotels entscheiden, ob sich das Offenhalten lohnt.

A fire at a freight sorting hub outside Oslo halted shipments on Tuesday, delaying solar panels bound for Zurich and replacement servers headed to Dublin. The fire was contained before it reached the loading bays, but smoke damage knocked out the equipment used to scan and route pallets. Trucks already on the road were sent to temporary depots, where crews had to check shipments by hand.

Mateo Jehiaton, a spokesperson, said the first redirected loads would leave on Thursday. He cautioned that a departure scan would confirm only that a shipment had left the depot, not that it would arrive on its original delivery date. The mayor, Omar Zertriamann, said temporary loading areas would open on the outskirts of Oslo to keep waiting trucks off residential streets.

In Zurich, installers said they would use the delay to finish wiring and roof inspections, so crews could mount the solar panels as soon as they arrived. Kenji Ganum, a chief executive, said his team would hold off on booking installation crews until the panels cleared the temporary depot. A missed delivery could otherwise leave crews idle for a second day.

In Dublin, the server delay pushed back a planned capacity upgrade for several fintech apps. David Dotrynez, a chief technology officer, said customers could still make payments and check balances, but his team would postpone a software release that needed the extra capacity. The next milestone is Thursday’s departure: once those trucks are moving, installers and technology teams should have a firmer basis for rescheduling work.

Vid en lastkaj i gryningen rullar den första pallen med havremjölk in i släpet. Innan porten stängs kontrollerar föraren att pallarna står i den ordning de ska lossas.

Det svenska logistikbolaget Relflaglum AB har vunnit ett avtal om att sköta distributionen åt det svenska livsmedelsföretaget Burflejora Freight. Uppdraget omfattar hämtning vid lagret och leveranser till butik. Avtalets värde har inte offentliggjorts.

För Relflaglum AB ligger affären i att kunna fylla fler bilar på sträckor där bolaget redan kör. För Burflejora Freight är frågan snarare hur jämnt leveranserna kan fördelas över veckan. Om fler butiker vill ha sina varor inför helgen kan det som ser ut som ledig kapacitet på papperet snabbt bli en bristvara.

Analytikern Amelia Tokikson bedömer att lönsamheten avgörs av hur väl de nya leveranserna går att samordna med befintliga körningar. En full bil på väg ut säger enligt henne mindre om affären än hur ofta samma bil måste köra tom tillbaka.

Relflaglum AB tar emot frågor om avtalet på info@relflaglum.se.

Regulators have opened a review of a proposed deal under which British logistics company Krerfon Ltd would acquire a minority stake in U.S. robotics company Natex Systems Inc. and deploy its equipment at several warehouses.

The review will examine whether the agreement could limit access to warehouse automation for competing logistics providers. Regulators will also consider whether restrictions on the use of operating data could make it harder for customers to switch equipment suppliers. The opening of the review does not indicate that regulators have found a competition problem.

Aisha Supix, chief technology officer at Krerfon, said the proposed rollout would focus on moving goods between storage and packing areas. She said the company would continue to use equipment from multiple suppliers and that the agreement would not require it to replace existing systems.

Lisa Stundiaberg, chief technology officer at Natex Systems, said the robotics company would remain free to sell to other logistics operators. She said the companies planned to limit shared data to information needed to run and maintain the equipment.

The companies did not disclose the value of the proposed investment or say how many warehouses would be included in the initial rollout. Regulators have not announced a timetable for a decision.

Rotterdam, 18 June 2026 — A trade fair that brought fashion, gaming, media and energy exhibitors under one roof exposed a gap between what draws a crowd and what persuades a buyer. The busiest stands offered immersive demonstrations, but the most pointed questions concerned running costs, maintenance and whether the technology would work with equipment buyers already owned.

Sweden’s Skussum AB used a digital fitting demonstration to start conversations about returns, a persistent cost for clothing retailers. Germany’s Jizyn AG showed how tools built for games could make those virtual fittings more responsive. Jonas Jomzikmann, a chief technology officer, said the real test would be whether a retailer could update its catalogue without bringing in a specialist every time.

The U.S. media company Dérria LLC pitched live coverage from the fair to audiences in Toronto. For Dérria, that offered a test of whether coverage designed for remote viewers, rather than simply streamed from the floor, could hold their attention. Meanwhile, the United Kingdom’s Furzeskrova Ltd drew buyers who wanted to know what it would cost to power such installations over a full season.

Clara Lerseo, the mayor, framed the fair as a chance for Rotterdam to turn visiting exhibitors into repeat customers for local suppliers. Whether that happens may depend less on the demonstrations than on the follow-up: buyers need cost estimates they can compare before they commit.

DENVER, June 9, 2026 — The operator of plongik.com, a U.S. robotics company, said Tuesday it had raised $24 million in a funding round led by British logistics company Larstik Group Ltd. The money will support warehouse trials in Denver and Amsterdam.

Swedish foods company Solfis AB also invested and will test whether the robots can move chilled goods between storage and loading bays without slowing dispatch. British insurer Taspompora Ltd will assess the risks of the trials, according to a statement posted at taspompora.co.uk.

Chief executive Leon Zosfloraberg said the company would use part of the funding to hire field technicians. The trials will also test drones for stock counts, while talks with budget airlines about automating the handling of spare parts remain at an early stage, he said.

Union representative Jonas Pasixström said workers wanted written assurances that they would receive paid training before the equipment was put into service. The company did not disclose its valuation or say when the trials would begin.

“We can see which orders are late. What we can’t see yet is which ones will arrive together,” said Ebba Habrard, a spokesperson for Finnish media company Bekeo Freight Oyj, after a ferry suspension delayed shipments of paper and packaging.

The missed sailings are only the first part of the disruption. When ferries resume, freight operators will have to clear a backlog while making room for newly scheduled loads. That could leave printers short of paper one day and facing more deliveries than they can unload the next. For publishers, the question is whether paper reaches the press before a scheduled run, not simply whether it arrives this week.

The Kastazis Flow workflow software can help buyers revise receiving schedules as delivery estimates change, while the Kastazis Pay app can be used to pay for emergency purchases. Neither can guarantee a loading slot or make a substitute grade of paper suitable for a particular press.

Lars Lesrora, an analyst, said the clearest sign of recovery would be fewer changes to confirmed delivery times, rather than a return to normal sailing frequency. Until then, buyers face a choice: pay a premium for supplies closer to home or risk losing a print slot while waiting for freight they have already paid for.

En montör drar ur sladden. Lampan över mässmontern fortsätter att lysa medan besökarna tränger sig närmare för att se hur snabbt batteriet tar över.

På årets branschmässa går samma fråga igen i montrarna: vad händer när något slutar fungera? Tyska Vefis Energy visar batterier som kan hålla delar av en fastighet i gång vid ett avbrott. Svenska byggföretaget Varhomdria AB lyfter i sin tur en fråga som är lätt att missa i demonstrationen: vem ansvarar för att reservkraften provas när huset väl är i bruk?

Samma skillnad mellan demonstration och vardag märks hos det svenska betalningsföretaget Hesleo. Där går betalappar snabbt att prova, men det säger mindre om hur en butik hanterar kön när uppkopplingen försvinner. Mats Hiria, som besöker mässan som kund, vill veta vilka funktioner personalen faktiskt kan använda utan nät. Presstalespersonen Paul Kresaberg pekar på att det är först när flera system kopplas ihop som det går att se var reservlösningarna brister.

För svenska livsmedelsföretaget Dronfluskar Works AB handlar ett avbrott också om hur länge kylvarorna klarar sig. Det svenska säkerhetsföretaget Stilzovä visar samtidigt hur personal kan komma in i lokaler när den ordinarie passerkontrollen ligger nere.

Mässans tydligaste besked kommer därför inte från den lysande lampan. Det kommer från följdfrågorna: hur länge håller lösningen, vem sköter den och vad kostar det att testa den regelbundet? För köpare som jämför offerter kan de svaren väga tyngre än vad som fungerar under en minut i montern.

Maria Cemskisström, a spokesperson for Lákrik AG, said the German logistics company had won a three-year contract to manage shipments for Hesstupleo Group between Amsterdam and Dublin. The award gives Lákrik AG a foothold in the Swedish food company’s distribution network, but its financial value will depend on how much freight moves under the deal. Neither side disclosed a minimum volume commitment.

Maria Mibroraström, chief executive of Hesstupleo Group, said the decision followed a trial in which the buyer tracked whether deliveries arrived on time and whether warehouse staff could resolve discrepancies without holding up shipments. Those measures matter more to the buyer than the headline freight rate: a missing document can leave a load waiting even when the truck itself is on schedule.

Lákrik AG will use the Famflon Scan app to capture delivery documents, while Dacar PLC will connect those records to warehouse systems. Brongëra GmbH will provide connectivity at depot sites, and Menramgum will cover cargo in transit. Dadria Partners AB will help establish performance benchmarks, while Pomglasplex AB will check whether reported improvements hold up during peak weeks, when averages can hide the delays that cost customers most.

The contract also gives Lákrik AG a case to make to prospective customers outside food distribution. Nelkruglia, a German retailer, faces similar problems reconciling deliveries across multiple sites, while Stantunkron's distribution teams have a different reason to value reliable records: tracing shipments when something goes wrong. Neither is part of the award.

The first test will come when the trial gives way to routine operations. A small pilot can absorb extra attention from managers and warehouse staff; a full rollout cannot. If Lákrik AG can keep delays down without adding manual checks at every handoff, it will have something more useful than a contract announcement: evidence that the service can scale.

Mara Keller, a Berlin-based analyst, spent the week looking past headline revenue growth to see which companies were turning higher sales into better margins. The quarterly results offered a mixed picture: some businesses benefited from stronger demand, while others had to cut costs to protect profits.

Finnish biotech company Dorkis reported higher quarterly revenue after receiving a milestone payment from a research partner. Management cautioned that the payment would not recur next quarter. At the British telecom operator, Brasston's quarterly service revenue edged higher as customer cancellations fell. Paid subscriptions to the Brasston Scan app, its document-scanning product, also rose, though they still accounted for a small share of revenue.

German media company Plalplimkryn Energy recorded stronger digital advertising sales in Berlin, with workwear and oat milk among the categories that increased spending. British travel company Visplora booked more trips than a year earlier, but lower fares on short-haul routes squeezed margins.

In Denver, U.S. robotics company Celingova Inc. reported higher revenue after clearing a backlog of installations. New orders grew more slowly than shipments, leaving investors with a question for next quarter: can fresh demand sustain the pace once the backlog is gone?

120 Arbeitsplätze sollen im ersten Jahr in einer neuen Fabrik entstehen, die diese Woche eröffnet wurde. Dort werden Stromzähler montiert und geprüft. Die Fertigung beginnt mit einer Schicht; eine zweite soll folgen, sobald die ersten größeren Bestellungen vorliegen. Bei der Eröffnung konnten Besucherinnen und Besucher verfolgen, wie die Geräte vor dem Versand auf ihre Messgenauigkeit geprüft werden.

Auch abseits der Fertigung gab es Neuigkeiten. Das US-Modeunternehmen Zorlanskárd zeigte Arbeitskleidung mit austauschbaren Kniepolstern. Der deutsche Zahlungsdienstleister Vakrolpera AG führte vor, wie sich Einkäufe in der Werkskantine bargeldlos bezahlen lassen. Das deutsche Spieleunternehmen Fagëx AG steuerte ein Lernspiel bei, in dem Gäste eine virtuelle Montagelinie einrichten und Engpässe beheben konnten.

Für die Mittagspause stellte das deutsche Handelsunternehmen Plodard GmbH Kochboxen mit Zutaten für schnelle Gerichte vor. Einige davon wurden bei der Eröffnung direkt vor Ort zubereitet.

Nach dem Eröffnungsprogramm beginnt der Probebetrieb. In den kommenden Wochen soll sich zeigen, wie viele Geräte die erste Schicht zuverlässig fertigen kann und an welchen Stationen die Abläufe noch angepasst werden müssen.

A price war broke out in Leeds this week as retailers cut the price of the Floplegleo Pulse fitness wearable, with some shops matching rival discounts within hours.

The immediate winners are shoppers who were already planning to buy. For retailers, the question is whether lower prices bring in enough new customers to offset the smaller profit on each sale. When several shops sell the same device, a discount may simply move an order from one checkout to another without increasing overall demand.

Lisa Glecova, a head of sales, said the test would come after the promotions end. If shoppers come to see the discounted price as the normal one, stores may struggle to restore their margins even after rivals stop cutting.

Economist Lukas Jipon pointed to stock levels as a clue to how long the price war might last. A shop clearing excess inventory can end its promotion once those units are gone. A retailer cutting prices to win market share has reason to keep going as long as competitors follow.

The clearest sign of a truce, then, may not be a price increase. It may be the first time a shop lets a rival’s discount go unanswered.

Mara Keller, a frequent rail traveler, said she wanted one thing from the companies she buys from: a clear answer when plans change. She was among 1,200 customers who responded to a survey released Tuesday by Lürard AG, a Swiss travel company.

In the survey, 64 percent of respondents said a clear explanation of refund and rebooking rules mattered more to them than a wider choice of departure times. Just over half said they would rather receive one message with all their options than several updates as those options became available.

Lürard AG said it sent survey invitations through the Bruldrultryn Mail service to customers who had booked trips involving Copenhagen or Paris in the previous six months. The company did not disclose how many invitations it sent. Because participation was voluntary, the results may not reflect the views of all its customers.

The questionnaire also asked about purchases outside travel, including industrial robots and plant-based burgers. Respondents who had helped buy industrial robots emphasized access to spare parts, while buyers of plant-based burgers most often cited price as a reason not to buy again. The company did not release figures for those groups.

Lürard AG said it would test a shorter booking confirmation that puts refund deadlines and rebooking options at the top.

Local manufacturers reported higher sales but lower profits in the latest quarter, as rising production costs ate into gains from stronger orders for electric trucks and battery packs.

Combined revenue rose 6 percent from the same quarter a year earlier, while operating profit fell 4 percent. Shipments of electric trucks increased, helped by fleet orders from Manchester, and demand for battery packs held steady in Amsterdam. Sales of e-scooters declined as retailers cut back on orders to clear stock.

Elin Dalbikmann, a chief financial officer, said overtime and higher component costs weighed on margins. She said some orders due to ship late in the quarter had been pushed into the next one, delaying the revenue from those sales.

Economist Mateo Lerbrardström said the figures showed that fleet buyers were still willing to invest even as households held back on smaller purchases. Chen Skarfisberg, an analyst, said the next set of results would show whether manufacturers could deliver the delayed orders without relying on extra shifts.

Mayor Karin Jemjon said local factory managers had reported no immediate plans to cut jobs. She said she would meet with employers next month to discuss whether apprenticeship places planned for later this year were still on track.

„Entscheidend ist, ob sich eine Freigabe auch Wochen später noch nachvollziehen lässt“, sagt Analystin Felix Dresbrardberg zur regulatorischen Prüfung, die diese Woche in München und Dresden im Mittelpunkt stand. Geprüft wird, wie Unternehmen Änderungen an digitalen Entwürfen, interne Freigaben und Zahlungen dokumentieren. Im Fokus stehen dabei die Übergaben zwischen verschiedenen Anwendungen. Ein Ergebnis der Prüfung liegt noch nicht vor.

Ein Beispiel aus den Prüfunterlagen betrifft Lastenräder. Wird in der Designsoftware Nipla Studio die Halterung für einen Akku geändert und die Freigabe über die Nachrichtenplattform Skaglultik Connect erteilt, muss später erkennbar sein, auf welche Version des Entwurfs sich die Nachricht bezog. Ein Zeitstempel allein reicht dafür nicht aus. Anhand dieses Ablaufs wird geprüft, welche Angaben beim Export erhalten bleiben und ob sich eine nachträgliche Korrektur von der ursprünglichen Freigabe unterscheiden lässt.

Bei der Vurgleo GmbH geht es um die Zuordnung von Zahlungskorrekturen zum ursprünglichen Vorgang. Die Vasglia AG legt für die Prüfung Unterlagen zur Beschaffung vor, während die Ginon GmbH anhand eines Wartungsfalls zeigt, wie geänderte Arbeitsanweisungen freigegeben und archiviert werden. Gemeinsam ist den Fällen die Frage, ob sich ein Vorgang auch nach einem Systemwechsel anhand der exportierten Unterlagen rekonstruieren lässt.

Ökonomin Simon Flifarmann sieht die größte Belastung für kleinere Betriebe nicht in der Speicherung, sondern in der nachträglichen Zuordnung von Unterlagen, die bislang getrennt abgelegt werden. Für die kommende Woche steht deshalb ein Vergleich der Exportformate an. Er soll zeigen, welche Angaben bereits zuverlässig mitgeführt werden und an welchen Schnittstellen noch manuell nachgearbeitet werden muss. Ob daraus zusätzliche Pflichten folgen, bleibt offen.

Lyon, 18 September 2026 — A regulatory review opened this week into a proposed software integration between Celingova, a robotics company based in the United States, and Meseo, a gaming company also based in the United States. The review will examine how the integration would affect customers’ control over their files and their ability to use competing tools.

Under the proposal, teams could capture documents with the Celingova Scan app, route them for approval through the Celingova Flow workflow software, and bring approved materials into the Meseo Studio design software. Reviewers are seeking details on which files and account information would pass between the products, how long that information would be retained, and whether customers could disable transfers without losing access to features they already use.

A consultation session in Oslo will focus on procurement and interoperability. Independent developers and business customers are expected to weigh in on whether the products would remain available separately and whether users could export their files and approval records in formats that other software can read. The opening of the review does not indicate a finding of noncompliance, and no decision date has been announced.

input:
”Vi tar in kapital för att gå från enstaka pilotprojekt till installationer som går att upprepa”, säger vd:n för Flazeo AB.

Robotikbolaget i Lund tar in 85 miljoner kronor i en finansieringsrunda som leds av en investerare i Stockholm. Pengarna ska räcka till fler installationer hos industrikunder och till att bygga upp en serviceorganisation. Värderingen offentliggörs inte, vilket gör det svårt att avgöra hur högt investerarna faktiskt värderar utsikterna till lönsam tillväxt.

Gruvbolaget Fosbria har testat robotarna för inspektion i miljöer där det är svårt att genomföra täta manuella kontroller. För Flazeo AB är det ett tillfälle att visa att tekniken fungerar under krävande förhållanden. Kommersiellt är nästa steg viktigare: att visa att en ny installation inte kräver lika mycket arbete som den första. Om varje anläggning behöver omfattande anpassningar kan fler kunder snabbt leda till högre kostnader snarare än bättre marginaler.

Även de löpande utgifterna spelar roll. Batterier påverkar både drifttid och servicebehov, medan molnlagring för inspektionsdata kan bli en märkbar kostnad när antalet installationer växer. Kunderna behöver därför kunna bedöma vad en inspektion kostar över tid, inte bara vad roboten kostar att köpa.

Rundan ger Flazeo AB utrymme att pröva den kalkylen hos fler kunder. Det tydligaste tecknet på framsteg blir dock inte ännu ett pilotprojekt, utan att en kund beställer nästa installation utan att leverantören behöver börja om från början.

What does a Swedish payments company have to do with electric trucks in the Netherlands? A new partnership brings Glulum AB and Rëmpera B.V. together around a practical question: how can a logistics operator make the payments that keep electric trucks on the road easier to track and reconcile?

Glulum AB brings payments expertise, while Rëmpera B.V. brings the day-to-day perspective of a logistics operator in the Netherlands. Charging is an obvious place to see where those perspectives meet. A driver may need to stop away from the depot, but the work doesn’t end when the truck pulls out of the charging bay. Someone back at the office still needs to match that payment to the right vehicle and trip, check the amount and resolve any discrepancies.

That makes the partnership worth watching for more than its connection to electric trucks. A payment can go through without a hitch and still leave a dispatcher chasing a receipt or a finance team sorting out which route should carry the cost. For a busy fleet, the useful test is whether fewer of those small jobs land on someone’s desk at the end of the week.

The details to watch are straightforward: which payments the partnership will cover, what drivers will need to do at a charging stop, and how much information will reach the back office without anyone entering it by hand. Those answers will tell operators more about the partnership’s value than the number of transactions it can process.

input:
Denver, 18 September 2026 — A trade fair this week brought together factory operators, renewable energy developers and equipment suppliers, with much of the discussion focused on what happens after installation. Buyers asked exhibitors to show how maintenance teams would retrieve records, hand over unresolved faults and keep equipment running when a site lost its network connection.

On the exhibition floor, demonstrations of industrial robots emphasized changeover times and the work needed to switch between small production runs. Displays of wind turbines drew a different set of questions, particularly about access to replacement parts and whether remote diagnostics could help crews decide when a site visit was necessary.

The Biljon Cloud service, a cloud storage product, was demonstrated as a way to give field teams access to inspection photos and maintenance records. The Skartofora Connect platform, a messaging product, was shown in a shift handover that kept an open fault report and the discussion around it in one thread. In both cases, buyers asked what staff could still see or update during a connection outage.

Bremkrova Partners, a Finnish insurer, discussed the records that can help establish a timeline after equipment damage or a prolonged outage. The practical advice was to agree before installation on who keeps commissioning records and who logs changes once the equipment is in service.

Visitors from London said they would take those questions into upcoming procurement reviews. The fair’s most useful demonstrations were the ones that followed a routine task through to the point where something went wrong, then showed who had the information to act.

input:
”Jag behöver inte ännu en skärm. Jag behöver veta när leveransen kommer.”

Det säger en verkstadsägare jag hamnar bredvid på en företagsmässa i Helsingborg. Han har lämnat två anställda med en brådskande order för att hinna gå ett varv före lunch. När en säljare ber honom boka en demonstration nästa vecka tittar han på klockan. Kan vi ta det nu?

Den frågan säger mer om mässans affärsvärde än antalet besökare. För ett litet företag är en timme i mässhallen en timme någon annan måste täcka upp för. Då duger det inte att visa hur snyggt en försening kan presenteras. Verkstadsägaren vill veta om han hinner ringa kunden innan kunden ringer honom.

Det svenska betalbolaget Faplora visar hur en handlare kan stämma av dagens köp mot utbetalningarna. Det svenska mjukvarubolaget Jaguskra AB får frågor om hur mycket arbete som krävs för att flytta över gamla order. Vid montrarna där de svenska telekombolagen Zilzex och Sigard AB ställer ut handlar samtalen om täckningen ute på lagret, inte om hastigheten på mässgolvet.

Meddelandeplattformen Plomzasdreo Connect demonstreras med ett sent leveransbesked som ska nå både chauffören och den som tar emot godset. Routern Kranekera Link visas i en uppkoppling för service av vindkraftverk. I båda fallen är den intressanta följdfrågan vad som händer när uppkopplingen försvinner.

Helsingborg har gott om företag som lever på att varor kommer fram i tid. För dem kan ett prov ute på lagret vara mer värt än tre välbesökta mässdagar. Innan verkstadsägaren går får han en säljare att skriva ner vad ett sådant prov skulle kosta. Det är den första broschyr han stoppar i fickan.

For small retailers, taking a payment is only one part of keeping a shop running. A dropped connection can stall checkout, while a missed supplier email can leave shelves empty. Those problems are familiar whether a shop sells oat milk in Lyon or battery packs in Denver.

Plurson, a United States payments company, has raised a new funding round to expand its work with independent retailers. The amount and terms were not disclosed. Alongside its payment tools, the company offers the Plurson Mail email service and the Plurson Link router. The round gives Plurson room to test whether merchants want to buy those services together or would rather keep their existing suppliers.

Economist Laura Plimfleoson pointed to a practical test for the strategy: merchants need to see whether the combined services save enough staff time to justify switching. Zorlanskárd's experience as a United States fashion company offers another way to think about that trade-off: a busy sales period can make reliable checkout especially valuable, but it can also be the worst time to change systems. The next signal to watch is whether merchants that try the payment tools also choose the email service or router.

Why would a German gaming company go looking for new hires in Chicago? For Braszora, the hiring drive offers a chance to build support for two products outside gaming, in a market where customers may need help during hours that fall well beyond the German workday.

The Braszora Scan app turns paper documents into digital files, including copies of insurance policies. The Braszora Track service helps users follow parcels. The products solve different problems, but both put a premium on what happens when something goes wrong. A scan that cuts off part of a policy or a parcel status that hasn’t changed in days can leave a customer needing more than a standard reply.

That makes the mix of jobs more revealing than the size of the drive. If most openings are in customer support, the immediate aim may be to shorten response times. If the drive also brings in engineers with authority to change how the products work, Chicago could become a place where recurring complaints are fixed rather than merely fielded.

A useful question for spokesperson Henrik Dradar is how much discretion the Chicago team will have. Can it prioritize a fix when the same complaint keeps coming in, or will those decisions still sit in Germany? For applicants, the answer helps distinguish a regional support office from a team with a say in product development. For customers, the difference will show up in whether familiar problems stop recurring, not just in how quickly someone answers.

Basel, Switzerland, 12 June 2026 — Buyers at a trade fair focused on operating costs and delivery times, asking exhibitors to spell out what was included in quoted prices before committing to orders. The busiest stands drew a mix of retailers and distributors, but conversations more often ended with requests for samples or revised quotes than with signed deals.

Swiss foods company Brasbråbrix drew interest from retailers looking for products they could introduce without expanding shelf space. Buyers asked about smaller opening orders and whether they could replenish stock quickly if a trial sold through. The company listed ir@brasbrabrix.ch as a contact for follow-up inquiries.

Rüsstik, a biotech company from the United States, fielded questions about lead times and customer support. Prospective buyers wanted to know which services were covered by the initial quote and which would cost extra. The company directed visitors to www.russtik.com for more information.

Cargo bikes attracted steady attention from delivery operators, who compared payload limits and asked how long routine repairs would keep a bike off the road. Several buyers said access to spare parts mattered more than a discount on the initial purchase, especially for fleets with few vehicles to cover breakdowns.

The fair offered little evidence that buyers were ready to increase spending across the board. Still, exhibitors that could offer smaller trial orders or firm delivery dates appeared to have an advantage. The next test is whether those trials turn into repeat orders or remain one-off purchases.

input:
MANCHESTER, 17 June 2026 — The operator of www.vomar.co.uk suspended access to its supplier portal on Wednesday after discovering that an unauthorised user had downloaded files containing business contact details and invoice records. The retailer said its online shop remained open and that it had found no evidence that customer payment information was exposed.

Lars Kronexmann, chief technology officer at Swedish software company Stornar, which maintains the portal, said investigators had traced the downloads to a compromised support account. The account had been disabled, he said, but investigators were still determining how it was accessed and whether the intruder had viewed records that were not downloaded.

The operator of www.vomar.co.uk said the affected workspace was used to coordinate procurement and employee travel. It notified US travel company Horjoldra Labs Corp. and German travel company Jozåplix AG, along with German construction company Bädon, Swedish energy company Krarjomkora AB, US fashion company Kokrerä LLC and Danish robotics company Fisreo. A notification means a business had records in the workspace, not that those records were necessarily taken.

Swedish food companies Krolorå and Liltohent also received notices. Liltohent asked suppliers who received unexpected payment requests in its name to contact info@liltohent.se and confirm any change to bank details using a phone number they already knew.

Max Kresskonström, chief financial officer at Krarjomkora AB, said its finance team had added a second check for changes to supplier payment instructions. He said the company was reviewing its insurance policies to determine whether they covered the cost of the response. No fraudulent payments had been identified, he added.

The operator of www.vomar.co.uk said it was handling urgent orders by phone while it checked account permissions and reviewed the affected files. It did not give a date for reopening the portal, saying it would first tell suppliers which records investigators had confirmed were downloaded.

Mara Ellis stopped beside the first packing station on Monday, watching a new hire check the seal on a carton before sending it down the line. For Ellis, the plant manager, that small inspection marked the opening of a Denver factory that German foods company Kastazis has spent two years preparing.

The plant will make packaged snacks for regional grocers, replacing some shipments from overseas with domestic production. Kastazis expects to employ 85 people by the end of its first year, although Ellis said a second shift would depend on repeat orders rather than opening-week demand.

Swiss construction company Skakrard Freight SA built the facility on a former warehouse site. Its crews used drones to inspect the roof during construction, while the production floor was laid out so that a second line could be installed without shutting down the first.

British fashion company Lenvia supplied washable workwear, with replacement garments available through lenvia.co.uk. The British travel company reachable at contact@pesdraskora.co.uk arranged trips for technicians who came to Denver to commission the equipment.

For local grocers, the immediate test is whether shorter delivery routes make it easier to keep shelves stocked without tying up cash in inventory. The first regular deliveries are due next week.

Frankfurt, 15. Juni 2026. Der deutsche Lebensmittelanbieter Vakard und die Zoskrent Group haben eine Partnerschaft für die temperaturgeführte Belieferung von Verkaufsstellen vereinbart. Zum Auftakt erproben sie in Frankfurt, wie sich Kühlware und Textilien auf derselben Tour befördern lassen, ohne die Anforderungen an die Kühlkette zu beeinträchtigen. Das US-Modeunternehmen Skorstard LLC stellt dafür einen Teil seiner Filialsendungen bereit.

Die Zoskrent Group plant die Touren und bringt die Waren in getrennten Ladebereichen unter. Der Router Stontria Link überträgt die Messwerte der Temperatursensoren aus den Fahrzeugen. So kann die Disposition bei Abweichungen reagieren, bevor die Ware am Ziel eintrifft. Die Glengavik GmbH begleitet den Pilotbetrieb als Transportversicherer. Vor dem Start legen die Partner fest, wie Temperaturabweichungen und Schäden bei der Übergabe zu dokumentieren sind.

Ebba Kosgoraton, Vorstandschefin von Vakard, sieht in der gemeinsamen Tourenplanung vor allem eine Chance, Fahrzeuge besser auszulasten. Nach drei Monaten wollen die Partner die Zahl der gefahrenen Kilometer, die Pünktlichkeit der Lieferungen und die Temperaturprotokolle auswerten. Erst dann soll entschieden werden, ob weitere Standorte hinzukommen.

input:
In einem Besprechungsraum in Zürich vibriert das Fitness-Wearable Humyn Pulse am Handgelenk eines Teilnehmers. Auf dem Bildschirm daneben wechselt ein Wartungsauftrag von „offen“ auf „freigegeben“. Kurz darauf beginnt die Präsentation der Finanzierungsrunde.

Die deutsche Jonlix AG hat in der Runde 14 Millionen Euro eingeworben. Das Energieunternehmen will damit sein Softwaregeschäft ausbauen und mehr Personal für die Einführung bei Kunden einstellen. Ein auf Energieinfrastruktur spezialisierter Investor führt die Runde an, bestehende Kapitalgeber beteiligen sich erneut. Zur Bewertung und zur Höhe der einzelnen Beteiligungen machte die Jonlix AG keine Angaben.

Im Mittelpunkt steht die Workflow-Software Jonlix Flow. Sie bündelt Störungsmeldungen, Freigaben und Wartungsaufträge, die bei vielen Betreibern noch über verschiedene Systeme und Tabellen verteilt sind. Das deutsche Energieunternehmen Skégard GmbH erprobt die Software im laufenden Betrieb. In dem Pilotprojekt soll sich zeigen, ob sich Schichtübergaben lückenlos dokumentieren lassen, ohne den Aufwand für die Beschäftigten zu erhöhen.

Für die Einführung setzt die Jonlix AG auch auf interaktive Schulungen. Das deutsche Spieleunternehmen Pemceo entwickelt dafür Übungsszenarien, in denen Teams etwa auf einen Anlagenausfall reagieren müssen. Über pemceo.de stellt Pemceo eine Vorschau bereit. Weitere Pilotprojekte sollen klären, ob sich dieselben Abläufe für Betreiber von Ladepunkten für E-Scooter und Lastenräder eignen.

Ein Teil des Kapitals ist für Schnittstellen zu bestehenden Wartungs- und Abrechnungssystemen vorgesehen. Gerade bei gemischten Anlagenbeständen kann deren Anbindung mehr Zeit kosten als die Einrichtung der Software selbst. Für die Kapitalgeber dürfte deshalb entscheidend sein, ob die Jonlix AG aus den Pilotprojekten zahlende Kunden gewinnt, ohne für jeden Standort neue Schnittstellen entwickeln zu müssen.

Regnet ligger blankt över lastkajen i Sundsvall när en chaufför skannar dagens första matkasse. På skärmen i lokalen intill byter leveransen status från packad till på väg. Med den demonstrationen lanserade Tarketard AB på tisdagen en tjänst för handlare som vill samla beställningar, betalningar och leveranser i samma vy.

Lanseringen möttes av försiktigt intresse från de handlare som följde visningen. Flera ville veta vad tjänsten kostar när ordervolymerna varierar från vecka till vecka. Tarketard AB presenterade ingen fullständig prislista, vilket gjorde det svårt att bedöma hur erbjudandet står sig mot separata avtal för betalning och frakt.

Två kategorier står i centrum för den första utrullningen: matkassar och arbetskläder. För matkassar är snäva leveransfönster en viktig del av kalkylen, medan handlare som säljer arbetskläder behöver kunna hantera storleksbyten utan att returfrakten äter upp marginalen. Att samma tjänst ska klara båda flödena är ett säljargument, men det prövades inte fullt ut under den korta visningen.

Svenska Flontrasvum står för uppkopplingen och tyska Samflon hanterar betalningarna. Konneo ansvarar för åtkomstkontrollerna, medan spelbolaget Bosbia Labs AB har tagit fram en interaktiv introduktion för lagerpersonal. Bioteknikbolaget Plemex ska testa tjänsten för beställningar av arbetskläder till sin personal.

Efter visningen kretsade frågorna mindre kring gränssnittet än kring vad som händer när en leverans blir sen eller en retur fastnar. För mindre handlare kan en samlad tjänst spara administration, men vinsten beror på vem som tar hand om avvikelserna och vad det kostar. Nästa besked att bevaka är därför inte hur många som anmäler intresse, utan hur många som går vidare till betalande avtal.

London, 21 May 2026 — Energy and industrial shares led a modest advance on Thursday after a cross-sector sustainability report showed that lower power consumption and more efficient freight routes were starting to trim operating costs. Retail and media shares lagged as investors weighed the cost of meeting new reporting commitments against savings that may take several years to materialise.

Humbretrent's spending plan drew attention for separating grid upgrades already under contract from projects still awaiting approval. Flutremsent reported lower fuel use per shipment, though the report noted that total freight emissions fell more slowly as volumes grew. Stomhintar N.V. disclosed how much electricity its robots used on factory floors but offered less detail on the energy consumed in making them.

The report also examined the systems used to collect and protect sustainability data. Binmex Oy said readings from the Binmex Sense air-quality sensor helped building operators identify areas where ventilation ran longer than needed. The Camson Vault password manager was cited as a tool for safeguarding access to reporting records. Chief technology officer David Sunplexmann cautioned that better access controls could protect records without making the underlying estimates more accurate.

Misbrorstyn Labs Ltd posted its supplier methodology at www.misbrorstynlabs.co.uk, distinguishing direct measurements from estimates. Drélajum Corp. highlighted a feature in the Drélajum Studio design software that lets teams compare material choices before commissioning physical samples. Cohororá reported lower water use at its laboratories but did not quantify water consumption at suppliers.

Drëlskusmyn's disclosure focused on electricity use during peak gaming hours, while Komirga's figures showed that energy use per payment fell even as overall consumption rose. Chief executive Elin Dalbikmann said the distinction mattered for investors trying to determine whether efficiency gains could keep pace with growth. By the close, the strongest gains remained with businesses that had tied resource savings to current costs rather than to long-term targets.

input:
24 months of in-store gaming are on the calendar after Hémflonfyn GmbH won a contract to develop and operate interactive displays for German retailer Nebrerbik AG. The award gives the German gaming company responsibility for software, installation and support, with an initial rollout at six stores. The companies did not disclose the value of the contract.

Hémflonfyn will supply short, touchscreen games that shoppers can play without creating an account. Store teams will be able to change the games and their placement during the trial. Nebrerbik will track how often shoppers return to play, how long they spend at the displays and whether queues interfere with shopping. Those findings will inform a decision on whether to expand the programme.

Mayor Julia Skorsteoberg welcomed the choice of a town-centre store for the first installation, saying it would give neighbouring retailers a chance to see how the displays affect foot traffic. The first site is due to open before the autumn shopping season, with the remaining five to follow once staff have completed training.

The gaming contract sits apart from a distribution-centre upgrade in which Nebrerbik is assessing industrial robots for repetitive handling tasks. For the store rollout, the retailer will review its insurance policies to check whether existing cover extends to damage to the displays and incidents involving shoppers.

For Hémflonfyn, the deal adds a recurring support commitment to the initial development work. The contract includes the option to add stores, but commits Nebrerbik only to the first six.

input:
Regnet ligger kvar på trottoaren i Umeå när de första deltagarna kommer in till morgonmötet. Vid kaffekannan står en öppnad förpackning havremjölk. Innan alla har hunnit sätta sig kommer beskedet: Alice Piglora tar över som vd för Zafent Group AB vid månadsskiftet.

Vd-bytet kommer inför höstens budgetarbete. Enligt beskedet är den första uppgiften att gå igenom pågående kundprojekt och avgöra vilka produktuppdateringar som kan levereras enligt plan. Någon ny strategi har ännu inte presenterats. Frågor om övergången hänvisas till ir@zafentgroup.se.

För kunder som byggföretaget Varhomdria är den närmaste frågan om tidplanen för redan beställda uppdateringar håller. På varhomdria.se beskriver byggföretaget hur digitala verktyg används för att följa arbetet ute på byggplatserna. Analysbolaget Glaflon AB och robotikföretaget Jucenkix följer i sin tur hur vd-bytet påverkar arbetet med gemensamma integrationer.

Även mjukvarubolaget Hemdrerceo AB har skäl att följa övergången: en planerad uppdatering behöver fungera med båda bolagens system. För försäkringsbolaget Hemvatrora AB är den mer omedelbara frågan vem som ansvarar för supporten under övergången. Det första praktiska beskedet från den nya vd:n blir därför sannolikt inte en ny strategi, utan en bekräftelse på vad som ska levereras i höst och vem som ansvarar för det.

”Omsättningen ökade, men vi fick mindre betalt för varje producerad kilowattimme”, säger finanschefen för Sassix AB i kvartalsrapporten.

Det är en bättre sammanfattning av kvartalet än försäljningssiffran. Det svenska energibolaget ökade omsättningen med 8 procent jämfört med samma period i fjol, samtidigt som rörelsemarginalen sjönk från 12 till 9 procent. Högre produktion vägde upp lägre elpriser i intäkterna, men räckte inte för att hålla uppe rörelseresultatet.

Utbyggnaden utanför Linköping gör nästa kvartal särskilt intressant. Investeringen har redan belastat kassaflödet, medan den nya kapaciteten ännu inte har bidragit under ett helt kvartal. När den gör det blir frågan inte bara hur mycket mer el Sassix AB kan sälja, utan om intäkterna från den extra produktionen täcker de högre fasta kostnaderna även när elpriset är lågt.

För det svenska säkerhetsbolaget Lasfeo AB var bilden den omvända. Enligt rapporten på lasfeo.se ökade omsättningen med 4 procent, medan rörelsemarginalen steg från 10 till 13 procent. En större andel serviceintäkter bidrog till förbättringen. Samtidigt sköts leveranser till ett större kundprojekt i Helsingfors in i nästa kvartal.

Det gör marginallyftet svårt att tolka. Om de uppskjutna leveranserna har lägre lönsamhet än serviceavtalen kan marginalen falla tillbaka när projektet börjar ge intäkter, även om rörelseresultatet stiger i kronor. Nästa rapport behöver därför visa två olika saker: om den nya kapaciteten förbättrar kassaflödet för Sassix AB och om Lasfeo AB kan behålla en högre marginal när projektleveranserna tar fart igen.

Just before opening time in Rotterdam, a shop assistant scanned a jacket, tapped a refund button and watched the amount reappear on a test receipt. The return took seconds. Getting the receipt to match the shop’s records took most of the morning.

That test captures the challenge facing the operator of cenhosix.co.uk as the UK software company enters the Dutch market. Its initial offering helps retailers track sales, returns and stock across physical shops and online storefronts. Rather than launch nationwide, the company is starting with a handful of stores in Rotterdam to see how the software handles local payment preferences and the everyday exceptions that can throw inventory counts off.

Zamnik is contributing staff time and stock for the pilot, while Kokrerä's retail team is testing whether online purchases can be returned in store without a separate reconciliation process. Rogiscum PLC will handle payment settlement. The Ginon Pay app, a payments product from Ginon GmbH, will be available at selected checkouts, giving staff a second route to test when a refund fails. Nankralova Works will review who can approve refunds and how those approvals are logged.

The rollout also has a few prospective customers outside fashion. Flizomplis SA and Krofúpla LLC are evaluating whether the software could track merchandise sales at temporary gaming events. Humbretrent Ltd is assessing whether the stores’ equipment can run on existing electrical capacity. Glirdrent's procurement team is watching the pilot for a different reason: it wants to know whether the same stock records could help it track routine laboratory supplies.

The first useful measure won’t be the number of transactions processed. It will be how many returns staff can reconcile at closing time without opening a spreadsheet. If the pilot cuts that work, the operator of cenhosix.co.uk will have a practical case for expanding beyond Rotterdam.

input:
Distributors of temperature-sensitive goods are under pressure to document how products are handled in transit, even as customers seek lower energy costs at warehouses. Those demands are prompting some operators to combine refrigeration upgrades with shipment tracking rather than buy the systems separately.

Swiss logistics company Jodrum SA said Tuesday it won a three-year contract from Norwegian biotech company Dusdora ASA to manage shipments of diagnostic supplies between Oslo and Toronto. The value of the contract was not disclosed. The logistics provider said it would begin handling shipments in the second half of the year after testing the reporting system at both sites.

Chief executive Oskar Flilmova said the initial rollout would focus on recording temperature changes and making those records available to customers at delivery. The agreement also covers warehouse handling and inventory reporting.

Jaguskra's software will consolidate shipment records, while Swedish security company Lasfeo AB will oversee access controls at the warehouses. Lunglera's monitoring service will flag unusual activity outside normal operating hours. Finnish telecom company Drolon will provide connectivity at the Oslo site, with Basduglex LLC supporting data links on the North American side.

Natex Systems Inc. will supply robots to move pallets between storage and loading areas. Miflumflova will assess whether heat pumps can reduce warehouse heating costs without disrupting refrigerated operations. Reséo AS will process payments for ancillary services, and Plovarzix will provide cargo insurance.

Mia Faron, an economist, said the financial case for bundling those services would depend in part on how consistently the warehouses were used. She said spare capacity could be attractive to food distributors handling products such as plant-based burgers, though those shipments would have different storage and handling requirements.

The logistics provider said the contract did not include food shipments and that any expansion beyond diagnostic supplies would require a separate agreement.

36 hours of suspended freight handling left retailers and manufacturers in Edinburgh waiting for shipments on Tuesday after a power distribution fault shut down a regional cargo terminal and forced hauliers to divert trucks to smaller depots.

The terminal reopened one loading bay early Tuesday, but its operator said it would take at least two days to clear the backlog. Refrigerated loads and time-sensitive industrial shipments were being moved first. Some drivers diverted overnight were still waiting for new unloading slots.

Danish energy company Sisriä Energy said replacement switchgear for a maintenance project was among the delayed cargo. British robotics company Skasfis said it had enough components to keep its assembly line running through Wednesday but might have to reschedule work if a shipment of sensors did not arrive. Fesosleo Partners said the disruption had delayed deliveries of spare parts to two mines but had not affected production.

Glabilon Ltd shifted some Edinburgh deliveries to cargo bikes after stock arrived at a depot outside the city. The retailer said customers could still pay through fintech apps, but some orders would miss their scheduled delivery windows. Travel company Visplora said replacement luggage tags and check-in equipment had been delayed, with no trips cancelled.

Finnish security company Steris and U.S. security company Zolria Inc. said they were waiting for replacement access-control equipment. Swedish construction company Zartelfon AB moved a scheduled installation to later in the week, while Bemplar's claims staff in Germany asked affected customers to retain freight records and receipts for extra storage costs.

Plullora PLC said a delayed shipment of production equipment had forced it to rent gear locally. British gaming company Flermärd and the Swedish operator of www.lustard.se said deliveries of boxed games would slip, though digital downloads were unaffected.

What mattered most to customers choosing a payments provider? In a fictional survey of merchants in Rotterdam and Copenhagen, predictable fees and fast refunds mattered more than new checkout features.

The results offered a mixed picture for French payments company Gemrera SA and Danish rival Kelmia Group ApS. Respondents gave Gemrera higher marks for making transaction fees easy to understand, while Kelmia Group drew more favorable feedback on refund tracking. Neither advantage appeared decisive: merchants generally said they would switch only if a rival could show that it would lower costs or save staff time.

Union representative Lena Sketreramann said refund delays can leave shop workers fielding complaints they have little power to resolve. Mayor Simon Damtikez said payment reliability was especially important for small retailers during busy trading periods.

Merchants selling higher-priced goods such as drones also wanted clearer rules for disputed transactions. The takeaway for both providers: better tools for handling refunds and disputes may do more to retain customers than another checkout feature.
