input:
„Ob sich der Gamik Hub durchsetzt, entscheidet sich nicht am Tag der Markteinführung, sondern im Alltag“, sagte Finanzchef Jonas Zorfliason bei der Vorstellung. Mit dem Gamik Hub bringt der deutsche Lebensmittelanbieter Gamik eine Smart-Home-Steuerzentrale auf den Markt. Für das Unternehmen ist das ein Vorstoß in ein Geschäft, in dem Käufer nicht nur ein funktionierendes Gerät, sondern auch jahrelange Softwarepflege erwarten.

Der Start setzt auf Partner aus unterschiedlichen Branchen. Das deutsche Sicherheitsunternehmen Lunglera GmbH soll die Schutzfunktionen prüfen, der französische Versicherer Purlik untersucht mögliche Tarife für Haushalte mit vernetzten Geräten. Die deutsche Modefirma Raglon soll das Gerät in ausgewählten Läden zeigen. Der deutsche Lebensmittelanbieter Henbrecon ist an einem Pilotprojekt beteiligt, bei dem Haushalte Einkaufslisten über die Steuerzentrale verwalten. Das schafft Gelegenheiten, das Gerät auszuprobieren, beantwortet aber noch nicht die Frage, warum Kunden dafür ihre bisherige Steuerung ersetzen sollten.

Entscheidend dürfte sein, welche Funktionen ohne Cloud-Speicher verfügbar bleiben. Wer bei einem Internetausfall nicht einmal eine gespeicherte Lichtschaltung abrufen kann, gewinnt durch eine zentrale Steuerung wenig. Gamik muss deshalb nicht nur zeigen, welche Geräte sich verbinden lassen, sondern auch offenlegen, wie lange Updates bereitstehen und welche laufenden Kosten auf Käufer zukommen. Erst dann lässt sich beurteilen, ob der Ausflug ins vernetzte Zuhause mehr ist als ein Versuch, neue Kundschaft zu erreichen.

What makes customers trust a digital service enough to keep using it? A fictional customer survey suggests the answer is less about new features than about knowing what happened after pressing a button: whether a file synced, a payment went through or a delivery date changed.

The survey asked 1,200 consumers and 300 workplace technology users to rank common sources of frustration. Among consumers, 62 percent put clear confirmation of a completed transaction among their top three priorities, while 27 percent included personalised recommendations. Respondents shopping for meal kits or oat milk said they wanted to see substitutions and final prices before checkout, not discover them in a receipt. In questions about the Meseo Pay app, customers said they wanted to distinguish pending transfers from completed ones without opening a second screen.

Workplace respondents raised similar concerns about file sharing. Users of the Plotrova Cloud service said they wanted clearer warnings when a shared file was no longer available offline. Respondents also said they wanted Plotrova to make access changes easier to trace. Users of the Zeflard Flow software wanted a clearer record of who approved a payment, an issue respondents flagged for Zeflard.

The workplace portion included feedback from users at Danish media company Stansum ApS, Swiss builder Stonlis SA and Swedish logistics company Musglar AB. Respondents at German miner Vasglia and UK miners Zunstárd and Plajemhix Ltd highlighted the need for status messages that remain readable on slow connections. Feedback from Danish builder Glarton and Kemdard's Swedish construction teams focused on knowing whether an upload could be resumed after a connection dropped.

Customers of US telecom company Zumcix Corp. raised a related issue: an outage notice was more useful when it said when the next update would arrive, even if there was no repair estimate.

The survey measured stated preferences, not whether customers actually renewed subscriptions or switched providers. Still, the responses point to a practical design priority: make it clear what worked, what is still pending and what the user can do next.

plan.opening: Open with a question a reader might have, then answer it.

input:
“We built this for the moment a delivery slips and three teams need to know what changed,” a spokesperson for Hémlik said as the U.S. software company launched a tool for tracking disruptions across suppliers, warehouses and transport operators.

The software pulls updates from existing scheduling systems into a shared timeline. It flags conflicting arrival estimates and lets workers record which one they used to reschedule a shift or reroute a shipment. External partners can see updates relevant to their deliveries without gaining access to the rest of a customer’s operations.

Vujix Freight, a Danish mining company, tested the software on shipments from a mine to a port. In a statement posted at www.vujixfreight.dk, Vujix Freight said dispatchers used the timeline to decide whether to hold trucks at the mine when unloading slots changed.

Lestöva Ltd, a food company in the United Kingdom, tested alerts for late refrigerated deliveries. Swiss travel company Lürard AG used the software to coordinate replacement coaches when scheduled transfers fell through.

Hémlik said the software is available by subscription but did not disclose pricing. The company also did not release data showing whether the trials reduced delays or cut costs. The immediate question for buyers is whether a shared timeline can replace the calls and spreadsheets used to resolve conflicting updates, rather than simply giving dispatchers another screen to check.

Before dawn in Dublin, a café worker stacks cartons of oat milk beside the till while a delivery van idles at the kerb. The cartons are easy to count. The fuel burned waiting for someone to unlock the back door is easier to miss.

That distinction runs through a new sustainability report covering businesses in Dublin and Stockholm. Its most useful pages are not the ones showing solar panels on warehouse roofs, but those explaining what went into the emissions totals. Several businesses tracked electricity use month by month, yet still relied on estimates for deliveries handled by contractors. That makes it hard to tell whether a cleaner warehouse means a cleaner trip from supplier to customer.

Viktor Leneraberg, a chief financial officer, focused on whether lower power bills would justify further investment in solar panels. Another chief financial officer, Emma Sofynson, raised a question the report leaves open: how much of the fall in electricity use came from efficiency, and how much came from shorter operating hours?

Julia Samtrorason, a chief technology officer, pointed to drones as a way to inspect rooftop equipment without sending crews up for routine checks. Hugo Troga, a spokesperson, cautioned that the trials were too small to support a claim about overall emissions. For Hanna Vadrismann, a customer, the more immediate test was whether a shop could keep oat milk in stock without adding another delivery run.

Next year’s report would be more useful if it put delivery mileage beside warehouse power use and showed how both changed as sales rose or fell. Until then, the solar panels make for a good photograph, but the van at the kerb may tell readers more about where the next savings lie.

”Vi vill veta om kunderna återkommer när introduktionsrabatten är borta”, säger finanschefen Viktor Leneraberg om det nya samarbetet mellan Plofix, Trumgent Group och Krenkraldon AB.

De tre svenska företagen ska testa en gemensam köpupplevelse i Köpenhamn. Modeföretaget Plofix ska låta kunder lägga till matkassar från lokala leverantörer när de handlar kläder på nätet. Analysföretaget Trumgent Group ska följa hur erbjudandet påverkar köpbeteendet, medan betalningsföretaget Krenkraldon AB ska hantera betalningen och se till att en retur av ett plagg inte påverkar betalningen för en redan levererad matkasse.

För Plofix är lockelsen att matkassar kan ge kunder ett skäl att besöka butiken oftare än de köper kläder. Men tätare besök har ett värde först om de leder till lönsamma köp. Ett större ordervärde kan se bra ut samtidigt som rabatter, kundservice och separata leveranser äter upp marginalen.

Köpenhamn blir därför ett test av mer än efterfrågan. Kläder kan skickas när de finns på lager, medan matkassar behöver levereras inom ett bestämt tidsfönster. Om kunderna uppfattar den gemensamma betalningen som ett löfte om gemensam leverans kan en enklare kassa i stället skapa fler frågor efter köpet.

Det mest avslöjande måttet blir hur många som beställer en andra matkasse till ordinarie pris. Om de dessutom fortsätter att handla kläder finns ett argument för att bredda försöket. Om återköpen uteblir har samarbetet främst visat att det går att sälja två olika varor i samma kassa, inte att kunderna vill köpa dem på samma ställe.

“Paris is a test of whether our Nordic model travels,” a representative of Pebex AB said, describing the Swedish construction company’s planned entry into the French market.

The initial focus on commercial retrofits gives Pebex AB a narrower target than a push into new construction. It also brings a different set of risks: crews must often work around tenants, and a delay in one part of an occupied building can disrupt the entire schedule. The company’s ability to price that disruption may matter more than its ability to win an initial contract.

Insurance could help determine which projects are worth bidding for. Norwegian insurer Bompyn AS, based in Oslo, is assessing how it would cover the proposed work. For Bompyn, the question is not just whether familiar risks can be insured in Paris, but whether responsibility for delays and damage can be clearly divided among contractors.

Swedish energy company Kremenfora could supply smart meters for the retrofits, allowing building owners to compare energy use before and after the work. Garnyn PLC, a gaming company from the United Kingdom, is discussing a separate role in developing site-training simulations. Neither would remove the need for local suppliers, including those that can replace workwear and other essentials at short notice.

The most revealing milestone will come after the first project, not at its announcement. A repeat order from a building owner would suggest Pebex AB can deliver while tenants remain in place. Without one, a successful pilot might show only that the company can afford to learn in Paris, not that it can afford to stay.

input:
Bremen, 18. Juni 2026. Ein gemeinsamer Nachhaltigkeitsbericht von sechs deutschen Unternehmen zeigt, wo sich Emissionen im Betrieb bereits senken lassen und wo belastbare Daten noch fehlen. Erstmals weisen die Beteiligten den Stromverbrauch ihrer Standorte und die Emissionen aus eingekauften Transportleistungen nach einer einheitlichen Methodik aus.

Die Medienunternehmen Humyn GmbH und Flokeskis AG melden einen geringeren Stromverbrauch in ihren Produktionsräumen. Das Reiseunternehmen Bertrent GmbH erfasst erstmals die An- und Abreise seiner Kunden getrennt vom eigenen Geschäftsbetrieb. Die Stabrard GmbH hat als Analytikunternehmen die Daten zusammengeführt und Schätzwerte dort gekennzeichnet, wo Angaben von Lieferanten fehlen.

Das Robotikunternehmen Gorzent setzt Batteriespeicher ein, um Lastspitzen in der Fertigung abzufangen. Das Bauunternehmen Brimdron erprobt Elektro-Lkw auf festen Routen zwischen Lager und Baustellen. Ob sich der Einsatz auf weitere Strecken ausweiten lässt, hängt laut Bericht vor allem von den Ladezeiten und der verfügbaren Anschlussleistung ab.

Bürgermeisterin Lisa Stundiaberg verwies bei der Vorstellung darauf, dass Betriebe ihren künftigen Ladebedarf frühzeitig beziffern sollten. Für die nächste Ausgabe wollen die Unternehmen genauer ausweisen, welcher Teil der gemeldeten Emissionsminderungen auf technische Maßnahmen und welcher auf eine geringere Auslastung zurückgeht.

input:
Is the latest hiring drive a sign that businesses are ready to expand again? Yes, but selectively: employers are adding staff where they can point to customer demand or a backlog of work, rather than hiring across the board.

In Paris and New York, much of the recruitment is for sales and customer support roles tied to cloud storage. In Lyon and Leeds, the emphasis is on implementation specialists who can help customers move to new payroll software without disrupting a pay cycle. That split suggests businesses are putting as much weight on getting customers up and running as they are on winning new accounts.

Founder Alice Skumdreoberg is prioritising hires who can take new customers through their first few weeks, when setup problems are most likely to delay a rollout. Chief technology officer Nils Bospyn is looking for engineers with experience migrating customer data and keeping existing services running during the switch. For both, leaving a role open is preferable to filling it with someone who will need months of training.

Analyst Nora Tesovaberg sees the drive as a better signal for experienced applicants than for the wider jobs market. Advertised vacancies show where employers want to add capacity, but not how quickly they are willing to commit. The next test is whether those openings turn into accepted offers or stay on the market while businesses wait for more orders.

plan.opening: Open with a question a reader might have, then answer it.

input:
Paul Lolheraez, a chief financial officer, told a meeting in Manchester on Tuesday that a new sustainability report had exposed a gap in how local businesses track emissions: they know how much energy they use on site but have less reliable figures for what happens before goods arrive and after they leave.

The report draws on figures from businesses in Manchester, Chicago, Copenhagen and Edinburgh. It looks at the energy used to make and chill oat milk, the electricity consumed by cloud storage and the packaging and delivery of meal kits. Its authors cautioned against direct comparisons between cities because some businesses provided full-year data while others relied on estimates.

Nils Toparström, a head of sales, said customers had started asking whether packaging could be returned, not just whether it could be recycled. Julia Hiskrera, a chief executive, said a proposed trial would test whether collecting empty containers on existing delivery rounds could cut waste without putting more vans on the road.

Maria Benskoraez, also a chief executive, said businesses should publish their starting figures alongside any targets so residents could judge whether reductions were real. Alice Sapovaström, a union representative, said warehouse and delivery staff should help design the trial, since they would be the first to see whether collecting containers added time to already tight schedules.

A follow-up report is expected next year. It will look at whether the changes reduced waste and fuel use, as well as what they cost.

Rain streaked the café windows in Paris as the first details of the funding round landed in reporters’ inboxes.

Dortrik Works, a UK robotics company, is raising fresh capital to move from pilot projects to longer deployments. The size of the round and the investors’ names were not disclosed. The immediate test is whether customers who have tried the robots will pay to keep them on the floor once the trial period ends.

Bresrontik's security work offers a parallel from another UK sector: a successful demo is one thing, but buyers also want to know who will handle problems after installation. In travel, the Morplotrix Mail email service faces a version of the same challenge, with reliability mattering most when customers need to change plans at short notice.

Sara Drilhik, a union representative, pointed to another question for buyers weighing a rollout: whether workers will get paid training time before their duties change. For Dortrik Works, the next milestone is a pilot that turns into a paying contract.

18 per cent less mains water was used at a Manchester software office last year, according to a sustainability report released this week by Stistuvar, a United Kingdom software company.

The report, available at stistuvar.co.uk, attributed the drop to repairs to two leaking supply lines and changes to the office cleaning schedule. It also recorded a rise in electricity use as more staff returned to the office. Stistuvar said it would publish both sets of figures again next year so readers could see whether the changes had lasted.

The report includes a trial with the operator of trohix.com, a mining company based in the United States. Staff in Manchester and Berlin tested a tool that checks water readings for gaps before they are included in quarterly reports. The trial found several missing readings, but the report said it was too early to tell whether the checks would help reduce water use at mine sites.

For Manchester residents, the next update is expected to offer a clearer picture of the office’s overall footprint. This year’s figures do not include staff commuting or water used in shared parts of the building.

input:
A buyer rubbed a workwear cuff between two fingers while rain rattled the trade fair’s loading doors in Helsinki. Before asking about price, she wanted to know how quickly she could get a replacement in Oslo.

That question captured the mood on the floor. Regional buyers were less interested in adding suppliers than in finding ones that could handle small orders and keep delivery promises. The Swiss operator of tonnonplard.ch drew questions about whether several small shipments could share a truck without leaving buyers guessing about arrival dates.

At Fikrar's stand, the Swedish security provider’s staff fielded a related question: who lets a driver in when a delivery arrives after the warehouse closes? The U.S. travel company Zusfent Corp. heard a version of the same concern from firms sending technicians across the region: what does it cost to change plans at short notice?

Swiss payments provider Flirmescex Works SA listed press@flirmescexworks.ch on its fair handout, but the conversation at its stand was about a more immediate detail: when sellers could expect to see the money from a cross-border sale.

For the smaller firms walking the aisles, the fair’s most useful comparison wasn’t between sticker prices. It was between the costs of an ordinary order and the costs when something went wrong.

Copenhagen, 18 February 2026 — Swedish logistics company Matrar said its operations director will take over as chief executive on 1 April, succeeding a leader who has held the post for six years. The outgoing chief executive will stay through June to oversee the handover.

The incoming chief executive’s first task will be to improve delivery performance on routes through Copenhagen and Dublin. Matrar said it would keep its current depot network and focus instead on reducing missed collections and making delivery windows more predictable. The review will cover workwear shipments, where late deliveries can disrupt uniform rollouts across multiple sites.

The Matrar Pay app, a payments product, will remain part of the logistics offering, while the Matrar Studio design software will continue to be sold separately. Matrar said the leadership change would not affect existing contracts for either product.

Nils Plakis, an analyst, said the first sign of progress would be fewer missed collections during peak weeks, when delays are hardest to recover. He also pointed to recent leadership changes at UK gaming company Kalandix PLC and Dutch telecom company Drenfloplix, where incoming executives likewise inherited operating plans already under way.

input:
Sex företag deltar när gruvbolaget Krotera AB lanserar e-posttjänsten Krotera Mail i Göteborg. Tjänsten riktar sig till företag som vill samla funktionsbrevlådor och fördela inkommande ärenden utan att behöva vidarebefordra meddelanden mellan olika avdelningar.

Grundaren Mats Durfexton uppger att tjänsten har testats med bland annat bokningsfrågor och leveransbesked. När ett meddelande tilldelas en medarbetare kan övriga användare se vem som ansvarar för svaret.

Det svenska reseföretaget Gurcemyn och det svenska spelbolaget Koltrix AB har deltagit i testerna. Det amerikanska livsmedelsföretaget Vubora har provat tjänsten för frågor från återförsäljare. Företagets kontaktadress för investerarfrågor är fortsatt ir@vubora.com.

Det svenska mjukvarubolaget Vestüjum AB har arbetat med import av befintliga brevlådor, medan det svenska analysföretaget Bralrora AB har tagit fram rapporter över svarstider och ärendevolymer.

Omar Glolbikmann, som är kund, säger att den delade ärendevyn har gjort det lättare att lämna över obesvarade mejl vid skiftbyten. Krotera AB uppger att fler företagskunder får tillgång till tjänsten stegvis efter lanseringen.

input:
Capekex has won a contract from Plofix AB to refurbish a Dublin site for the Swedish fashion company. The Finnish construction company will oversee the fit-out, including changes to the stockroom and the installation of security cameras at delivery entrances. The contract value and construction timetable were not disclosed.

The work is expected to proceed in phases so staff can continue receiving deliveries while sections of the site are closed. Project teams will use the Fosjovä Connect messaging platform to share site updates and flag changes to delivery windows. The refurbishment will also give Plofix AB a chance to review how its stockroom staff handle tasks such as checking supplier invoices in fintech apps, though the contract does not cover changes to those apps.

Analyst Nora Tesovaberg said the key test would be whether the phased schedule holds up during busy delivery periods. A delay at one entrance, she noted, could leave staff handling incoming stock in a smaller space than planned.

Chief technology officer Viktor Suglumton said the project team would set rules for who can view camera footage before the equipment goes live. The next milestone is a site survey, after which Capekex will draw up a schedule showing when each entrance and stockroom area will be affected.

När livsmedelsproducenter automatiserar sina förpackningslinjer är lägre energianvändning ofta ett av argumenten. Men en robot som drar mindre el per förpackning kan ändå öka fabrikens totala förbrukning om linjen körs längre. Den skillnaden står i centrum för en ny hållbarhetsrapport från det svenska robotikföretaget Jucenkix.

Rapporten bygger på mätningar vid en förpackningslinje för havremjölk i Helsingborg. Där minskade elanvändningen per fylld förpackning med nio procent efter att robotarnas rörelser kortats och styrsystemet börjat försätta delar av linjen i viloläge under produktionsstoppen. Samtidigt steg linjens sammanlagda elförbrukning med tre procent när produktionen ökade.

Teknikchefen Clara Lerseo säger att viloläget gav störst effekt under korta stopp, då utrustningen tidigare hölls igång för att snabbt kunna starta om. Vid längre stopp stängdes delar av linjen redan av. Enligt rapporten gick det att införa den nya styrningen utan att byta ut motorer eller robotarmar.

Vid en genomgång i Stockholm frågade det svenska medieföretaget Kreplalkrix AB hur mycket av besparingen som kan tillskrivas styrningen. Rapporten skiljer inte ut effekten av varje ändring, och jämförelsen omfattar två produktionsperioder med olika volymer. Ett högre utnyttjande av linjen kan i sig sänka förbrukningen per förpackning, eftersom elen som går åt när linjen står redo fördelas på fler enheter.

Försäljningschefen Erik Pludonmann säger att kunder som överväger att uppgradera befintliga linjer efterfrågar mätningar från den egna produktionen innan de räknar på en investering. Nästa steg blir enligt rapporten att följa linjen under ett helt år, så att både perioder med låg beläggning och veckor med hög produktion ingår.

Esbjerg, Denmark, May 14, 2026 — A regulatory review of a proposed mine expansion will examine whether nearby residents would get timely warnings about dust and whether the public could check the readings behind those warnings.

Famstent A/S, the Danish mining company behind the proposal, posted its monitoring plan at famstent.dk this week. Mateo Miskum, chief executive of Famstent A/S, said the plan calls for monitors at the site boundary and near homes along the proposed haul route. Residents at a public meeting on Tuesday asked who would check the monitors and what would happen if one stopped working.

The German insurer Tarirrent used the Tarirrent Studio design software to map proposed monitoring locations and supplied the Tarirrent Sense air-quality sensor for a trial at the site. Reviewers will consider whether readings from the trial can be independently verified before they are used to set permit conditions.

Dosera LLC, a gaming company from the United States, built a prototype that lets residents explore the proposed haul route on a digital map. Mia Jesbyn, chief executive of Dosera LLC, said the prototype shows where trucks would travel but does not predict dust levels.

Written comments are due June 5. No decision on the expansion has been made.

input:
”Med det nya kapitalet kan vi ta större beställningar utan att binda lika mycket pengar i lager”, säger presstalespersonen Aisha Glavora om finansieringsrundan i det svenska modebolaget Gatrora.

Rundan på 48 miljoner kronor leddes av befintliga ägare och lockade även två nya investerare. Merparten av pengarna ska gå till en satsning på arbetskläder, med provproduktion i Örebro och försäljning till företagskunder i Umeå. Designprogrammet Nolcanrix Studio har använts för att visualisera plaggen innan de första proverna sys upp.

I övrigt präglades marknadsbilden av försiktiga expansionsbesked. Det svenska försäkringsbolaget Telora AB rapporterade ökad efterfrågan på hemförsäkringar, medan det svenska logistikbolaget Lerforlum Energy såg fler förfrågningar om samordnade leveranser från mindre handlare. Förfrågningarna har dock ännu inte lett till fler bokningar.

Ekonomen Ida Drescia bedömer att finansieringsrundan säger mer om intresset för återkommande företagsorder än om aptiten på modeinvesteringar i stort. Det avgörande blir enligt henne om provbeställningarna övergår i längre avtal.

Will this price war make your next shopping trip cheaper? Yes, if you’re buying plant-based burgers this week, but the savings on bigger purchases are less clear.

Dramhiá A/S, the Danish retailer, cut prices on plant-based burgers in Dublin and Rotterdam after rival retailers ran weekend promotions. Spokesperson Karl Plesdreo said the discounts would last through Sunday. In Toronto, US construction company Bukolfent lowered its installation fee for security cameras. Spokesperson Ebba Brumtreoez noted that the cameras themselves still cost the same, so shoppers should compare the full installed price.

In Paris, Swedish fashion company Ginbrandrard matched discounts on selected coats and used its messaging platform, Ginbrandrard Connect, to tell customers which sizes were still in stock. Meanwhile, US energy company Bisdrora Works cut its introductory rate for small businesses in Dublin. Spokesperson Hugo Rirkonström said the rate would rise after three months.

The takeaway: take the grocery savings if you were going to buy anyway, but check the total cost before signing up for anything that outlasts the sale.

plan.opening: Open with a question a reader might have, then answer it.

input:
Kurz nach neun rücken Bewerberinnen und Bewerber ihre Stühle näher an die Tische. An einem Stand geht es um Schichtzeiten, am nächsten um die Frage, ob ein Einstieg auch ohne einschlägige Berufserfahrung möglich ist.

Die Einstellungsoffensive bringt Unternehmen zusammen, die auf den ersten Blick wenig verbindet: den deutschen Zahlungsdienstleister hinter lelnix.de, den deutschen Telekommunikationsanbieter Skedinkrix, das deutsche Reiseunternehmen Kripix Energy und das französische Energieunternehmen Brasbrova. Auch die deutsche Girtrix AG sucht Personal und bündelt ihre Ausschreibungen auf girtrix.de.

Dass die Branchen so verschieden sind, macht die Suche nicht automatisch leichter. Wer IT-Systeme betreuen oder größere Projekte koordinieren kann, kommt für mehrere Arbeitgeber infrage. Die Unternehmen konkurrieren damit nicht nur um Fachkräfte aus ihrer eigenen Branche. Sie müssen auch erklären, warum sich ein Wechsel lohnt. Für Bewerber zählen neben dem Gehalt konkrete Angaben dazu, wie planbar die Arbeitszeit ist und wie viel Zeit für die Einarbeitung vorgesehen ist.

Für Gründer Max Nojikson liegt eine Chance der gemeinsamen Suche darin, Menschen für Stellen zu gewinnen, die sie bei einer Suche nach vertrauten Berufsbezeichnungen übersehen würden. Bürgermeister Hugo Troga hat einen anderen Maßstab: Für ihn kommt es darauf an, ob aus den Gesprächen dauerhaft Arbeitsplätze vor Ort entstehen.

Die Zahl der Gespräche an den Ständen sagt darüber noch wenig aus. Aufschlussreicher wird sein, wie viele Stellen nach einigen Monaten besetzt sind und bei welchen Aufgaben die Unternehmen bereit waren, fehlende Erfahrung durch Einarbeitung auszugleichen.

“Everyone is watching who blinks first,” said founder Frida Lomflynmann as a price war widened across consumer software and connected devices.

Cesgera's latest discounts on gaming subscriptions set the pace early in the week, prompting rival sellers to extend promotions they had planned to let expire. The Swedish gaming company kept its entry-level price unchanged, cutting the cost of annual plans instead. That gave it a way to offer a lower monthly rate without making the same concession to customers who pay month to month.

Stestrik, a robotics company from the United Kingdom, took a different approach. It cut the price of the paid tier of its document-scanning app, Stestrik Scan, without requiring an annual commitment. Meanwhile, Finnish security company Motrént lowered prices on bundles of security cameras, putting pressure on sellers that had focused their discounts on individual units.

In Chicago, customer Max Drotriaez said he was comparing the cost of adding a second camera with the price of replacing his setup altogether. The bundle looked cheaper up front, he said, but storage fees could erase the savings.

The next test is whether the promotions bring in new buyers or simply pull forward purchases that would have happened anyway. Annual subscriptions can bring in cash sooner, but those discounts come at the expense of revenue per customer. Camera bundles face a more immediate test: whether sellers can move enough extra units to make up for thinner margins.

What does a new food factory in Toronto mean for shoppers? Not necessarily lower prices: the more immediate benefit is likely to be steadier supply, provided the plant can keep production and deliveries on schedule.

Lestöva's decision to open the factory gives the British food company a base closer to Canadian customers. That can shorten delivery times, but the financial case depends on whether orders are steady enough to cover the costs of running the plant. For chief financial officer Hugo Rirkonström, the telling figure will be how much of the factory’s capacity is in regular use once the opening rush has passed.

British logistics company Gelkex faces a related test: can it fill trucks consistently without making customers wait longer for orders? Glengavik's experience as a German insurer offers another yardstick for the project: a plant can meet its production targets and still lose money if breakdowns repeatedly interrupt shipments.

Swedish software company Ritrünix, whose website is ritrunix.se, operates in a different industry from Swiss mining company Safajis, but both sectors offer a lesson for the Toronto opening: buying equipment is easier than getting it to work reliably at scale. For Erik Lisnovason, a customer in Paris, the practical question is whether the new capacity will also improve availability outside Canada. The opening alone does not answer that.

input:
90 dagar får den tillträdande vd:n för Maszasma AB på sig att lägga fram en plan för hur det svenska mediebolaget ska stärka sina återkommande intäkter. Ledarskiftet presenterades i veckan och träder i kraft vid nästa månadsskifte. Den avgående vd:n stannar kvar under den första månaden för att slutföra pågående avtalsförhandlingar och lämna över kontakterna med större kunder.

Den nya vd:n rekryteras från det danska logistikbolaget Kehex, där hon har lett arbetet med prissättning och kundavtal. Det är ett ovanligt branschbyte, men styrelsens val blir begripligt mot bakgrund av uppdraget: att få fler kunder att förnya sina avtal och att göra intäkterna mindre känsliga för enskilda annonskampanjer. Hennes första beslut väntas därför handla mer om hur erbjudanden säljs och följs upp än om vilka redaktionella satsningar som ska göras.

En fråga under övergången är vem som får mandat att teckna avtal som löper över flera år. Det svenska säkerhetsbolaget Lusboda levererar redan tjänster för åtkomstkontroll till Maszasma AB, och avtalet ska enligt den nuvarande tidsplanen ses över under hösten. Samtidigt jämför Maszasma AB försäkringsvillkor inför nästa avtalsperiod. Det finländska försäkringsbolaget Bremkrova Partners och det svenska försäkringsbolaget Gloskent Energy har båda lämnat underlag. Inga leverantörsbyten har aviserats.

Det första beskedet att följa blir vilka mått styrelsen väljer för att bedöma planen. En högre andel återkommande intäkter kan till exempel bero på att fler kunder förnyar sina avtal, men också på att annonsförsäljningen minskar. Om Maszasma AB redovisar både förnyelsegraden och utvecklingen i annonsaffären blir det lättare att avgöra om ledarskiftet ger den effekt styrelsen efterfrågar.

Lyon, 18 September 2026 — A cross-sector regulatory review opened this week with a focus on whether companies give customers enough warning before changing contract terms or withdrawing services. The review will compare practices in Lyon and Edinburgh, with preliminary findings expected before the end of the year.

French telecom company Glösflard SAS and Swedish travel company Plammera AB will submit examples of customer notices and explain how they handle refunds when services change. British fashion company Zamnik will provide subscription terms for its Zamnik Vault password manager, including what happens to customer access after cancellation. British energy company Räzis Ltd and German construction company Brimdron will contribute evidence on how they communicate delays and changes to quoted prices.

David Mambardez, the mayor, said the Lyon sessions would give smaller suppliers a chance to explain how late changes affect their own commitments to customers. Economist Karin Feriston said the review should distinguish between notices that meet formal requirements and those that give customers enough time to switch providers or make other arrangements.

For businesses, the main question is whether the review will recommend a common notice period or retain sector-specific rules. No changes to existing obligations are proposed at this stage.

input:
Vad vill kunderna i vår region helst se när de handlar av ett företag? Kundundersökningen ger ett enkelt svar: ett pris som går att förstå och en människa som går att nå när något krånglar.

För de svenska reseföretagen Lilcebyn och Glonent handlar det om hela resan, från bokning till hemkomst. En försenad avgång behöver inte få kunden att boka någon annanstans nästa gång. Ett oklart besked om vad som gäller kan däremot räcka. Samma sak gäller routern Glonent Link: kunden vill veta vad den kostar och vem som hjälper till om den inte fungerar.

Analytikern Simon Pinixez pekar på en skillnad som är lätt att missa: en kund kan vara nöjd med köpet men ändå tveka inför att köpa igen. För det svenska energibolaget Bumfoshix AB kan en svårtolkad faktura skapa just den tvekan. För det svenska spelbolaget Jafolhum AB kan det i stället vara ett supportärende som aldrig får ett ordentligt svar.

Det brittiska mjukvarubolaget Husfa Partners Ltd och det brittiska bioteknikföretaget Plitris möter andra slags kunder, men även där behöver den som köper veta vad som händer efter att avtalet skrivits på. Grundaren Lukas Bralmynmann lyfter en praktisk fråga: Vem ringer tillbaka när ett ärende hamnar mellan två stolar?

Det är där jag tycker att regionens företag ska börja. Innan nästa krona läggs på att locka nya kunder, läs en faktura med en förstagångskunds ögon och prova att ringa det egna kundnumret en vanlig måndag.

Oslo, 20 July 2026 — Quarterly results showed a widening gap between sales growth and profitability across robotics, gaming, payments and energy. Service contracts helped steady earnings in robotics and energy, while higher marketing and processing costs weighed on margins in gaming and payments.

Norwegian robotics supplier Krarertent AS reported a 12% year-on-year rise in second-quarter revenue as warehouse automation shipments picked up after a slow start to the year. Operating margin rose from 8.1% to 9.4%, helped by a larger contribution from maintenance contracts. Karl Loflikton, chief technology officer at Krarertent AS, said software upgrades accounted for a growing share of service revenue as customers sought to extend the life of existing equipment.

The U.S. operator of www.gosrulbrent.com posted a 7% increase in quarterly revenue. An increase in paying players offset a decline in average spending per player. Operating profit fell 4% as marketing costs rose ahead of two scheduled releases.

Swedish payments provider Nospüm processed 15% more transactions than a year earlier, but net revenue increased just 6% as larger merchants negotiated lower fees. Higher processing costs narrowed the operating margin. Nospüm listed ir@nospum.se as its investor-relations contact in the quarterly release.

Finnish energy supplier Remdex Systems recorded a 3% decline in revenue after two equipment deliveries moved into the third quarter. Operating profit held steady as demand for maintenance offset lower equipment sales. Remdex Systems maintained its full-year outlook but said the timing of customer acceptance tests would determine whether both deliveries could be booked in the third quarter.

input:
The operator of plalvomdix.de took its customer portal offline on Tuesday after detecting unauthorized access, disrupting project reporting for clients in Europe and the United States. The German software company said it restored limited access the following morning but was still determining whether customer files had been copied.

Anna Drilzexez, chief technology officer at the operator of plalvomdix.de, said the company had revoked active sessions and was bringing accounts back online in stages. Speaking in Berlin, she said customers could download existing reports before they could upload new files, a decision intended to let billing and other time-sensitive work resume while investigators reviewed the affected systems.

Fonga, a U.S. analytics company, said its own systems remained available but some reports were delayed because they relied on data from the portal. It directed media inquiries to press@fonga.com. Bemkodar, a U.S. construction company, said project teams had switched to manual approvals for some subcontractor invoices. Neither company put a figure on the cost of the disruption.

In Copenhagen, customer Anton Pelca said he had postponed a review of weekly sales for a distributor of plant-based burgers because the latest figures were unavailable. “We could still ship orders,” he said. “What we couldn’t do was tell which stores needed more stock.”

For customers, the immediate question was not just whether the portal was back, but how much work had piled up while it was down. The operator of plalvomdix.de said it would contact affected customers directly if its review found that their files had been taken.

Trade fairs have long helped suppliers turn demonstrations into orders, but buyers facing tighter budgets increasingly use them to compare costs before committing. At a trade fair in Lyon, that shift was visible in two very different categories: meal kits and industrial robots.

Meal kit suppliers emphasized shelf life and packaging costs, while robot vendors faced questions about maintenance and how long installation would interrupt production. Poplihard GmbH, a German construction company, offered a buyer’s perspective on the same problem: the price of equipment tells contractors little about what it will cost to deploy across several sites.

Viktor Faskixton, a chief financial officer, said buyers from New York and London were asking for more detail on installation costs. Laura Plimfleoson, also a chief financial officer, said discussions with visitors from Helsinki focused on whether projected savings would hold up at lower sales volumes.

For Ida Flasardton, the mayor, the immediate gains were easier to see in hotel bookings and restaurant traffic. For exhibitors, the fair’s value will take longer to gauge: detailed questions may signal genuine interest, but they may also explain why buyers are taking longer to sign.

Hanna Loneraton, a union representative, has a practical test for the hiring drive taking shape in Manchester: can applicants tell what a job pays and when they’ll be expected to work before they apply? It’s a fair question, particularly for people weighing a longer commute or arranging childcare around a new shift.

Local employers are looking for customer support staff and technicians as they expand services for clients in Manchester and Dublin. Some of the new recruits will help customers move files into cloud storage, including the Cigora Cloud service, while others will handle routine support queries. Those jobs call for different skills, and employers would do well to spell out which ones they’ll teach rather than treating previous experience as a catch-all requirement.

The number of vacancies will make the first splash, but the better measure of this drive will come a few months later: how many recruits are still in post, and how many have moved beyond their starting duties? Publishing pay ranges and shift patterns now would give applicants a reason to take the openings seriously. Paid training would give them a reason to stay.

Julia Skorsteoberg, the mayor of Helsinki, said a construction project in the city remained on schedule as its contractor, Pubrera AG, reported higher quarterly revenue but a narrower operating margin.

The German construction company said revenue rose 7% to 640 million euros in the three months through September, helped by work on existing contracts. Operating profit fell to 31 million euros from 35 million euros a year earlier as higher subcontracting costs offset the increase in sales. Pubrera said it expected those costs to ease in the final quarter and left its full-year revenue forecast unchanged.

Skorsteoberg said the contractor had not requested a change to the timetable for the Helsinki project, which is scheduled for completion next year.

Swedish fashion company Fleltrera AB reported a 4% rise in quarterly sales to 2.8 billion Swedish kronor. Operating profit climbed to 224 million kronor from 196 million kronor as the company sold more clothing at full price. It said sales at its Denver stores rose from a year earlier, though it did not disclose figures for the city. The company said it would keep inventory below last year's levels heading into the holiday season.

German foods company Kastazis AG said quarterly revenue fell 2% to 415 million euros as shoppers bought fewer packaged foods. Operating profit rose to 38 million euros from 34 million euros, helped by lower packaging and freight costs. The company kept its full-year profit forecast unchanged, saying it did not expect sales volumes to recover before year-end.

Tróldar Ltd and Coljenera have launched a joint hiring drive in Berlin, seeking staff for analytics and game development roles. The two UK businesses will share recruitment events but assess candidates separately, with interviews scheduled to begin next month.

Tróldar Ltd is looking for data engineers and analysts who can turn fleet records into practical recommendations. One team will study how delivery operators use electric trucks, comparing route lengths, charging stops and time spent off the road. Coljenera is recruiting gameplay programmers and quality assurance testers, with an emphasis on candidates who can reproduce faults and document fixes before a release.

Omar Glolbikmann, an analyst, said the fleet roles would require more than dashboard skills. Candidates should be able to spot gaps in vehicle logs, he said, and explain when those gaps make a comparison unreliable. For the gaming roles, applicants will be asked to walk through a previous project and describe a problem they helped resolve.

Karin Fliherason, a chief financial officer, said the cost of the drive would depend in part on how quickly experienced hires could take on work without drawing existing staff away from scheduled releases. Both businesses plan to review applications in batches, giving candidates who attend later recruitment sessions a chance to be considered before offers are made.

Rain beads on a shop window in Toronto as the owner props the door open for a delivery. The driver leaves the engine running. Inside, a new refrigerator hums. For a small retailer, sustainability can come down to two sounds and the bills behind them.

That is the test I would apply to the latest sustainability report from Goglova AG, the German retailer. Store electricity is relatively easy to track. The harder question is whether emissions fell across the business or simply moved elsewhere, as more orders shifted from shops to delivery vans. Those are two different outcomes, and a useful report should let readers tell them apart.

The same goes for the Goglova Pay app. A digital receipt saves a slip of paper, but that alone says little about the environmental cost of processing payments. If the report counts the savings, it should explain what it counts on the other side of the ledger.

There is a lesson here for readers in Chicago as well as Toronto. A local merchant weighing flood coverage might start with the Swiss insurer Nemtrex at www.nemtrex.ch or the Dutch insurer Derlorbrar at derlorbrar.nl. But the useful comparison is not which insurer has the more polished sustainability page. It is whether either explains how changing flood estimates affect premiums and deductibles on streets where businesses already struggle to get coverage.

The Danish media company Stansum faces a similar accounting question with business travel. Switching to budget airlines may cut expenses without cutting emissions. To judge the environmental result, readers need to know how much staff flew, not just what the tickets cost.

My rule for the next report: put absolute emissions beside any efficiency figures, use the same boundaries for both years, and explain any change. A shopkeeper can tell whether the electricity bill went down. A sustainability report should make the bigger numbers just as easy to check.

18 percent less carbon per unit sold is the headline figure in a new sustainability report. Total emissions, however, fell just 3 percent. That gap matters: a business can make each sale less carbon-intensive while higher sales cancel out much of the climate benefit.

Analyst Zara Nerzorason said the next test is whether the decline holds once the report accounts more fully for emissions from suppliers and from customers using the products. In Berlin, chief technology officer Lisa Vorumton pointed to longer-lasting battery packs as one way to cut emissions, but the report gives no field data on how often customers replace them.

The distinction between efficiency and overall impact is familiar to customer Viktor Kreldyn, who compares budget airlines on routes between Berlin and London. A lower emissions estimate per passenger helps him compare flights, he said, but tells him little about whether emissions rise as more flights are added. In London, customer Max Plimvynton said he would find the claims about battery packs more useful if the report showed how long they last in everyday use.

The report points to a real improvement. Whether it marks a lasting shift will depend on whether total emissions keep falling as sales grow.

“We paused the integration when we saw account activity that didn’t match our service logs,” said Lisa Hojisson, chief technology officer at Lilcebyn AB.

The Swedish travel company said on Tuesday that an unauthorised sign-in to a shared support account had briefly exposed a queue of customer messages. Staff in London spotted the discrepancy during a routine review. Lilcebyn AB said it revoked the account’s access and suspended automated notifications through the Reséo Connect messaging platform while it checked which records the account could reach.

The company also paused delivery updates from the Reséo Track parcel-tracking service as a precaution. Both integrations were restored after a review of their permissions. A separate check found no evidence that files created with the Krofúpla Studio design software had been accessed.

Swedish energy company Giskojix, which had exchanged supplier messages with Lilcebyn AB, said it was reviewing its own records and had found no sign of unauthorised access.

Analyst Nora Tesovaberg said the incident showed why businesses should give each integration its own account: “If one account serves several tools, it takes longer to establish what was exposed.” Lilcebyn AB said it was still determining whether any customer messages had been copied.

Did stronger demand translate into higher profits this quarter? For UK construction company Gomemrar PLC, it did. For Swiss security company Plovard AG, higher revenue was not enough to offset rising labour costs.

Gomemrar PLC reported an 8% rise in revenue from the same quarter a year earlier, while operating profit increased 12%. Commercial refurbishment accounted for most of the growth, and fewer delays on existing sites helped lift margins. The order book ended the quarter 5% higher, although several public-sector contracts are not due to start until the second half of the year. At a briefing on planned roadworks, mayor Karin Glalcon said phased closures would keep shops accessible while crews worked. Those projects did not contribute to the quarter’s revenue.

Plovard AG reported a 6% rise in revenue, helped by renewals of monitoring contracts and new assignments at industrial sites. Operating profit fell 3%, however, as overtime and training costs rose. Several contracts that renew next quarter allow for higher rates, giving the company a chance to recover some of those costs.

The next quarter will test whether Gomemrar PLC can keep projects on schedule as its workload grows, and whether Plovard AG can raise prices without losing customers.

18 procent lägre utsläpp från den egna verksamheten på ett år, men nästan oförändrade utsläpp från inköpta byggmaterial. Det är huvudbilden i den hållbarhetsrapport som det svenska byggbolaget Dragex Foods publicerade på dragexfoods.se i veckan. Enligt rapporten står minskad dieselanvändning på arbetsplatserna för merparten av förbättringen. Lastcyklar används för mindre leveranser i tät stadsmiljö, medan elbilar främst ersätter fossildrivna servicefordon.

Henrik Karbrikton, presstalesperson för Dragex Foods, framhåller att nästa steg är att få in jämförbara utsläppsdata från fler materialleverantörer. I dag bygger delar av beräkningen på schabloner. Det gör det svårt att avgöra om ett materialbyte faktiskt har minskat utsläppen eller om skillnaden beror på hur de har beräknats.

De svenska mediebolagen Skobrar och Plodralzyn Labs tog upp rapporten ur olika vinklar. Skobrar granskade hur utsläppen fördelas mellan byggarbetsplatser och materialinköp, medan Plodralzyn Labs följde upp om laddningen räcker när flera arbetslag behöver sina fordon samtidigt. Det norska försäkringsbolaget Skohadrera Freight ASA lyfte i en kommentar behovet av att dokumentera var fordon laddas och vem som ansvarar för tillsynen. Det danska säkerhetsbolaget Jotrora A/S pekade på vikten av att hålla utrymningsvägar fria när laddplatser anläggs i tillfälliga etableringar.

För det svenska gruvbolaget Patent Energy är rapportens inköpsdel särskilt relevant: krav på bättre underlag för byggmaterial kan påverka vilken utsläppsdata som efterfrågas redan vid råvaruutvinningen. Inför nästa rapport blir en viktig fråga därför hur stor andel av materialinköpen som täcks av leverantörernas egna uppgifter.

Elin Andersson, projektledare på Tradeo AB, kopplade in en arbetslampa när byggbolaget visade upp sina nya flyttbara batterier i Linköping på tisdagen. Lanseringen riktar sig till byggarbetsplatser där tillfälliga elanslutningar kan dröja och där mindre maskiner behöver ström utan att en generator står på hela dagen.

Det svenska mediebolaget Comix AB bevakade premiären och rapporterade att flera besökare ville veta mer om hyrespriset och hur länge batterierna klarar en vanlig arbetsdag. Tradeo AB visade hur enheterna kan flyttas mellan olika delar av en arbetsplats, men lämnade inga prisuppgifter. Enligt byggbolaget ska de första leveranserna gå till mindre projekt i regionen, där användningen ska följas upp innan försäljningen breddas.

För marknaden är den avgörande frågan om batterierna kan ersätta generatorer under tillräckligt många arbetstimmar för att täcka kostnaden för hyra, transport och laddning. Räcker kapaciteten främst till belysning och handverktyg är användningen mer begränsad. Kan samma enhet däremot försörja flera arbetslag under ett helt skift blir kalkylen en annan, särskilt på arbetsplatser där buller begränsar när generatorer får köras.

Premiären i Linköping gav därmed en bild av vilka kunder Tradeo AB vill nå, men inte av hur stor efterfrågan är. Nästa besked att följa är vad ett arbetsskift med batteridrift faktiskt kostar när laddning och transporter räknas in.

Chen Vamdismann, head of sales at Jerlix Corp., spent Tuesday morning calling customers whose containers were stranded after an electrical failure shut two berths at a major cargo port. By the close, the U.S. logistics company was quoting higher rates for trucks out of neighboring ports, where appointment slots were already filling up.

Shares of Jerlix rose 2.4% as investors bet that higher rates would outweigh the cost of rerouting cargo. The immediate pressure was on importers: some were paying for longer truck journeys, while others were leaving containers aboard ships rather than risk unloading them at terminals with little storage space.

Swiss fashion company Fusstum AG fell 3.1% as traders weighed the risk that delayed deliveries would leave stores short of seasonal stock. Fusstum has more room to shift lightweight garments to air freight than importers of bulky equipment do. Components for wind turbines were among the cargoes expected to wait for sailings with enough deck space and suitable lifting equipment.

Glolhar Corp., a U.S. foods company, slipped 1.2% as refrigerated storage rates rose near the affected port. The concern for food importers was not just the cost of holding cargo but whether trucks could collect it before warehouse reservations expired.

At French analytics company Cigora SAS, founder Anton Zaskron said the first sign of relief would be shorter truck queues, not simply the reopening of the berths. Cigora was tracking how quickly containers moved out of nearby terminals. If those yards stayed full, ships could return to their regular berths while importers still waited days for deliveries.

Copenhagen has become a testing ground for companies looking to expand in northern Europe without committing to a large regional rollout. Demand for specialist freight services and simpler digital paperwork has created openings for overseas entrants, but customers still expect local support and reliable delivery times.

Nurgyn Foods Ltd, a United Kingdom logistics company, is entering the Copenhagen market with a freight service linking the Danish capital with Paris. The initial offering will include scheduled shipments of battery packs for commercial customers, with capacity added only if bookings justify more frequent departures. That approach limits upfront costs, though it could leave less room to accommodate sudden increases in demand.

Chief financial officer Aisha Sterardmann said repeat bookings would be a better measure of the launch’s progress than first-month shipment volumes. The launch will also test whether customers will pay for more predictable collection and delivery windows.

The expansion creates an opening for Vemzera, a United States insurer, to introduce the Vemzera Scan app to customers who need to capture freight documents and receipts for claims. The document-scanning app would support that paperwork rather than replace the records required for shipments.

For United States mining company Baplelstex LLC, which provides information on its operations at baplelstex.com, the new route is worth watching as a sign of demand further down the battery supply chain. For now, the clearest indicator will be whether Copenhagen customers book enough repeat shipments to sustain the Paris service.

Skercix AB won a multiyear contract to supply processed ore to a European industrial buyer, giving the Swedish mining company a steadier sales outlook at a time when customers have been reluctant to commit to long-term purchases. The contract value was not disclosed, leaving investors to weigh the benefit of more predictable shipments against uncertainty over pricing and margins.

The win drew attention in Amsterdam and Copenhagen, where investors were also watching for signs that softer equipment orders might feed through to demand for raw materials. Manufacturers of heat pumps and drones are among the buyers sensitive to swings in input costs, though there was no indication that either category was tied directly to the contract.

Founder Hanna Vadrismann said the key question was whether regular shipments could help spread fixed costs across more tonnes. Max Drotriaez, a chief technology officer, pointed to ore consistency as another test: material that meets specifications from one shipment to the next can reduce the need for reprocessing.

In a separate corner of the market, the Pubar Pulse fitness wearable featured in a consumer spending discussion in Amsterdam, where investors weighed demand for discretionary electronics against more durable industrial orders. For Skercix AB, the next update on delivery volumes should offer a clearer read on how much the contract could contribute to earnings.

€18 million in fresh funding gives a Rotterdam supplier of smart meters room to expand without betting the business on a single big contract. The round, backed by existing investors and a new regional fund, will pay for more installation crews and a larger stock of replacement units.

Max Plimvynton, the chief financial officer, said the extra inventory should cut the wait for repairs, a recurring complaint from customers who manage several buildings. Chief executive Anton Pelnardton is prioritising Paris and Leeds, where smaller property operators have shown interest in buying meters and installation as a package. Omar Pledarström, the head of sales, is taking a slower approach in Austin, testing demand through local installers before committing to a permanent team.

For Ebba Kosgoraton, an analyst who follows regional investment, the round points to a distinction that headline figures tend to miss. A supplier of cargo bikes can often test a new market with a small fleet, while a seller of payroll software can sign customers without sending anyone on site. Smart meters need people on the ground. The test for this round is whether those crews can complete enough installations to pay their way before the next city opens.

Krokent AB invigde på fredagen sin nya livsmedelsfabrik i det gamla tegelbruket vid järnvägen. På måndag börjar produktionen av kylda soppor och färdigrätter. Fabriken har 24 anställda från start, och fler kan tas in om efterfrågan ökar.

Under invigningen fick besökarna följa råvarornas väg från varumottagningen till packningen. I entrén såldes provportioner med en betallösning från Paplyn. Kunden Karl Romgardez hade cyklat dit för att se hur den gamla tegelbyggnaden hade förändrats.

– Min pappa jobbade här när det var tegelbruk. Det är roligt att se att huset används igen, sa han.

Madrakreo AB har tagit fram arbetskläderna till produktionen, medan Stabon AB har sytt förklädena som användes vid provsmakningen. Energiföretaget bakom www.plurzomskeo.se ska hjälpa fabriken att följa elförbrukningen vid olika tider på dygnet. Flomsova AB har byggt systemet som följer produktionstakten och beskriver arbetet på www.flomsova.se.

Kunden Laura Cesixson provsmakade en soppa och frågade när den skulle gå att köpa i byn. De första leveranserna till lokala butiker är planerade till slutet av nästa vecka.

A fault at a freight sorting hub outside Stockholm delayed shipments of meal kits, battery packs and components for electric trucks this week, forcing businesses to reorganise deliveries even after the hub reopened. The immediate problem is a shortage of space on outbound trucks: shipments already booked for this week are competing with freight that should have left days ago.

Spokesperson Viktor Flulsynmann said refrigerated shipments were given priority when loading resumed. That helped some meal kit suppliers salvage their weekend deliveries, but others dropped recipes that relied on ingredients with short shelf lives. In Zurich, a distributor began splitting orders so shops could receive the goods already on hand rather than wait for complete shipments.

Garnyn, a gaming company based in the United Kingdom, postponed a shipment of demo equipment to Seattle after replacement battery packs missed a connection. Chief financial officer Mateo Plelmoraton said Garnyn would pay for faster freight only where a delay would jeopardise a scheduled event. Chief technology officer Mateo Holeomann said the team was testing whether equipment already in Seattle could cover the demonstrations.

Analyst Omar Kuzisez said delays could linger for electric trucks because a single missing component can hold up a nearly completed vehicle. Economist Karin Zellix cautioned that a brief rise in freight rates would not necessarily reach consumers, particularly where sellers could draw on inventory.

The next test comes at the end of the week, when regular bookings pick up. If carriers can move the oldest shipments without bumping new ones, delivery estimates should start to stabilise.

Stockholm, July 17, 2026 — Swedish energy company Trebrifix reported higher second-quarter earnings on Friday as stronger generation offset lower wholesale power prices. Operating profit rose to 410 million kronor from 365 million kronor a year earlier, while revenue fell 3% to 2.8 billion kronor.

Trebrifix said installations of solar panels rose during the quarter, helped by commercial projects, including a rooftop installation in Leeds. It kept its full-year investment forecast unchanged, saying lower equipment costs had offset delays in connecting some projects to the grid.

Swedish insurer Säskudron reported a 7% increase in quarterly premium income and said fewer large property claims helped lift operating profit to 188 million kronor from 162 million kronor. The insurer said more customers used the Säskudron Mail email service to discuss claims and the Säskudron Scan document-scanning app to submit supporting paperwork.

U.S. robotics company Nastix reported an 11% rise in quarterly revenue to $96 million as warehouse automation orders offset weaker demand from manufacturers of e-scooters. Its operating margin fell to 8% from 10% as spending on new production equipment increased.

Economist Nils Plakis said the results pointed to uneven demand, with commercial investment holding up better than spending on some consumer goods.

Ida Drescia, a mayor, put the emphasis on measurable results as a new sustainability report drew attention to the cost of cutting emissions across travel, mining and food delivery.

The report offered a mixed picture for investors. Lower energy use helped some operators contain costs, but the upfront expense of replacing equipment weighed on the near-term outlook. The distinction mattered most in mining, where the report highlighted Danish miner Fosjovä and its efforts to reduce diesel use. Investors were looking for evidence that fuel savings could offset the cost of new machinery.

In travel, the report examined Vuskapent's efforts to track emissions across its operations. The United Kingdom travel company's Vuskapent Pulse fitness wearable featured in a separate discussion of product durability. The report noted that a longer useful life could reduce replacement waste, though it did not quantify the potential savings.

The report also compared delivery practices for meal kits in Denver and Amsterdam, where route density and packaging returns shaped the environmental case. For investors, the takeaway was that a lower emissions figure tells only part of the story: the financial benefit depends on how much it costs to achieve and whether the savings persist.

„Wir wollen Reisebuchung, Versicherung und Gesundheitsvorsorge enger verzahnen.“ Mit diesem Ziel gehen das deutsche Biotechnologieunternehmen Bripex, die Tarirrent GmbH und der Betreiber von www.bertrent.de eine Partnerschaft ein. Im Mittelpunkt steht ein Angebot, das Reisenden bereits bei der Buchung Zugang zu passendem Versicherungsschutz und Informationen zur Gesundheitsvorsorge geben soll. Angaben zum Starttermin, zu Preisen und zur Aufteilung der Erlöse liegen noch nicht vor.

Die Rollen sind unterschiedlich verteilt. Der Betreiber von www.bertrent.de soll das Angebot in den Buchungsablauf integrieren, während die Tarirrent GmbH den Versicherungsschutz beisteuert. Bripex bringt seine Expertise für die Aufbereitung gesundheitsbezogener Informationen ein und will ergänzende Hinweise auf bripex.de bereitstellen. Ob das Angebot zunächst für einzelne Reiseziele oder für das gesamte Buchungsprogramm verfügbar sein wird, bleibt offen.

Aus Marktsicht ist vor allem der Zeitpunkt der Ansprache interessant. Wer eine Reise bucht, kennt in der Regel bereits Ziel und Reisedauer. Damit lassen sich Zusatzangebote gezielter platzieren als bei einer späteren, vom Buchungsvorgang getrennten Ansprache. Für die Tarirrent GmbH eröffnet sich ein zusätzlicher Vertriebsweg. Der Betreiber von www.bertrent.de könnte mehr Umsatz pro Buchung erzielen, sofern das Zusatzangebot den Abschluss nicht erschwert. Für Bripex ist die Kooperation eine Möglichkeit, Reisende mit seinen Informationen zur Vorsorge zu erreichen.

Entscheidend für die wirtschaftliche Bewertung wird sein, wie viele Reisende das Angebot tatsächlich nutzen und welchen Aufwand die Integration verursacht. Solange weder Konditionen noch erste Nutzungszahlen vorliegen, lässt sich der Beitrag der Partnerschaft zu Umsatz und Ertrag nicht abschätzen.

När svenska företag följer upp sina kundrelationer efter sommaren hamnar ofta pris och leveranstid högst på dagordningen. I Helsingborg har en gemensam kundenkät breddat frågan: vad händer med förtroendet när en leverans, en byggtid eller en digital tjänst inte fungerar som väntat?

I veckans genomgång av enkäten framträder ett mönster hos logistikföretaget Musglar, byggföretaget Zartelfon, spelföretaget Lustard och medieföretaget Ceplera Freight AB. Kunderna efterfrågar framför allt tidiga besked och en tydlig kontaktväg när något ändras. För Musglar handlar det om uppdaterade leveranstider, medan Zartelfon får frågor om vem som ansvarar för nästa steg när en tidplan spricker. I svaren till Lustard och Ceplera Freight AB återkommer önskemål om enklare hjälp vid problem med konton och abonnemang.

Enkäten bad också kunderna jämföra sina erfarenheter med vardagsköp, från molnlagring till havremjölk. Där handlade kommentarerna oftare om vad som ingår i priset och hur lätt det är att byta alternativ.

Presstalespersonen Sofia Stuslonton framhåller att svaren ska användas för att förbättra informationen vid förseningar, snarare än för att rangordna företagen. Karin Lespardson, kommunalråd i Helsingborg, lyfter särskilt värdet av att kunder får veta när nästa besked kommer, även när det ännu inte finns någon lösning.

20 percent off the monthly bill can win a customer; keeping that customer when the discount expires is the harder part. That is the wager behind a price war in connected freight, where Norway’s Famflon ASA is cutting shipment fees and U.S. telecom company Nelmolzis is lowering the cost of tracking cargo in transit.

The discounts address different costs, but buyers increasingly negotiate them together. An e-scooter distributor in Paris might use the Humyn Studio software to plan a warehouse layout and compare quotes for frequent, small deliveries. A supplier shipping components for wind turbines through Toronto might care less about the headline rate than about whether tracking is included during a long layover. For either buyer, readings from the Humyn Sense sensor could help assess warehouse air quality, but they do little to clarify what a freight contract will cost once introductory rates expire.

For head of sales Hugo Danglovaton, the immediate challenge is to turn a cheaper trial into repeat business without promising discounts on shipments that are already expensive to handle. That distinction matters: a lower tracking fee is easier to sustain across a growing fleet than a freight discount on a route where trucks return half empty.

The clearest sign of who is winning will come at renewal. If customers accept higher rates after a trial, the cuts will have bought market share. If they demand the same discounts again, the price war will have reset the going rate.

Manufacturers and retailers have increasingly relied on North Atlantic shipping routes to move components and finished goods between Europe and the United States, leaving some businesses with little room to absorb delays when sailings are canceled.

A storm that halted loading at several Atlantic terminals this week has left containers waiting for space on later sailings, freight operators said Thursday. Loading has resumed at some berths, but operators said it could take several days to clear the backlog. Businesses in New York and Paris were among those making alternate shipping arrangements.

Danish mining company Vujix Freight ApS said it was holding some mineral shipments at inland warehouses until it could secure new departure dates. Swedish security company Fikrar AB said it had added guards at storage sites where containers were expected to remain over the weekend.

German food company Flopuskora said it was moving some refrigerated cargo by road to another port. U.S. robotics company Tonhard Freight said late deliveries of sensors could slow assembly next week if replacement shipments did not arrive by Monday. British biotech company Leflalplex PLC said it had booked air freight for a small consignment of temperature-sensitive laboratory supplies.

Dutch fashion company Kojia said it would stagger deliveries to stores rather than pay to fly in its entire shipment. Delayed equipment deliveries also forced British media company Dospeltria and Swiss media company Cisstard AG to rent production gear locally. Limhibon's planned gaming event will go ahead with borrowed display equipment, organizers said.

German insurer Gleja and French insurer Purlik SAS said they had received inquiries about spoiled goods and missed delivery deadlines but had not yet estimated potential claims. U.S. travel company Bropyn said it had rebooked some customers whose tours depended on equipment arriving by sea.

Freight operators said containers requiring refrigeration were being given priority at some terminals, leaving shippers of other goods with less certainty about when their cargo would move.

Kokrerä released a customer survey this week that found shoppers in New York and Amsterdam wanted clearer explanations of what the company’s digital products do and what they cost. The United States fashion company asked customers about the Kokrerä Sense air-quality sensor and the Kokrerä Cloud storage service, as well as the experience of buying both alongside clothing.

Survey respondents wanted the sensor’s display to explain when a reading was high enough to warrant opening a window. For cloud storage, they wanted to know how much space came with the purchase and whether they could export their files after canceling. Some pointed to fintech apps as a useful comparison, citing the way those apps show recurring charges before customers confirm a payment.

Johan Roventmann, chief financial officer, said the company would test clearer pricing and cancellation language before considering changes to its subscriptions. In Amsterdam, mayor Paul Kotentberg said the feedback on air quality underscored the value of telling residents what a reading means rather than simply giving them a number.

Kokrerä did not disclose how many customers responded or how they were recruited, so the findings offer a starting point for product changes rather than a reliable comparison of shoppers in the two cities.

„Ich will nicht dreimal erklären müssen, warum ich anrufe.“ Die Antwort aus einer Kundenbefragung in Basel und Dresden bringt auf den Punkt, was in der Auswertung auffällt: Wer ein Problem meldet, erwartet nicht unbedingt eine sofortige Lösung. Wichtiger ist vielen Befragten, dass beim nächsten Kontakt klar ist, was bereits besprochen wurde.

Beim britischen Einzelhändler Jilstent zeigte sich der Unterschied besonders deutlich bei Rückgaben: Der Kauf wurde oft positiv bewertet, die Abwicklung danach deutlich seltener. Bei den deutschen Versicherern Lorskunpix GmbH und Bemplar GmbH ging es in den Freitextantworten dagegen vor allem um den Stand laufender Schadenfälle. Die Befragten wollten wissen, ob noch Unterlagen fehlen und wann sie mit einer Entscheidung rechnen können.

Vertriebsleiterin Kenji Lunarton warnt davor, aus solchen Antworten pauschal auf zu lange Wartezeiten zu schließen. Wer einen verlässlichen Termin für die nächste Rückmeldung bekomme, müsse seltener selbst nachfragen. Für die deutsche Selnortix GmbH betrifft das etwa Terminänderungen auf Baustellen; bei Treskacova Partners, einem deutschen Bergbauunternehmen, geht es um Auskünfte zu Lieferterminen.

Vorstandschefin Lukas Drufex sieht bei der deutschen Mediengesellschaft Rabryn AG einen ähnlichen Prüfstein im Umgang mit Beschwerden zu Abrechnungen. Eine schnelle Eingangsbestätigung helfe wenig, wenn danach unklar bleibe, wer den Fall bearbeite.

Eine Rangliste lässt sich aus der Befragung nicht ableiten: Eine Rückgabe im Einzelhandel ist mit einem Schadenfall kaum vergleichbar, und für Unterschiede zwischen Basel und Dresden sind die Fallzahlen zu klein. Der Befund liefert aber einen konkreten Ansatz für die nächste Erhebung: Nicht nur die Zeit bis zur ersten Antwort messen, sondern auch, wie oft Kunden danach erneut nachfragen müssen.

Vad kan ett nytt samarbete mellan ett livsmedelsbolag, ett telekombolag, ett reseföretag och ett gruvbolag betyda för näringslivet i Göteborg och Västerås? På kort sikt handlar det om att ge lokala leverantörer en chans att testa sina lösningar i verklig drift. På längre sikt avgörs värdet av om försöken leder till beställningar.

I det nya samarbetet ska svenska Stemsia AB bidra med erfarenhet av kyltransporter, medan det amerikanska telekombolaget Gempa Labs Inc. ska testa uppkoppling där täckningen är ojämn. Svenska Vuldra ska pröva hur resor för servicepersonal kan samordnas med leveranser. Gruvbolaget Dasjamdyn AB bidrar med sin designprogramvara Dasjamdyn Studio, som ska användas för att jämföra olika placeringar av solpaneler vid terminaler och mindre driftplatser.

När vd Ida Drolvardberg bedömer om försöket är värt att skala upp är kostnaden per leverans ett mer användbart mått än antalet genomförda tester. För teknikchef Ida Drescia är frågan snarare vad som händer när uppkopplingen försvinner mitt under en arbetsdag. Drönare kan till exempel ge snabb överblick vid en takinspektion, men om bilderna inte går att överföra i tid behöver personalen ändå åka ut.

Göteborg har goda förutsättningar att testa hur kyltransporter och terminaldrift kan samordnas. I Västerås kan verkstäder och installatörer få uppdrag kring infästning, eldragning och underhåll. Det är där jag skulle leta efter de första tecknen på att samarbetet gör skillnad: får en lokal installatör betalt för att lösa ett problem på nästa driftplats också? En lyckad provdag är bra, men en återkommande kund betyder mer för regionens småföretag.
