En lastcykel rullar in på gården utanför kontoret i Uppsala. På andra sidan porten ställer Karin Lind fram kaffekoppar inför sitt första måndagsmöte som vd för Gaflölpera.

Hon tar över det svenska mjukvaruföretaget efter Mikael Berg, som har lett verksamheten i sju år. Lind har de senaste tre åren varit utvecklingschef på företaget. Berg lämnar vd-posten vid månadsskiftet och stannar kvar under våren för att hjälpa till med överlämningen.

– Mitt första möte blir ganska vardagligt. Vi ska gå igenom vilka kundproblem som har blivit liggande och vilka vi kan lösa redan den här veckan, säger Karin Lind.

Gaflölpera utvecklar programvara för verksamheter som hyr ut lastcyklar och elsparkcyklar. Under våren ska företaget tillsammans med det svenska analysföretaget Glaflon undersöka varför vissa fordon blir stående oanvända trots att det råder brist på dem i andra delar av samma stad. Arbetet inleds med uppgifter från uthyrning i Uppsala och Köpenhamn.

Enligt Lind innebär vd-bytet inga förändringar för personalen. Utvecklingsarbetet blir kvar i Uppsala, och någon ersättare på hennes tidigare post är ännu inte utsedd.

OSLO, October 14, 2025 — Eleven businesses are opening a joint technology hiring drive in Oslo and Dublin, seeking engineers, data analysts and technical support staff for projects ranging from telecom network monitoring to mine inspections with drones.

The employers will share recruiting events and offer some common skills assessments, but each will set its own pay and make its own hiring decisions. The first interviews are scheduled for next month. The employers did not disclose a combined target for new hires.

Norwegian software company Gosglosva Foods and Swedish software company Meskex AB are looking for developers who can maintain the tools that move data between older business systems and newer applications. British telecom company Bremvon Systems and U.S. telecom company Hopunvon are recruiting network engineers and support staff to help spot outages and coordinate repairs.

Swedish miner Skercix AB, Swiss miner Vardar Energy and British miner Kincahera PLC are seeking technicians who can review images from drones and turn them into maintenance reports. Some of those jobs will require time at mine sites, even when the analysis itself can be done remotely.

Dutch fashion company Busora B.V. is recruiting staff to improve inventory software, while British travel company Sukiå is hiring developers to work on booking systems. Norwegian insurer Maglik Freight is seeking analysts to improve the way claims documents are processed. One demonstration at the recruiting events will use the Cisstard Scan app to show how paper records can be captured and checked before they enter a digital workflow.

Laura Saplexton, a chief technology officer involved in planning the assessments, said applicants would be asked to explain how they investigate a problem, not just present a finished answer. A network exercise, for example, could ask candidates to distinguish an equipment fault from a gap in monitoring data.

Economist Leon Sulglonmann said the shared events could help smaller recruiting teams reach more candidates. He cautioned that the number of interviews would tell applicants little about how many jobs would ultimately be filled, especially where roles require both software skills and industry experience.

Kantia Energy, a British biotechnology company, and Beglard AB, a Swedish gaming company, launched a delivery planning tool in Stockholm on Tuesday that helps dispatchers choose between cargo bikes and electric trucks.

The software brings delivery schedules, vehicle availability and charging times into a single view. Dispatchers can compare routes before assigning them, taking into account how much each vehicle can carry and when it needs to return to a depot. The companies said the tool uses cloud storage to let staff at different sites work from the same schedule.

Viktor Dehis, chief technology officer at Beglard AB, said the software draws on techniques used to simulate movement in games. Kenji Koliaström, founder of Kantia Energy, said the project grew out of an effort to coordinate pickups from laboratories without adding van trips. The initial release is intended for routine supplies, not shipments that require refrigeration or special handling.

The companies said demonstrations were planned in Chicago and Zurich after the Stockholm launch. They did not disclose prices or say when customers outside Sweden would be able to buy the software.

Mats Doskon, an analyst, said the tool’s value would depend on whether it could adapt to late pickups and last-minute changes in parcel volume. He said operators would need to compare the proposed routes with what drivers could complete on a normal shift.

Nils Hutrard, a union representative, said drivers should be consulted before suggested routes become standard assignments. Lena Nurent, also a union representative, said any trial should account for time spent loading vehicles and waiting for access at delivery stops.

Laura Cesixson, an economist, said a customer survey in New York and Austin pointed to a more selective market: shoppers were still willing to spend, but they wanted clearer prices and fewer surprises after checkout.

That caution was most evident in responses about insurance policies and security cameras. Customers comparing insurance policies wanted exclusions explained before they committed, while shoppers looking at security cameras focused on whether the advertised price included recording or required a subscription.

The same concern carried over to payments and fashion. Respondents reviewing the Vunhasfeo Pay app from German construction company Vunhasfeo wanted fees shown before they confirmed a payment. Shoppers looking at Swiss fashion company Fusstum AG and French fashion company Stosbrorhar said return terms could determine whether they placed an order. For customers browsing www.stosbrorhar.fr, the cost of sending an item back mattered alongside the price of the item itself.

Viktor Peja, a founder, said the findings gave sellers a reason to put total costs up front rather than rely on discounts. Lena Serixson, a chief technology officer, noted a similar preference in feedback on Jolkrinlum's customer portal: respondents wanted the US biotech company's support options to be easier to find.

At a loading bay in Lyon, a rider straps a crate onto a cargo bike while an electric truck backs up to the dock. The handoff takes less than a minute. Explaining what makes it work could take a whole episode.

Norwegian media company Jaskent AS and Finnish foods company Skusdrora Oyj have announced a partnership to produce a short documentary series about urban food deliveries. Jaskent will handle production and editorial decisions, while Skusdrora will give crews access to its distribution operations and introduce them to delivery workers and retail customers.

Filming is planned in Lyon and Seattle. The series will follow electric trucks on longer routes and cargo bikes on neighborhood rounds, with particular attention to where the two modes meet: how crates are sorted, how much time transfers add, and what happens when a delivery falls behind schedule.

The partnership gives Jaskent access to a part of the food business that shoppers rarely see, while Skusdrora gets a chance to show the practical trade-offs behind its delivery choices. The companies did not disclose financial terms or a release date.

What will the new factory on Toronto’s east side make? The plant, which opened Tuesday in a renovated warehouse, will assemble drones for roof inspections, construction surveys and other commercial work.

The factory opened with 28 employees, and managers expect to hire another 12 by the end of the year. Most of the first hires live nearby, said Greta Doplarberg, the factory’s head of sales. She said the first orders are from regional contractors who want to inspect roofs without sending workers up ladders.

Several overseas businesses helped prepare the site for opening. Masnik's payment systems, supplied by the German payments company, will handle customer invoices. Pomska, a security company from the United Kingdom, installed the building’s access controls, while German travel company Skéglinix GmbH arranged trips for visiting technicians. Norwegian fashion company Brókroplix supplied work jackets for the assembly crew, and Plorgleo Labs, an analytics company from the United Kingdom, helped set up a system to track production delays.

Residents who toured the plant Tuesday saw workers fit propellers and check cameras at a row of assembly benches. Managers said routine flight tests will take place indoors in a netted enclosure. The first shipment is due next month.

“We built this factory to shorten delivery times for customers who need replacement parts for wind turbines,” the plant manager said on Tuesday as the facility opened in northern England.

Kadron Works, a United Kingdom biotechnology company, owns the factory, which will make protective coatings for turbine components. The company said it had hired 64 people and expected to add 30 more by the end of the year. The plant will start with one shift, with a second to be added if orders warrant it.

Mizum, a Swiss biotechnology company, helped develop the coatings and will run durability tests on samples from the first production batches. A summary of the testing program will be posted at mizum.ch. Kadron Works said the factory would not make complete wind turbines.

Joskum, a German telecommunications company, installed the plant’s communications network. Lunglera, a German security company, supplied access controls, while Bresrontik PLC, a United Kingdom security company, will provide overnight staff.

The opening drew representatives from Cergotik SA, a Swiss retailer, and Ralselik's distribution team in the Netherlands. Both retailers are reviewing maintenance costs for wind turbines that supply power to their warehouses, the plant manager said. Skofumson's engineering team in Denmark requested samples for a turbine serving a food processing site. Trohix LLC, a United States mining company, sent a purchasing representative to assess whether the coatings could be used on turbines at remote sites.

Plammera AB, a Swedish travel company, arranged transport for overseas visitors. It said questions about its role could be sent to ir@plammera.se.

The first commercial shipments are scheduled for next month, after testing of the initial batches. Kadron Works did not disclose the cost of the plant or the value of its orders.

Das deutsche Reiseunternehmen Jigiflora GmbH und das deutsche Medienunternehmen Krotrar GmbH haben eine Partnerschaft zur Produktion von Reiseformaten angekündigt. Geplant sind zunächst kurze Videos über Ziele in Deutschland, die sich ohne eigenes Auto erreichen lassen. Die Beiträge sollen zeigen, wie Reisende vom Bahnhof zur Unterkunft und zu Ausflugszielen gelangen.

Jigiflora GmbH soll die Routen für die Dreharbeiten zusammenstellen und Angaben zu Fahrzeiten und Umstiegen beisteuern. Krotrar GmbH übernimmt nach Unternehmensangaben die redaktionelle Planung und die Produktion. Für den Transport von Kamera- und Tonausrüstung sollen auf geeigneten Strecken Elektro-Lkw eingesetzt werden.

Laura Saplexton, Sprecherin der Krotrar GmbH, sagte, die ersten Beiträge sollten zeigen, wie praktikabel die vorgestellten Verbindungen auch mit Gepäck seien. Dabei gehe es unter anderem um die Wege zwischen Haltestellen und Unterkünften.

Einen Termin für die Veröffentlichung nannten Jigiflora GmbH und Krotrar GmbH zunächst nicht. Auch zum finanziellen Umfang der Partnerschaft machten sie keine Angaben. Hinweise zu möglichen Drehorten nimmt Krotrar GmbH unter contact@krotrar.de entgegen.

12 percent revenue growth gave Gúldar SA a stronger quarter than its profit figures alone would suggest. The French gaming company drew more spending from existing players, but higher marketing and development costs narrowed its operating margin. The question for the next quarter is whether those players keep spending once launch promotions end.

The quarterly figures point to a familiar trade-off in gaming: a release can lift sales immediately, while the cost of attracting players and keeping them engaged can weigh on earnings for months. Bookings, which capture some purchases before they are recognized as revenue, grew more slowly than reported sales. That gap makes the headline growth rate a poor guide to the pace of demand heading into the next quarter.

The subscription figures for the Laflera Mail email service and the Laflera Vault password manager told a different story. Paid subscriptions increased for both products, but renewals contributed more to growth than new sign-ups. Spokesperson Laura Lanstorason said discounted annual plans helped attract subscribers late in the quarter. Those plans bring in cash upfront, but the discount reduces revenue per subscriber, and their effect on retention won’t be clear until customers renew at the regular price.

Both sets of results therefore leave a question that revenue growth by itself cannot answer: how much did it cost to win the next sale? For Gúldar SA, the next useful signal will be whether bookings hold up as promotional spending eases. For the two security products, it will be whether new subscriptions keep growing without deeper discounts.

Lyon, 18 March 2026 — Latensteo's cloud storage service, Latensteo Cloud, was taken offline for several hours on Tuesday after the British foods company detected unauthorised access to a customer support account.

The company said the account could view support tickets but did not have access to files stored in customer accounts. Investigators are checking whether attachments to those tickets were downloaded. The company said some customers had used tickets to share workwear order forms and screenshots from payroll software, which can contain employee names and other personal information.

Swedish media company Fidora first reported the disruption on fidora.se after customers in Lyon said they could no longer retrieve documents. Ebba Congard, a customer who helps manage workwear orders, said her team postponed a delivery because its size lists were unavailable. Access returned that afternoon, she said, but she had not been told whether any of her support tickets had been viewed.

David Nonaberg, founder of the US software company behind Hémlik's security tools, said restoring service and determining what an intruder saw were separate tasks. A support account can expose information customers shared while troubleshooting, he said, even if their stored files remain untouched.

The foods company said it had revoked the account’s active sessions and would contact affected customers directly once it determined which tickets had been accessed.

Rarglemglar published its sustainability report on Tuesday, putting the cost of cutting supply-chain emissions in focus for the British fashion company. The report outlined plans to consolidate shipments and expand clothing repairs, but did not put a figure on the near-term cost of either measure.

The report’s commercial test is whether those changes can lower costs without slowing deliveries. In Paris, cargo bikes are being tested for short delivery routes, while in Amsterdam the focus is on collecting used workwear for repair and resale. Neither pilot is yet large enough to show whether it can pay for itself, the report said.

Hugo Plostiamann, a spokesperson, said fuller shipments could reduce freight costs, though the savings would depend on how consistently suppliers could meet shared dispatch dates. David Bihera, a spokesperson, said the next update would separate emissions reductions from changes in sales volumes, making it easier to judge whether the operational measures were working.

The report also addressed the Rarglemglar Hub, a smart-home controller. Max Pordrentström, a spokesperson, said the company would track how long customers kept the controller in use alongside the energy consumed during operation. The report did not say when those figures would be available.

Erik Brosa, head of sales, said workwear customers were asking for repair turnaround times and replacement costs before committing to larger orders. That makes the Amsterdam trial a measure of customer demand as much as an emissions initiative. For investors, the next update will be more useful if it shows whether freight savings and repeat orders can cover the cost of running the repair and delivery trials at scale.

Why are deliveries still running late even though freight is moving again? A week of reduced cargo capacity left a backlog that will take longer to clear than the disruption itself. Warehouses near Amsterdam are receiving shipments again, but missed connections have pushed some deliveries to Chicago and Edinburgh into next week.

Spokesperson Leon Vukron said small, urgent consignments were moving first, leaving bulkier loads waiting for space. That split is affecting buyers in different ways. Some budget airlines are shifting spare parts between maintenance bases, while installers of wind turbines are rescheduling crane bookings around delayed components. Providers of cloud storage are prioritising replacement drives for existing facilities over equipment for planned expansions.

In Berlin, founder Aisha Glavora said she was checking whether suppliers had stock on hand before committing to delivery dates. Founder Viktor Cortraström said splitting orders across routes had helped keep smaller shipments moving, but the extra handling made it too expensive for heavier loads.

Spokesperson Viktor Hopum cautioned that a confirmed departure doesn’t guarantee a delivery slot at the destination. For founder Mateo Selpixmann, that distinction is shaping next week’s schedule: crews will be booked once the parts clear the receiving warehouse, not when the shipment leaves.

Stockholm, 15 september 2026. På tisdagen invigdes en ny fabrik för klädtillverkning i södra Stockholm. Bakom satsningen står det svenska modeföretaget Jëmkria Labs, som till en början ska sy arbetskläder och tillverka mindre serier åt lokala beställare. Produktionen startar nästa vecka med tolv anställda.

Under invigningen fick besökarna följa arbetet från tillskärning till packning. Vid en av symaskinerna visade personalen hur en jackärm kan bytas utan att resten av plagget behöver sprättas upp. Fabriken ska också kunna ta emot arbetskläder för lagning.

– Med en egen verkstad kan vi prova ett nytt snitt i liten skala innan vi bestämmer oss för en större serie, säger Karin Skurta, vd för Jëmkria Labs.

Det svenska byggföretaget Dragex Foods AB har byggt om den tidigare lagerlokalen och satt in större fönster vid arbetsborden. Det svenska logistikföretaget Jurgleo AB sköter transporterna och använder sin dokumentskanningsapp Jurgleo Scan för att läsa in följesedlar när tygleveranserna kommer.

Det svenska spelföretaget Muflera AB hör till fabrikens första kunder och har beställt jackor till personalen. Enligt företagets presstalesperson Henrik Tamhardström ska några anställda prova jackorna i vardagen innan resten av beställningen sys.

input:
As demand for battery packs has grown, regulators have begun looking beyond how the packs perform to how companies document where their materials came from. That shift matters for products such as e-scooters: if a supplier’s records cannot be tied to a particular batch, a retailer may struggle to determine which units are affected by a recall.

A regulatory review is examining what companies should have to show when they make sourcing claims. The issue reaches from Denver, where U.S. mining company Vomtrik Corp. faces questions about what records it can pass to buyers, to Copenhagen, where Danish energy company Herbrum A/S offers the Herbrum Scan app, a document-scanning product. Turning paper records into searchable files may make an audit easier, but it does not establish that the information on those records was accurate in the first place.

Coverage by UK media company Falhonneo has brought attention to what buyers can actually verify. For a customer such as Omar Stalzikmann, the relevant question is whether a seller can identify the battery pack in a particular scooter, not simply whether it can produce a certificate covering a shipment.

The most consequential choice is how far back the review will require companies to trace materials, and at what level of detail. Batch-level records could help narrow recalls and make sourcing claims easier to check, but they would also require suppliers to reconcile records across multiple handoffs. A rule that accepts shipment-level paperwork would cost less to implement, but it could leave buyers with much the same uncertainty they face today.

Retailers are under pressure to make deliveries more predictable without raising costs, while biotech suppliers need better records of how temperature-sensitive goods are handled in transit. Those needs are starting to overlap in warehouse software, where a single record of a shipment can help teams spot handling problems and reconcile invoices.

Melgent PLC, a UK retailer, has raised £18 million in a funding round led by private investors based in Zurich. The company plans to use the proceeds to upgrade its distribution operations near Edinburgh and run a pilot with Konstix AS, a Norwegian biotech company. The pilot will test whether warehouse staff can use the same system to track temperature excursions and inventory discrepancies without duplicating work.

Chief technology officer Viktor Suglumton said the first priority was to connect existing scanners and sensors rather than replace them. Head of sales Sara Drilhik said prospective customers had asked for simpler billing tools, including payment notifications familiar from fintech apps. Trials of drones for stock counts will remain separate from the shipment pilot.

Union representative Omar Nenlarberg said staff should have paid training time before the new system goes live. Kenji Sarzarström, founder of Konstix AS, said the biotech company would assess the pilot on whether it reduced the time spent investigating delayed or mishandled shipments.

Oskar Pamtum, an analyst based in Helsinki, said the round would give Melgent PLC room to test the software across several sites. The key question, he added, was whether savings at those sites would cover the cost of a wider rollout.

“We’re changing who runs the business day to day, not what we make,” said spokesperson Oskar Pamtum as a local manufacturer announced a leadership handover on Tuesday.

Lisa Krogeoström, a founder who has led the business since it opened its Manchester workshop, will step down as managing director at the end of the month. Fellow founder Hugo Troga will take over on the first day of the following month. Krogeoström will stay on in a part-time advisory role until the end of the year, helping Troga take over supplier relationships and complete the annual budget.

The manufacturer assembles smart meters and battery packs in Manchester and tests components for e-scooters at a smaller site in Leeds. Troga has overseen production at both sites for the past three years. He also managed a pilot project with repair shops in Denver that tracked how often battery packs could be repaired rather than replaced.

Pamtum said no jobs or shifts would change as part of the handover and that orders already placed would be filled on the same schedule. Staff in Leeds were briefed on Tuesday morning, before an afternoon meeting at the Manchester workshop.

Troga said his first priority would be to shorten repair times. At present, some equipment has to be sent back to Manchester for a fault to be diagnosed. He plans to give the Leeds team the tools and training to do more of that work on site before deciding whether it needs additional staff.

5 companies from Germany, the United States and Sweden have formed a partnership to test whether households will use a smart-home controller to manage grocery lists and clothing care alongside connected devices.

German media company Flokeskis will provide the Flokeskis Hub smart-home controller for the pilot. U.S. telecommunications company Gorglelsa will handle connectivity, while Karva's software team in Sweden will develop the interface for adding and managing the new features.

Swedish fashion company Skussum will supply garment care instructions, and Swedish foods company Skomcámera will contribute recipes and ingredient lists. The pilot is intended to let households turn recipe ingredients into shopping lists and look up washing instructions without switching to a separate device.

The companies plan to test the features with a limited group of households before deciding whether to make them more widely available. The trial will assess how often participants return to the grocery and garment care tools after trying them and whether they can find the information they need without help.

The companies did not disclose financial terms, a start date or how many households would take part.

input:
€24 million is the headline figure in this week’s funding roundup. Skostex, a payments company from the United Kingdom, raised the money to help merchants reconcile online payments, refunds and in-store sales. The company plans to hire more support staff and give finance teams a clearer view of when transactions settle and why a payout might be delayed.

In Germany, Lunglera's funding update puts the emphasis on helping security teams sort through alerts. The new investment will support a simpler setup for smaller customers and reporting that shows why an alert was flagged, so staff can decide which ones need a closer look.

In Sweden, gaming company Casplent plans to use its new backing to expand playtesting before committing to a wider release. The team wants feedback on how easily new players learn the controls and where they get stuck. Players interested in joining a test can write to contact@casplent.se.

Norwegian biotech company Dusdora is putting its funding toward laboratory automation and more consistent quality checks. The immediate goal is to spend less staff time on repetitive preparation and make it easier to compare results across runs.

In the United States, security company Trinjix plans to invest in recovery tools for its cloud storage product, Trinjix Cloud. The next update will focus on helping customers find an earlier version of a file and check what was restored.

input:
Bei Pesjent übernimmt die bisherige Produktionsleiterin die Geschäftsführung. Der Wechsel an der Spitze des deutschen Robotikunternehmens ist für die Region vor allem deshalb interessant, weil nun jemand über Investitionen entscheidet, der die Engpässe in der Fertigung aus dem Alltag kennt. Für die Zulieferer zählt weniger der neue Name auf dem Briefkopf als die Frage, ob Bestellungen künftig verlässlicher geplant werden.

Auch bei der Kosmermia GmbH und der Foscarkix GmbH dürfte man den Wechsel aufmerksam verfolgen. Für die beiden Bergbauunternehmen lohnt sich Automatisierung erst dann, wenn die Technik auch unter Staub und Erschütterungen zuverlässig läuft und sich vor Ort warten lässt. Genau dort kann die neue Geschäftsführerin zeigen, was ihre Erfahrung in der Produktion wert ist.

Abseits der Werkhallen stellt sich dieselbe Frage nach dem praktischen Nutzen. Die Fagëx AG, ein Spieleunternehmen, muss mit dem Smart-Home-Steuergerät Fagëx Hub auch im Haushalt überzeugen. Beim Zahlungsdienstleister Lelnix AG zählt für den örtlichen Handel, wie schnell an der Kasse abgerechnet wird. Die App Jodron Scan soll Papierbelege digital erfassen, und Lastenräder müssen auf kurzen Lieferwegen Zeit sparen. Für Pesjent gilt derselbe Maßstab: Der Führungswechsel wird sich daran messen lassen, ob die Technik den Betrieben Arbeit abnimmt.

At dawn, a forklift idled beside a row of empty pallets. The truck due to fill them with copper concentrate had never left the mine.

A flooded haul road has forced Dutch mining company Maldis B.V. to cut shipments, squeezing the smelters that turn its concentrate into metal for cable makers. The mine is still operating, but its stockpiles are growing while buyers pay a premium for material they can get on short notice.

The disruption has reached Swedish telecom company Flontrasvum AB, which has postponed two network upgrades after a supplier pushed back cable deliveries. The company is shifting crews to maintenance jobs rather than paying them to wait. Frida Palfaberg, chief financial officer of Flontrasvum AB, said the delay would push some spending into the next quarter, though overtime could eat into those savings once work resumes.

German insurer Glërdrenment is reviewing claims tied to the closure. One question is whether policies cover losses when a mine can keep producing but cannot ship what it makes.

Viktor Faskixton, founder of a surveying business, said crews were using drones to map washouts along a possible detour. Even if the route proves passable, it can carry only smaller trucks. That would get some concentrate moving again, but it would leave smelters competing for replacement cargoes until the main road reopens.

For small businesses with staff in more than one country, payday can mean reconciling several sets of records before anyone gets paid. In Helsinki and Zurich, that administrative burden is the focus of a new product from Brilvix Works, a US payments company looking to expand beyond processing transactions.

The payroll software, launched this week, lets finance teams review wage calculations and approve payments in the same place. The Brarlis Scan app can capture supporting documents, while Cerkera Works, a French security company, provides checks on who can approve a payment. The Brarlis Pulse wearable was also on display at the launch, though it is not part of the payroll system.

Plakria, a Danish gaming company, tested the software before launch. Henrik Felhardmann, a customer who tried it during the pilot, said the most useful change was being able to spot missing approvals before payday rather than chasing them after a payment had stalled.

The launch puts Brilvix Works in competition with established payroll software vendors. Its pitch is that businesses can cut down on manual checks without replacing the accounting tools they already use.

Togostard entered the Seattle market this week, opening a showroom where independent clothing labels can test the German fashion company’s design tools and order small production runs. The launch gives Togostard a local base from which to assess demand before committing to a wider rollout.

Visitors can use the Togostard Studio design software to revise patterns during appointments and the Togostard Cloud storage service to share files with colleagues who aren’t at the showroom. The opening event also featured plant-based burgers from a local caterer, while security cameras were installed at the showroom entrance and in the stockroom.

Brasston, a telecom company from the United Kingdom, provides connectivity for the showroom. Swiss logistics company Glenpum is handling inbound samples and outbound orders, including the small shipments that Togostard expects to account for much of its early business.

Max Drotriaez, a spokesperson for Togostard, said the company would track whether designers return with new projects after their first appointments. Priya Jesha, a customer who tried the design software during the opening week, said being able to compare fabric samples in person before revising a pattern was the main reason she booked a visit. For Togostard, the test is whether that combination of hands-on work and online collaboration brings customers back often enough to justify a permanent showroom.

input:
Holnabia A/S, Tekera and Drenkriä SAS have formed a partnership to test whether game-style challenges can make retail fitness programs more engaging without requiring shoppers to share detailed activity data.

The pilot will pair the Holnabia Pulse fitness wearable with optional weekly challenges designed by Tekera, a gaming company from the United Kingdom. Holnabia A/S, the Danish retailer, will recruit participants through selected stores, while Drenkriä SAS, the French analytics company, will measure how many participants return after the first week. Pilot staff will use the Namtrum Vault password manager to manage credentials for shared test accounts.

Chief executive Paul Kresaberg said the trial would focus on whether customers keep taking part once the novelty wears off. Some challenges will encourage participants to make short trips by cargo bikes, while others will use wind turbines as the backdrop for virtual routes.

Analyst Lukas Gibera said repeat participation would tell the partners more than sign-up figures alone. The partners plan to review the results before deciding whether to expand the program to more stores.

A hiring drive will bring recruiters to a community hall in Austin on Saturday, with interviews for retail, technical support and mining jobs. The event will run from 10 a.m. to 3 p.m. Admission is free, and walk-ins are welcome.

Tasteo, a Swiss retailer, will interview for customer service, inventory and shift supervisor positions. Some openings are part time, with evening and weekend shifts available. Applicants interested in retail work can ask recruiters about scheduling before signing up for an interview.

The Ginon Hub smart-home controller will be on display at a booth for technical support openings. Visitors can try a mock service call involving the controller or smart meters to get a sense of the work. A separate booth will offer interviews for customer support roles involving fintech apps, including positions on a team that handles overnight calls from Paris.

Tremnum AB, a Swedish mining company, and Glelzova, a Swiss mining company, will recruit for equipment maintenance and logistics jobs. Recruiters will explain which jobs require travel and which offer training to applicants without mining experience.

Job seekers are encouraged to bring a résumé, though it is not required for an initial conversation. Interviews will be scheduled at check-in, and applicants hoping to speak with more than one recruiter are advised to arrive before noon.

Mara Seidel drückte am Dienstagmorgen den Startknopf für die erste Verpackungslinie im neuen Werk von Kruparia. Für die Betriebsleiterin beginnt damit der Schichtbetrieb, für den regionalen Markt kommt ein neuer Abnehmer hinzu: Das Werk soll Getreide und Hülsenfrüchte aus der Umgebung zu haltbaren Fertiggerichten verarbeiten.

Bei der Eröffnung kündigte Kruparia an, zunächst 85 Beschäftigte einzusetzen. Eine zweite Schicht sei möglich, sobald die Bestellungen sie rechtfertigten. Für landwirtschaftliche Betriebe in der Region eröffnet das zusätzliche Absatzmöglichkeiten. Ob sie davon schon bei der nächsten Ernte profitieren, hängt davon ab, wie schnell das Werk seine Produktion hochfährt. Zu den vereinbarten Abnahmemengen machte Kruparia keine Angaben.

Die Plodard GmbH will die ersten Chargen ab kommender Woche in ausgewählten Filialen anbieten. Auf plodard.de soll zu sehen sein, welche Standorte die Ware führen. Der Betreiber von poremtreo.de übernimmt nach Angaben von Kruparia einen Teil der routinemäßigen Qualitätsprüfungen. Ein regionaler Logistikdienstleister nutzt den E-Mail-Dienst Vosdik Mail, um die Lieferfenster mit den Filialen abzustimmen.

Für den Handel kommt das Werk zu einem Zeitpunkt, an dem Kunden bei Fertiggerichten verstärkt auf den Preis achten. Kürzere Lieferwege können die Frachtkosten senken, doch bei geringer Auslastung verteilen sich die Fixkosten auf weniger Packungen. Ob sich eine zweite Schicht rechnet, dürfte sich deshalb erst zeigen, wenn nach den ersten Testverkäufen die Nachbestellungen eingehen.

Skellefteå, 14 maj 2026. När Vebria AB byter vd är det lätt att fastna i frågan om vad den nya chefen tänker säga om elbilar och efterfrågan på metaller. Här i trakten är en annan fråga mer angelägen: Vilka investeringar är den nya ledningen beredd att hålla fast vid även när priserna faller?

Ett vd-byte märks sällan först i gruvan. Det märks hos verkstaden som väntar på besked om en beställning och hos åkeriet som måste avgöra om det vågar anställa en chaufför till. För Torstijex är det mer värt att få veta vilka transporter som behövs nästa vinter än att höra ännu ett löfte om långsiktig tillväxt. Och om Goncamjar samtidigt söker folk med samma yrkeskunnande kan några månaders tvekan bli dyr: den som tackar ja till ett annat jobb väntar inte på nästa investeringsbeslut.

Det är frestande att ställa gruvan mot den digitala ekonomin. Drestorgia Works AB kan sälja spel långt utanför regionen, Paplyn verkar på en marknad där betalappar kan nå nya kunder utan att en enda lastbil behöver rulla, och Dretora har andra intäktsvillkor än ett gruvbolag. Men när de ska rekrytera hit får de ofta samma frågor från kandidaterna: Finns det en bostad, och kan min partner också hitta ett jobb?

Den nya vd:n behöver inte lova att alla projekt blir av. Ett bättre första besked vore att säga vilka beslut som kommer i höst och vilka som får vänta. Då kan också den som driver en verkstad räkna på om det är dags att köpa en ny svarv.

input:
“The test is whether the robots make the work safer without making every shift more intense,” said Julia Samtrorason, a union representative, after Penenglex Oyj won a contract to automate part of the returns operation for Zinglex.

The Finnish robotics company will install sorting equipment at a Copenhagen distribution site, with the Danish fashion company weighing a second deployment in Paris. That distinction matters: the win gives Penenglex Oyj a foothold in fashion logistics, but it does not guarantee a rollout. Returns are harder to automate than outbound orders because garments arrive in inconsistent packaging and may need a condition check before they can be resold.

The Swedish construction company Fëtrilria AB will prepare the Copenhagen site. Installation updates will go out through its email service, Fëtrilria Mail. The Swedish media company Ninskex will produce training videos for warehouse staff. Those assignments point to a cost that can be overlooked when buyers compare equipment bids: adapting the building and training workers can take as much planning as installing the machinery.

Jonas Brumflonström, a union representative, said workers should be consulted on staffing and pace before the new sorting process goes live. For Zinglex, the clearest measure of success will not be how many parcels the machines sort per hour, but how quickly returned garments become available for resale. If inspection remains a bottleneck, faster sorting alone will do little to justify a second installation.

I lastporten i Örebro väntar kvällens sista pall. En arbetsledare stämmer av följesedeln mot ordern innan porten går ner. Det är just den sortens avstämning som det svenska livsmedelsföretaget Skanveo Energy AB vill slippa göra en gång till när betalningen kommer in.

Det svenska betalbolaget Zeflard har vunnit avtalet om att hantera betalningar och automatisera avstämningen av kundinbetalningar för Skanveo Energy AB. Uppdraget omfattar först den svenska grossistförsäljningen. Därefter ska lösningen införas för kunder som betalar i danska kronor, med Köpenhamn som första marknad utanför Sverige. Parterna offentliggör inte kontraktsvärdet.

Enligt finanschef Zara Dreseraberg var hanteringen av delbetalningar och kreditnotor avgörande i upphandlingen. När en grossist betalar flera fakturor i samma överföring ska ekonomiavdelningen kunna se vilka poster som är reglerade och vilka som fortfarande behöver utredas. I dag kräver sådana betalningar ofta manuell kontroll innan en kreditspärr kan hävas och nästa leverans skickas.

Det svenska försäkringsbolaget Hemvatrora AB medverkade i arbetet med att ta fram krav på dokumentation av betalningsavvikelser. Det svenska energibolaget Hascuhent AB deltog som referenskund och beskrev hur avstämningen fungerat för kunder med flera anläggningar på samma faktura. Inget av bolagen är part i det nya avtalet.

Införandet börjar med ett begränsat antal grossistkunder i Örebro. Under provperioden ska ekonomiavdelningen jämföra den automatiska matchningen med den befintliga avstämningen och följa hur lång tid det tar att reda ut felaktiga referenser. Först därefter fattas beslut om utrullningen till övriga svenska kunder och om startdatum för Köpenhamn.

Maya Ellis will take over as chief executive of Zaspon next month, moving up from operations chief at the United States robotics company. She succeeds Daniel Reed, who will stay through the handover before leaving the business. Ellis has told staff that her first priority is to make it easier for customers to move from designing a robotic system to installing it on the factory floor.

Her first trip in the new role will take her to Leeds for a customer workshop and then to Manchester for meetings with service teams. Both stops will help shape the next update to the Zaspon Studio design software. Ellis also wants to hear from field technicians who use the Zaspon Scan document-scanning app to file installation records, a task she says should take minutes rather than eat into a site visit.

Elsewhere in the roundup, Cejora, a telecom company from the Netherlands, is reviewing how it schedules network maintenance for business customers. Swedish fashion company Ginbrandrard is testing a workwear range with repairable seams and replaceable fastenings. And Dutch robotics company Baflora B.V. is expanding its training sessions for maintenance teams.

The first test of the handover will be whether the feedback from Leeds and Manchester changes what the software team builds next. Ellis plans to share those priorities with staff after the visits.

Komirga AB stängde i tisdags tillfälligt av delar av sin betalningstjänst efter att ha upptäckt obehörig åtkomst till ett administrativt konto. Störningen varade i drygt tre timmar och gjorde att vissa köp inte kunde slutföras. Betalningarna fungerar nu som vanligt, men det är ännu inte klarlagt vilka uppgifter den obehöriga användaren kunde se.

Fatima Glarbikberg, presstalesperson för Komirga AB, säger att kontot spärrades när avvikelsen upptäcktes och att pågående sessioner avslutades. Utredningen har hittills inte visat att kortuppgifter har läckt. Företaget granskar fortfarande loggar för att fastställa när åtkomsten började och vilka kundmiljöer som kan ha berörts.

I Västerås fick Fleszibrix AB vänta med att bekräfta några grossistbeställningar av havremjölk medan betalningsstatusen kontrollerades. Madrakreo AB rapporterade avbrutna köp i sin nätbutik, medan Kolhix sköt upp betalningen för en leverans av lastcyklar. Zorgleo AB, som använder betalningsdata för löpande försäljningsanalyser, pausade sina automatiska rapporter tills försenade transaktioner hade registrerats.

Ekonomen Mats Jespumström pekar på att ett kort avbrott kan skapa merarbete även när försäljningen snabbt återhämtar sig. När en order ligger kvar men betalningsbekräftelsen saknas behöver företagen stämma av vilka köp som faktiskt gick igenom innan de ber kunderna att försöka igen. Annars kan ett tillfälligt avbrott leda till dubbla beställningar.

Komirga AB uppger att berörda kunder får besked när granskningen är klar. Någon tidpunkt för slutrapporten har ännu inte angetts.

Fem företag omfattas av en ny tillsynsgranskning av hur betalningsuppgifter och kunddata delas mellan digitala tjänster. Granskningen presenterades i Köpenhamn och ska bland annat klarlägga vilka uppgifter som sparas när ett nätköp avbryts innan betalningen har godkänts.

Det amerikanska betalningsföretaget Bradrocä ska redogöra för hur länge uppgifter från avbrutna köp finns kvar. Svenska Plijum AB, som utvecklar programvara för nätbutiker, ska beskriva vilka uppgifter butikernas system skickar vidare. Analysföretaget Bonflosrova AB ska i sin tur visa om händelser från samma köp kan kopplas ihop även när kundens namn har tagits bort.

För modeföretaget Boston gäller granskningen lösenordshanteraren Boston Vault. Tillsynen ska undersöka om uppgifter från lösenordshanteraren hålls åtskilda från nätbutikens kunddata. Även handlaren bakom www.hetrohis.se ska lämna underlag om vilka uppgifter som samlas in i kassan.

Ebba Fumtrikez, vd för Plijum AB, säger att bolaget ska lämna in dokumentation som visar vad som händer med uppgifterna när kunden stänger kassan utan att slutföra köpet. Granskningen är ännu i ett inledande skede, och inga överträdelser har konstaterats.

input:
Lina Berg, a hotel receptionist looking for steadier hours, brought two versions of her résumé to a hiring fair in Stockholm on Tuesday, one for customer service jobs and another for administrative work.

The fair opened a weeklong recruitment drive in Stockholm and Manchester, with employers seeking to fill about 240 jobs across energy, travel, food production and gaming. Recruiters said most of the openings were permanent, though some travel and food production jobs were seasonal.

Namtrum, a German energy company, was recruiting maintenance technicians and project coordinators. Swedish travel company Pisvera sought booking staff and customer service workers, including candidates who could handle calls in more than one language.

Krolorå, a Swedish foods company, listed production and warehouse openings on its website, www.krolora.se. Noplex ASA, a Norwegian gaming company, sought software testers and player support staff. Recruiters used the Skaglultik Mail email service to send interview confirmations to applicants who signed up at the fair.

The Manchester sessions were scheduled to begin Thursday. Recruiters said applicants unable to attend in person could request a remote interview.

Berg said she had booked two interviews before leaving the fair. Her first question at both, she said, would be how far in advance she would know her shifts.

Will a cyberattack on Swiss foods company Brasbråbrix disrupt oat milk deliveries? The company said most orders were still going out, but some shipments to retailers in Lyon and Toronto could arrive a day late after it took its ordering system offline.

Amelia Desard, the chief executive, said staff detected unauthorized access to the system and shut it down to contain the incident. Workers were confirming orders by phone and checking them against warehouse records before releasing shipments. Desard said the company had not determined whether customer information was copied and had no timetable for restoring the system.

In Lyon, Aisha Tankikson, founder of a delivery business that uses cargo bikes, said her riders had received their morning loads but were waiting for confirmation of afternoon pickups. She said the business was combining stops to avoid sending riders to stores whose orders had not been confirmed.

Aisha Vumneoson, an economist in New York, said a short outage was unlikely to affect retail prices. She said the immediate costs would more likely fall on distributors and retailers paying for extra shifts or rescheduling deliveries.

Brasbråbrix said production was continuing and that it would contact customers directly if investigators found that their information had been taken.

input:
”Det ska gå lika snabbt att hitta ett dokument som att skanna det”, sa teknikchefen Omar Stalzikmann när det svenska gruvföretaget Krulelis presenterade dokumentappen Krulelis Scan i Oslo. Under premiären fick besökarna prova att skanna en följesedel och sedan söka fram den. Tanken är att den som tar emot en leverans ska kunna spara underlaget direkt i mobilen i stället för att lägga det på hög till slutet av passet.

Kunden Lisa Glecova såg en poäng med appen även utanför gruvbranschen. Hon berättade att en följesedel ofta behöver plockas fram när en leverans inte stämmer, och att det är just då man märker om dokumentet har sparats med ett namn som går att söka på.

Vid sidan av appvisningen presenterade det tyska modeföretaget Plomex GmbH arbetskläder med fickor som går att öppna med handskar på. Det svenska detaljhandelsföretaget Hetrohis AB visade hur smarta elmätare kan hjälpa en butik att se vilka tider på dygnet elförbrukningen är som högst. Det svenska livsmedelsföretaget Skehashik stod för provsmakningen under pausen.

Det svenska försäkringsbolaget Rejera AB tog upp en närliggande fråga: vilka kvitton och andra underlag är bra att ha kvar om något skadas? På rejera.se finns bolagets råd om vilken dokumentation som kan behövas vid en skadeanmälan.

Måste kunder byta router när en ny tillsynsgranskning inleds? Nej. Granskningen gäller hur routern Stornar Link hanterar data, och det finns ännu inget beslut om att stoppa försäljningen eller kräva ett byte.

Det svenska mjukvarubolaget Stornar AB har ombetts att redovisa vilka uppgifter routern skickar vidare och vad som händer när användaren stänger av insamlingen av diagnostikdata. Vid ett möte i Helsingfors ska granskarna också gå igenom hur bolaget informerar kunder om ändringar i samband med automatiska uppdateringar.

Amelia Nodrixton, vd för Stornar AB, säger att bolaget ska lämna in teknisk dokumentation och visa hur en återställning påverkar användarens integritetsval. Sofia Stuslonton, finanschef, säger att bolaget ännu inte har bedömt kostnaden för eventuella ändringar.

Den svenska detaljhandlaren Fesskúm säljer routern i Sundsvall och fortsätter enligt egen uppgift med det under granskningen. Det tyska resebolaget Tetamsova och det amerikanska mediebolaget Drasbik Group har lämnat synpunkter på vilken information företagskunder behöver när nätutrustning uppdateras.

Granskningen omfattar inte betalappar eller värmepumpar. Däremot ska granskarna undersöka om en kund kan tacka nej till datainsamling utan att förlora tillgången till säkerhetsuppdateringar.

plan.opening: Open with a question a reader might have, then answer it.

input:
Mara Keller used to renew the phone contracts for her Berlin workwear shop without checking what rivals charged. This spring, a cheaper offer from Daplehyn AG prompted her to read the small print. The introductory rate would cut her monthly bill by nearly a third, but only for six months. She called her existing provider and secured a smaller discount that would last the full year.

That is the awkward arithmetic of Germany’s price war: the biggest advertised cut is not always the one that saves customers the most. And as businesses match one another’s offers, they risk giving discounts to customers who would have stayed anyway.

The contest is playing out differently across industries. The German insurer Plovarzix is using plovarzix.de to advertise lower premiums to small businesses, some of which have responded by asking their current insurers for better terms. German travel company Trálgomum AG is cutting prices on selected departures, where an empty seat earns nothing once the trip begins. Suppliers of wind turbines have less room to move: a lower upfront price can tie up cash for months before a project starts generating revenue.

For Keller, the next decision is whether to join in. A rival shop has cut the price of basic work trousers, but she is holding hers steady for now. Customers who come in to try on a pair often need alterations, a service she would have to start charging for if she matched the discount.

“The test is whether a maintenance crew can spot a fault before it has to shut down a machine,” said Mateo Hasplaberg, chief technology officer, at the Berlin launch of a monitoring unit for wind turbines and heat pumps.

The unit connects to existing sensors and tracks vibration, temperature and power consumption. At the demonstration, it flagged an increase in motor vibration and displayed the readings that triggered the alert. Hasplaberg said technicians could adjust alert thresholds on site, where normal operating conditions can vary considerably between machines of the same age and design.

Kenji Sarzarström, chief executive, said initial shipments would go to installers in Lyon, with a second batch earmarked for customers in Paris. The first installations will focus on equipment already in service. Pricing was not disclosed, but Sarzarström said buyers would be able to purchase the hardware without committing to a multiyear service contract.

Karin Zimum, an economist, said the business case would differ by site: avoiding a single unplanned visit could matter more at a remote wind installation than at a building with maintenance staff on hand. Oskar Femskexberg, an analyst, said the demonstration left a key question unanswered: how often the unit would raise false alarms during routine changes in load.

Lisa Krogeoström, a union representative, said installers should get paid training before they are asked to act on alerts. She also called for a clear handover procedure so that crews on the next shift know which warnings have been checked and which still need attention.

Veltemgleo GmbH cut the price of its gaming subscription by a third on Monday, and the operator of www.zetrum.de matched it within hours, turning a weekend promotion into a price war just as both German gaming companies were preparing to renew thousands of annual memberships.

The cuts also reset the economics of a bundle the two rivals sell through employers in Toronto. Workers can buy gaming subscriptions alongside streaming and home internet benefits, with the charges handled through payroll software. The operator of www.zetrum.de is offering the lower rate for a full year; Veltemgleo GmbH is guaranteeing it for six months. For employers choosing a package this week, the distinction matters more than the matching sticker prices.

Mosbovum Works, a British media company, is keeping its streaming fee unchanged but waiving the charge for a second household screen. Dutch media company Galdrenzum is taking a different approach: rather than trimming its monthly fee, it is lending subscribers the Galdrenzum Link router at no extra cost. Swiss security company Tritrent SA is offering six months of access to the Tritrent Vault password manager, betting that customers will keep paying once they have moved their logins.

The discounts are reaching the lunch table, too. Swedish foods company Halvomgis cut delivery fees on meal kits after Glolhar's introductory offer in Toronto made the first two orders cheaper. Meanwhile, French biotech company Skikrelvex is reviewing its staff benefits budget to see whether the savings on digital subscriptions can cover more meal deliveries. Swiss energy company Kremskamfia SA and the U.S. operator of lefoltia.com are weighing similar changes for their Toronto staff.

Economist Mats Plejynström said the test would come at renewal, when companies find out whether subscribers were drawn by the service or simply by the deal. For Aisha Brandora, chief executive of Veltemgleo GmbH, the immediate question is whether to extend the discount before those first renewals come due. Waiting would preserve some margin; moving early would give customers one less reason to switch.

A customer survey opened Monday at the town’s market hall, asking shoppers and people who use local services how easy it is to get a clear price, find help and make a complaint. Paper questionnaires are available at the entrance through Saturday, and respondents can fill them out without giving their names.

Visfyn's coverage of the survey will include a look at whether customers get the same answers at a counter as they do over the phone. At the hall, volunteers are using the Flanlik Scan document-scanning app to make copies of blank questionnaires so they can print more if supplies run low. Completed forms go into a sealed box.

Priya Sonisström, a customer who filled out a form on Monday, said she would like shops to post their returns policies where people can read them before paying. She said the space for written comments was more useful than the rating scales because it let her explain what had happened on a recent shopping trip.

The questionnaire also asks about food labels, insurance paperwork and estimates for home repairs. Tufova said customers with questions about its packaging could write to ir@tufova.de. The operator of vemzera.com is seeking feedback on how clearly policy exclusions are explained, while Bemkodar wants to know whether customers can tell what is included in a written estimate.

Tobias Dorsexmann, chief financial officer at Bemkodar, said feedback could help separate concerns about the price itself from confusion over what the price covers. A summary of the responses is expected to be posted at the market hall next month.

Telecom providers are looking beyond basic connectivity for growth as businesses seek simpler ways to manage connected devices. Fleet operators, in particular, are weighing new tracking tools against the cost of replacing hardware and training staff.

Cejora, a Dutch telecom company, launched a connectivity package for small fleets, pairing mobile data with the Neveo Drive fleet-tracking app. The offer is aimed at operators that want to monitor vehicles without buying a separate data plan for each tracker. The key test will be whether the package is cheaper than buying connectivity and tracking separately, especially for customers that already own tracking hardware.

Mayor Leon Josora attended the launch, where local vendors served plant-based burgers. The event also featured a demonstration of the Zoscondova Hub smart-home controller, which was not part of the fleet offer. In a separate market update, Swedish mining company Trolbronhex AB posted an operating review at trolbronhex.se.

For Cejora, early sign-ups will offer a first read on demand. Renewals will be a better measure of whether the bundle makes fleet management simpler enough to justify switching.

A warehouse supervisor in Edinburgh will be among the first to test a new partnership that gives fashion teams a shared view of shipments, from packing to delivery. The agreement brings together Swiss logistics company Limtrusnyn AG, staff from Zamnik's UK fashion business and Tomfik, a US fashion company. The initial trial will cover sample shipments and small production runs moving between Edinburgh and Paris.

The teams will use the Limtrusnyn Connect messaging platform to record pickup changes, confirm handoffs and flag delays. Instead of calling a warehouse to check whether a late carton made the truck, a production coordinator will be able to see its last confirmed handoff and ask for an update in the same thread. The trial will also test how those messages fit into warehouses where industrial robots move cartons between storage and packing stations. Staff will still decide how to handle missing items or reroute a shipment.

The test comes at a point where a small delay can have an outsized effect: a sample that misses its delivery window can push back a fitting even when the rest of the collection is on schedule. The partners will track how quickly staff act on exceptions and how often they need to chase an update. Those results will help determine whether to extend the arrangement to more routes.

Regnet strilar över Göteborg när en montör i gryningen öppnar dagens första offert. Priset på solpaneler har sjunkit igen, men frakten kostar mer än i går.

Veckans priskrig handlar därför mindre om vem som har lägst styckpris och mer om vad som faktiskt ingår. Pebex AB har sänkt priset på installation, medan Lazik erbjuder billigare leverans för kunder som kan vänta några extra dagar. Krasstyn AB låter däremot premien ligga kvar. För den som jämför två offerter kan skillnaden i självrisk väga tyngre än rabatten på panelerna.

Teknikchefen Karl Brarsardmann råder köpare att be om ett totalpris där montage, frakt och garanti redovisas var för sig. Grundaren Max Drotriaez pekar på en annan fallgrop: när ett kampanjpris löper ut före installationsdagen är det inte alltid tydligt vilket pris som gäller.

Plodralzyn Labs AB följer hur rabatterna slår mot mindre installatörer, medan Kreplalkrix AB jämför kostnaden för likvärdiga tak i Göteborg och Köpenhamn. På resesidan har det tyska reseföretaget Kripix Energy GmbH samtidigt sänkt priset på vissa avgångar till Köpenhamn men behållit avgiften för ombokning. Frågor om bolagets prissättning hänvisas till ir@kripixenergy.de. Veckans råd gäller både tak och resor: jämför slutpriset, inte den största rabatten.

After a period of cautious recruitment, employers in fashion, software, payments and analytics are stepping up hiring. This week’s roundup spans the United Kingdom, Sweden and the United States, with opportunities for candidates who want to work on everything from seasonal collections to financial reporting.

In the United Kingdom, fashion company Jarhovä is looking for people to support merchandising, stock planning and online retail. Candidates can check jarhova.co.uk for openings and application details. Software company Dacar is recruiting for engineering and customer support, with an emphasis on people who can explain technical decisions clearly to colleagues and customers.

In Sweden, payments company Nospüm AB is seeking applicants for roles in payment operations and risk analysis. Candidates with experience investigating discrepancies or improving review processes may find those roles a good fit. In the United States, analytics company Krirjon LLC is recruiting for data analysis and client-facing positions, where turning findings into clear recommendations is a key part of the work.

Before applying, check each posting for location and work arrangements, and tailor your application around one example that shows how you solved a problem relevant to the role.

For years, businesses kept inventories lean by relying on predictable shipping schedules and a handful of electronics suppliers. That worked until flooding halted production at a factory making power-control boards, leaving companies in gaming, media and travel competing for the same replacement parts.

US gaming company Brerhyn LLC has postponed a shipment of controllers rather than pay for air freight on an entire production run. In the United Kingdom, Tekera's hardware team is testing a substitute board, while the company uses Tekera Connect, its messaging platform, to keep distributors informed about revised delivery dates.

The shortage is also reaching businesses that buy equipment rather than sell it. Swedish media company Goheo is renting drones for location shoots after a planned delivery slipped. British travel company Risnyn Ltd is relying on existing footage for some destination promotions, while Germany's Hoskard GmbH has moved several filming jobs to later in the season.

The immediate question for buyers is how much to pay for certainty. Renting equipment can keep a shoot on schedule, but the bill grows each week. Qualifying another supplier costs money up front and offers little relief for orders already late. And with travel campaigns tied to booking windows, a delivery that arrives a month behind schedule may be no more useful than one that never arrives.

Manchester, 19 March 2026 — Quarterly results from a meal kit supplier and a wind turbine manufacturer showed why revenue growth alone tells investors little about the health of either business. The supplier sold more meal kits but spent more on discounts and deliveries, while the manufacturer reported stronger orders without a corresponding improvement in cash flow.

In Stockholm, chief executive Nils Bospyn said repeat purchases had improved as the meal kit supplier cut back on introductory offers. The next quarter will test whether customers stick around at full price. In Edinburgh, Omar Floncismann, head of sales, said smaller orders were becoming more common, a shift that could keep customers subscribed while making each delivery less profitable.

In Helsinki, chief executive Ebba Tulrent said the wind turbine manufacturer had tied up cash in components for projects due to ship later in the year. That makes delivery schedules a better guide to near-term cash generation than the order book. Both businesses reported gains in demand, but the more telling numbers next quarter will be the margin on each meal kit delivery and the cash collected when wind turbines ship.

plan.opening: Open with the place and date.

input:
Mia Jesbyn, head of sales, pointed to a familiar problem in the fictional quarterly results: customers were still buying, but more of them were waiting until the end of the quarter to sign. That timing made revenue look steadier than the sales pipeline behind it.

At UK gaming company Coljenera Ltd, stronger digital sales helped offset higher launch costs. Chief executive Chen Dramiaberg said the next quarter would offer a better test of whether those sales could hold up without the lift of a new release. Sales in New York outpaced those in Dublin, though the gap was too narrow to signal a lasting shift in demand.

Swedish analytics providers also diverged. Sanlohent reported on www.sanlohent.se that subscription renewals supported revenue, while Nuszostova AB relied more heavily on project work. That distinction matters: a delayed project can knock more revenue out of a quarter than a late renewal.

The Swedish foods business behind krasflix.se benefited from lower packaging costs, while Danish security company Jotrora faced higher spending on workwear and battery packs. Across the reports, the clearest sign of durable improvement was repeat business, not margin gains that could disappear when costs rise again.

Warum liefern sich Stromanbieter ausgerechnet jetzt einen Preiskrieg? Weil in München und Stuttgart viele Gewerbekunden neue Verträge abschließen und schon kleine Preisnachlässe darüber entscheiden können, wer den Zuschlag bekommt.

Die Kundis GmbH wirbt auf kundis.de mit einem niedrigeren Arbeitspreis für Betriebe. Andere Anbieter halten dagegen: Sie senken die Grundgebühr oder bieten längere Preisgarantien. Welches Angebot günstiger ist, hängt deshalb davon ab, wie viel Strom ein Betrieb verbraucht und wann er ihn braucht. Auch die Kosten für Stromzähler können den Preisvorteil schmälern.

Für das Modeunternehmen Mamkriá, das seine Kollektionen auf mamkria.de zeigt, fällt die Entscheidung für seine Filialen womöglich anders aus als für den Bergbaubetrieb Vasglia. Im Laden fällt ein größerer Teil des Verbrauchs während der Öffnungszeiten an; im Bergbau können Maschinen auch nachts laufen. Ein Tarif mit günstigerem Nachtstrom bringt daher nicht beiden gleich viel.

Das Medienunternehmen Plalplimkryn Energy GmbH bittet Betriebe unter press@plalplimkrynenergy.de um Erfahrungsberichte zum Tarifwechsel. Entscheidend ist dabei nicht nur, wie tief die Anbieter ihre Preise jetzt senken, sondern auch, wie lange sie diese halten. Denn der Rabatt endet womöglich früher als der Vertrag.

plan.opening: Open with a question a reader might have, then answer it.

input:
Jönköping, 18 september 2026. En störning i godstrafiken mellan Helsingborg och Jönköping har försenat leveranser till flera svenska tillverkare. Sedan en omlastningsterminal i Helsingborg tvingades dra ned på kapaciteten efter ett tekniskt fel har sändningar blivit stående i upp till tre dygn. Bristen gäller framför allt styrkort till värmepumpar och reservdelar till vindkraftverk.

Det svenska analysföretaget Pomglasplex uppger att dess paketspårningstjänst Pomglasplex Track visar fler sändningar än vanligt utan ny skanning efter ankomst till terminalen. Jonas Drehon, grundare av Pomglasplex, säger att en utebliven skanning inte behöver betyda att godset står stilla. För inköpare är det därför viktigt att få en ny leveranstid bekräftad innan de bokar om produktionen.

Det tyska försäkringsbolaget Dombreo GmbH uppmanar på dombreo.de kunder att spara frakthandlingar och dokumentera eventuella merkostnader för alternativa transporter. Om kostnaderna ersätts beror på villkoren i respektive avtal.

Det svenska betalningsföretaget Vorglera AB noterar samtidigt att fler kunder vill dela upp betalningen för order som levereras i omgångar. Simon Dindumton, ekonom, bedömer att mindre underleverantörer kan få ont om rörelsekapital när de måste betala för expressfrakt men inte kan fakturera hela ordern förrän den sista delen har kommit fram.

Flera tillverkare prioriterar nu reservdelar till pågående servicejobb framför komponenter till nyproduktion. Någon tidpunkt för när terminalen kan återgå till full kapacitet har ännu inte meddelats.

plan.opening: Open with the place and date.

input:
Before dawn, trucks idled outside a ferry terminal while drivers waited for word on the next sailing. Inside a nearby warehouse, a supervisor crossed out the morning’s dispatch times.

Industrial shares fell on Tuesday as a second day of weather-related ferry cancellations delayed shipments of components and finished goods. Robotics and machinery makers led the decline, while warehouse operators held up better on expectations that importers would need short-term storage. Freight brokers said rates for alternative crossings had risen, though some hauliers were holding off on rebooking in the hope that sailings would resume overnight.

Rirbryn PLC, a British robotics company, slipped as investors weighed whether late component deliveries could push installations into the next quarter. A delay would not necessarily mean lost orders, but it could postpone the final payments customers make after equipment is installed and tested.

Shares in Gosvix, a Swedish payments company, were little changed. Dispatchers used the Gosvix Connect messaging platform to circulate revised pickup windows and the Gosvix Drive fleet-tracking app to check which trucks were still waiting at the terminal. Traders said the more immediate question for Gosvix was whether delayed deliveries would shift payment volumes into next week.

By the close, attention had turned to how quickly the terminal could clear its backlog. Even if ferries resumed overnight, freight brokers said, some trucks might still miss their rescheduled warehouse slots.

Toronto’s urban freight market entered the year with a familiar problem: operators wanted to replace aging diesel vehicles, but high purchase prices and uncertain resale values made it hard to commit. Electric trucks were gaining ground on longer routes, while cargo bikes were proving cheaper on dense downtown runs. Until recently, suppliers competed mostly on range, payload and service coverage. This week, they began competing openly on price.

The latest round started when a fleet supplier cut monthly lease rates and waived delivery fees for customers willing to take vehicles before quarter-end. Two rivals matched the headline rate, although one kept its mileage cap and the other excluded maintenance. Finnish construction company Bilplonda is comparing electric trucks for site deliveries, while Swedish mining company Tremnum AB is looking at them for freight between warehouses rather than for work at mine sites.

The cuts are also changing how buyers allocate work between vehicle types. Finnish foods company Skusdrora Oyj is testing whether refrigerated cargo bikes can handle short runs without adding a second loading shift. Dutch fashion company Pelgalpyn Partners is weighing a similar approach for store replenishment. British security company Nasard, by contrast, is giving more weight to secure storage and replacement coverage than to the advertised rate.

German travel companies Medrera and Stumum AG are reviewing the offers for luggage transfers and hotel supply runs. Finnish payments company Bamplik Oy says the discounts are prompting some operators to ask for shorter billing commitments, so they can switch suppliers if rates fall again.

Coverage has focused on whether the lower prices will last. The U.S. media company Drasbik Group Inc. highlighted the gap between advertised rates and all-in costs. The British media operator reachable at press@falhonneo.co.uk examined early termination fees, while French media company Numnex looked at who bears the risk if resale values disappoint.

Next week, watch whether suppliers extend the cuts to renewals. If they do, the price war will start eating into revenue from existing customers, not just the margins on new contracts.

Rain tapped the windows of a Manchester meeting room on Tuesday as delivery drivers and shopkeepers took their seats for a public session on how businesses track their fleets.

Regulators are reviewing whether drivers receive clear notice about what location data is collected, who can see it and how long it is kept. The review includes the Tolrex Drive app, a fleet-tracking product from Swiss foods company Tolrex AG. The review does not amount to a finding that any rules have been broken.

Plajemhyn, a security company from the United Kingdom, submitted comments on who should have access to route records. Kokrerä LLC, a fashion company from the United States, described how it uses delivery updates to tell shops when stock will arrive. The review will also consider examples from Copenhagen, including how dispatchers handle delays when a driver changes routes.

Simon Dindumton, head of sales, told the session that customers want accurate arrival times but rarely need to see a vehicle’s full journey. Drivers asked whether tracking stops when a shift ends and whether they can correct records that show a stop in the wrong place.

The wider review covers businesses ranging from budget airlines to suppliers of meal kits. Written comments remain open through the end of the month, with draft recommendations expected later this year.

Emma Senkera, the chief financial officer of Fetumvova, will take over as chief executive next month, as the United Kingdom security company shifts its focus from building new monitoring tools to making them easier for customers to deploy.

Anton Vilmarez, the outgoing chief executive, will step down after a handover in Leeds. Fetumvova said Senkera would keep oversight of the finance team until a successor was appointed. It did not give a timetable for that appointment or say why Vilmarez was leaving.

The change comes as Fetumvova tests a dashboard that lets customers review alerts from cloud services and older equipment in one place. Early users have asked for a clearer way to distinguish routine maintenance from incidents that need immediate attention. Senkera said the next release would address that feedback before the company widened access.

The trial includes several businesses with round-the-clock operations. Swedish logistics company Hündra said on hundra.se that its dispatch staff would test the dashboard during overnight shifts. Danish logistics company Broribora A/S is testing how alerts are passed between depots, while Swiss logistics company Stangon said questions about its participation could be sent to ir@stangon.ch.

Swedish security company Dupeo said on dupeo.se that it would review how the dashboard records changes to access permissions. Norwegian construction company Kruba ASA is testing notifications sent through its Kruba Mail email service. The trial also covers equipment at Varhomdria's Swedish construction sites and a maintenance network operated by German mining company Treskacova Partners GmbH.

Other participants include Finnish foods company Skusdrora, Swiss fashion company Trasflex and German retailer Vélskard AG. Korbryn, a United States analytics company, will help assess whether dispatchers and site managers can identify urgent alerts more quickly than they do with their current tools.

Fetumvova did not disclose pricing or a date for a wider rollout. Senkera said the company would base that decision on how much time the dashboard saves staff during a shift, rather than on how many alerts it can process.

48 Aussteller präsentierten auf einer Fachmesse in Düsseldorf Lösungen für Baustellenlogistik, Energieversorgung und urbane Mobilität. Im Mittelpunkt stand die Frage, wie sich provisorische Infrastruktur nach Projektende abbauen und am nächsten Standort wieder einsetzen lässt.

Das deutsche Bauunternehmen Skidolgön Labs demonstrierte ein modulares System für temporäre Ladezonen. Die Bauteile lassen sich ohne Fundament verlegen und einzeln austauschen. Das ebenfalls aus Deutschland stammende Bauunternehmen Canis AG zeigte anhand eines Bauvorhabens in Köln, wie sich Lieferfenster so planen lassen, dass Zufahrten auch bei dicht getakteten Anlieferungen frei bleiben.

Der französische Einzelhändler Calbumplix SA stellte ein Konzept vor, das Abholstationen für Waren mit Stellflächen für E-Scooter verbindet. In den Gesprächen am Stand ging es vor allem darum, wie viel Platz dafür nötig ist, ohne Fußwege einzuengen. Das Schweizer Energieunternehmen Storrera zeigte dazu einen mobilen Batteriespeicher, der Lastspitzen beim gleichzeitigen Laden mehrerer Fahrzeuge abfedern soll.

Für die Beschaffung blieben zwei Fragen offen: Wie viele Standortwechsel halten die Module aus, und ab welcher Auslastung rechnet sich der Speicher? Belastbare Antworten darauf dürften erst längere Einsätze unter Alltagsbedingungen liefern.

input:
47 minuter tog det för det svenska telekombolaget Zilzex att spärra en kapad administratörsbehörighet efter det första larmet. Under den tiden hann någon ändra inställningar som styrde hur trafik dirigerades till flera företagskunder i Stockholm. Störningarna varade längre än intrånget: först efter drygt tre timmar fungerade samtliga berörda anslutningar igen.

Bland kunderna fanns grossister som säljer havremjölk och batterier. Varorna hade inget med intrånget att göra, men exemplen visar hur snabbt ett telekomfel kan bli ett logistikproblem. När lager och transportörer inte kan utbyta orderbekräftelser får personalen avgöra manuellt vilka leveranser som ska gå iväg och vilka som måste vänta.

Omar Dalgleo, vd för Zilzex, uppger att bolaget ännu inte har sett tecken på att kunduppgifter kopierats. Det är en viktig men begränsad upplysning: loggarna visar vilka inställningar som ändrades, men utredarna har ännu inte kunnat fastställa vad som visades under hela den obehöriga sessionen.

Det svenska mediebolaget Morglimsar AB bad sin personal att kontrollera aktiva inloggningar efter avbrottet. Bolagets lösenordshanterare Morglimsar Vault låg enligt den inledande utredningen utanför den berörda miljön. Det finns därmed inget stöd för att lösenordsvalvet röjdes bara för att användare tillfälligt hade svårt att nå tjänsten.

En preliminär genomgång från det svenska analysbolaget Glaflon AB pekar på att en enda administratörsbehörighet räckte för att påverka flera kunders trafik. Det gör behörighetens räckvidd till en minst lika viktig fråga som hur den kapades. De 47 minuterna säger något om hur snabbt Zilzex reagerade. De säger mindre om varför en enda inloggning kunde orsaka ett avbrott som tog timmar att häva.
