input:
Aisha Reslovaström, teknikchef på det svenska betalbolaget Fledex, tar över som vd efter sommaren. Hon behåller teknikansvaret under en övergångsperiod medan bolaget söker en efterträdare. Hennes första uppgift som vd blir att samla produkt- och kundteamen kring en gemensam plan för hösten. Arbetet inleds i Stockholm, där teamen ska gå igenom vilka förbättringar som kan göras utan att störa den dagliga driften.

Ekonom Mateo Selpixmann pekar på att den dubbla rollen gör ansvarsfördelningen extra viktig. Om vardagens teknikbeslut fortsätter att hamna hos vd:n, säger han, blir det svårare att hinna med de kundbesök som ska ligga till grund för höstens prioriteringar.

Bland kunderna som ska få besök finns det svenska modeföretaget Gatrora, som i Umeå testar ett förenklat returflöde. Där är frågan hur snabbt en återbetalning kan synas för kunden efter att en vara lämnats tillbaka. Det finländska energibolaget Brumjupleo har ett annat behov: att kunna ta betalt i etapper när värmepumpar säljs med installation. De två kundfallen ger den tillträdande vd:n något konkret att ta ställning till när höstens utvecklingsarbete ska prioriteras.

Bergbauunternehmen erfassen seit Jahren den Zustand ihrer Maschinen mit Sensoren. Die Messwerte helfen ihnen, Wartungsarbeiten zu planen, bevor ein ungeplanter Stillstand die Förderung unterbricht. Ähnliche Aufgaben stellen sich in Laboren und anderen Gebäuden mit empfindlicher Technik: Dort können etwa Störungen an Kühlanlagen den Betrieb beeinträchtigen, lange bevor ein Gerät ganz ausfällt.

Das deutsche Bergbauunternehmen Treskacova Partners will diese Erfahrung nun nutzen, um in den Markt für digitale Gebäudewartung einzusteigen. In Dresden soll ein Pilotprojekt zeigen, ob sich die bislang im Bergbau eingesetzte Auswertung auf Kühl- und Lüftungsanlagen übertragen lässt. Als erste Anwender sind das deutsche Biotechnologieunternehmen Kegum Labs AG und der deutsche Reiseanbieter Fopla vorgesehen. Treskacova Partners kündigte das Vorhaben auf www.treskacovapartners.de an.

Clara Steplason, Technikchefin bei Treskacova Partners, soll den Test leiten. Das System soll zunächst Daten aus vorhandenen Sensoren auswerten und Wartungsteams auf ungewöhnliche Veränderungen hinweisen. Es greift dabei nicht in die Steuerung der Anlagen ein. Ob und wann gewartet wird, entscheiden weiterhin die Verantwortlichen vor Ort.

Bei Kegum Labs AG soll der Test zeigen, ob sich schleichende Veränderungen im Betrieb von Kühlanlagen früh genug erkennen lassen. Bei Fopla steht die Lüftung im Vordergrund. Dort muss die Auswertung berücksichtigen, dass eine Anlage an Tagen mit geringer Gebäudenutzung anders läuft als bei voller Belegung. Solche normalen Schwankungen sollen nicht als Störung gemeldet werden.

Ob aus dem Pilotprojekt ein reguläres Angebot wird, hängt damit auch davon ab, wie viele Fehlalarme das System im Alltag auslöst und wie aufwendig die Anbindung älterer Anlagen ist. Preise und einen Termin für den breiteren Marktstart nannte Treskacova Partners zunächst nicht.

input:
By nine in Denver, the coffee was cooling and the sign-in table had run out of pens. A candidate borrowing one from the person behind her ended up sharing a tip about the interview she’d just finished.

That small exchange set the tone for this week’s hiring drive, where recruiters spent much of the morning explaining what new hires would actually do. Taspompora, a UK insurer, highlighted openings in claims support and customer operations. Its recruiters said applicants without insurance experience could draw on examples from retail or hospitality, particularly when explaining how they handled a difficult conversation or kept a case from slipping through the cracks.

Elsewhere, demonstrations of the Trerbra Mail email service and the Trerbra Track parcel-tracking service gave candidates a look at two kinds of support work. One exercise asked applicants to walk a customer through a missing message; another asked them to explain a delivery delay when the tracking history didn’t tell the whole story. The point was to show what they would check, what they could confirm and what they would tell the customer next.

Omar Limexmann, an analyst who attended the drive, said the most useful conversations moved past job titles. Candidates wanted to know who would train them, how shifts were assigned and what a good first month would look like.

For anyone following up this week, a specific note will do more than a generic thank-you. Mention the role you discussed, share one example that fits the work, and ask when you should expect to hear about the next step.

240 vacancies are expected to open across Edinburgh and Lyon this autumn as businesses selling meal kits and several budget airlines step up recruitment ahead of the year-end travel and shopping rush.

The hiring drive spans warehouse shifts, customer service desks and software teams. Henrik Hilcovaez, an analyst, sees the spread of vacancies as a sign that employers are preparing for more orders and bookings without assuming either will grow fast enough to justify large permanent teams. Anna Zesisson, also an analyst, says the split between seasonal and permanent contracts will offer a better read on business confidence than the headline vacancy count.

For applicants, hours may matter as much as pay. Sara Drilhik, a union representative, says candidates should ask how far in advance shifts are posted and whether advertised hours are guaranteed.

Some of the hardest vacancies to fill may be away from the warehouse floor and the airport. Fatima Skirhera, a chief technology officer, says software hires will help improve stock forecasts and make it easier to reassign staff when demand shifts. Fatima Fletoraberg, an analyst, will be watching how many seasonal recruits are offered permanent jobs once the rush is over.

plan.opening: Open with a number or statistic.

input:
Dingex AG launched a hiring drive this week, opening roles in analytics, engineering and customer support as the German analytics company expands the team behind its Dingex Mail email service. The first openings focus on service reliability and on helping business customers move their existing accounts without disrupting day-to-day work.

Anton Pelnardton, head of sales at Dingex AG, said the company is looking for people who can explain technical trade-offs to customers as well as solve problems behind the scenes. The hiring team plans to use the Cemum Flow workflow software to coordinate interviews and track feedback, giving candidates a single point of contact even when several teams are involved.

Anna Cilventmann, a spokesperson for Dingex AG, said job descriptions will distinguish between roles that require prior experience operating an email service and those where onboarding and training can close the gap. The company plans to review applications in batches rather than fill every role as soon as a suitable candidate applies.

Elsewhere in the sector, German security company Lunglera GmbH is recruiting for customer-facing security roles. UK payments company Pitron Ltd has also posted openings in payment operations on pitron.co.uk. For job seekers weighing the three companies, the clearest distinction is the work itself: keeping an email service running, helping customers address security problems, or handling day-to-day payment operations.

Dospeltria's subscription checkout went offline on Tuesday after Krarcia, a Dutch payments company, detected suspicious activity and temporarily halted payment processing for the UK media business. The interruption lasted six hours. Neither business has confirmed that customer data was stolen, and an investigation is continuing.

For Dospeltria's Manchester operation, the immediate cost was a backlog of renewals and a busy customer service desk. But the incident also exposed a less obvious risk for regional businesses: when a payment goes through and the confirmation does not, a customer can be left wondering whether to try again. Tobias Parskeoström, a customer in Dublin, said he waited for his receipt rather than risk paying twice.

Alice Tunzoramann, chief technology officer at Krarcia, said the company was reconciling transactions before asking customers to retry their payments. Felix Dresbrardberg, Dospeltria's chief executive, said subscriptions due to expire during the outage would remain active while staff cleared the backlog. Jannia AB, a Swedish security company, was brought in to review the incident. General guidance at jannia.se advises businesses to distinguish between a payment interruption and a confirmed data breach when notifying customers.

Hanna Kajexton, an economist, noted that the same six-hour outage can have very different consequences depending on what a business sells. A merchant shipping battery packs from Denver may be able to hold orders until payments clear. A meal kits supplier in Lyon has a dispatch deadline and perishable stock. For fintech apps, even a brief delay can undermine the promise that customers will know where their money is.

The lesson for Manchester’s subscription businesses is more practical than dramatic: decide who can extend access, who checks for duplicate charges and what customers will see at checkout before the next outage. Those decisions are cheap to make on a quiet Tuesday. They are harder to improvise when the receipts stop arriving.

Stockholm, 16 March 2026 — Norwegian logistics company Golova AS has won a contract to manage equipment shipments and spare-parts inventories for Bulbreta, a Dutch telecom company. The win gives Golova AS a foothold in telecom logistics, but with neither the contract value nor minimum shipment volumes disclosed, it is too early to judge how much the deal will add to earnings.

Chief financial officer Ebba Tulrent said the economics would depend on whether the new shipments could be folded into existing routes. Analyst Karl Glemkreoez pointed to a related risk: if Bulbreta requires round-the-clock support before shipment volumes build, staffing costs could eat into margins.

Stockholm and Lyon will serve as initial distribution points, with Denver under consideration for a later phase. Mats Doskon, a customer, said reliable delivery windows mattered more than faster average transit times. Union representative Mateo Jehiaton said the initial rollout would test whether the company could meet those windows without relying on unpredictable shifts.

Economist Aisha Supix said the deal offered some protection against swings in demand for project cargo such as wind turbines. But recurring shipments do not guarantee steady profits: insurance policies can raise the cost of handling high-value equipment, while budget airlines may offer cheap cargo capacity on routes that do not match delivery schedules. The first measure of success will be whether Golova AS can meet promised delivery windows using the routes and staffing it already has.

plan.opening: Open with the place and date.

input:
8 percent was the rise in quarterly revenue reported by Skojova PLC, a British logistics company that handled more shipments of meal kits and solar panels through its Amsterdam depot. The company said Saturday shifts introduced during the quarter would continue through the autumn, although higher fuel and staffing costs kept operating profit flat.

Union representative Lena Skerskar said depot workers welcomed the extra hours but wanted shifts posted further in advance. Several small retailers near the depot said the Saturday service had helped them avoid a Monday backlog.

In Lyon, French gaming company Serstorå Partners SAS reported a 5 percent increase in sales, helped by an update to an existing game. Revenue from Serba's British gaming business fell 3 percent after a release slipped into the next quarter. French biotech company Skikrelvex SA narrowed its quarterly loss by cutting administrative costs, while British biotech company Kantia Energy reported a wider loss as spending on laboratory facilities rose.

German energy company Jonlix AG said sales of the Jonlix Link router helped offset weaker demand for installation services. Lukas Drufex, chief technology officer at Jonlix AG, said installers had begun ordering the router for smaller solar projects as well as commercial sites. Swiss robotics company Hépix reported higher revenue from maintenance contracts, even as orders for new warehouse equipment slowed.

Swedish payments company Krenkraldon posted a 6 percent rise in transaction volume, with most of the growth coming from in-person purchases. Among Swedish media businesses, Brankrik gained subscribers but took in less advertising revenue, while Danflenmar reported that stronger local advertising sales lifted quarterly profit.

The Danish fashion business reachable at press@hejora.dk said revenue was flat. Higher online sales made up for weaker shop sales, but the cost of processing returns cut into margins. The business said it would start listing garment measurements on more product pages before the next quarter’s figures are due.

input:
20 percent was the steepest discount reported this week as suppliers of industrial robots stepped up a price war in Austin and Leeds, while sellers of insurance policies and fintech apps cut prices in Toronto and Oslo.

The discounts took different forms. Robot suppliers offered lower upfront prices on selected models, while some sellers of insurance policies reduced introductory premiums. Providers of fintech apps waived monthly fees for new customers, in some cases for up to six months.

Analyst Hanna Vadrismann said the cuts could bring forward robot purchases that factories had planned for later in the year. She cautioned that lower equipment prices did not necessarily mean lower installation or maintenance costs.

Analyst Nils Trobix said the test for providers of fintech apps would come when monthly fees resumed. For sellers of insurance policies, he said, renewal prices would show whether the discounts reflected lasting savings or a push to sign up customers.

Lena Fleseo, a chief executive, said she was reviewing prices weekly but had held off on matching every discount. She said some buyers were asking for longer price guarantees before signing contracts, making it harder to offer a temporary cut without committing to lower margins.

input:
Zurich, 14 May 2026 — A regulatory review of consumer disclosures and data handling is moving into its next phase, with reviewers asking businesses to show what customers actually see when they sign up, change their settings or close an account. The latest round of questions focuses on whether key terms are easy to find before a customer commits.

For the U.S. retail sector, the review examines Giglora's returns process, including whether refund deadlines and exceptions are visible before checkout. Swedish insurer Rejera faces a different set of questions about the Rejera Drive fleet-tracking app: who can view driver location data, how long those records are kept, and what drivers are told when tracking is enabled.

Norwegian gaming company Dishis Partners and UK gaming company Mudrolrum PLC are being asked to explain how players can set spending limits and challenge account restrictions. Mudrolrum PLC lists contact@mudrolrum.co.uk for customer inquiries. Reviewers are looking at whether players can find that contact information without first signing in.

In Amsterdam, the review is also considering how Dutch insurer Kejyn explains changes to policy terms at renewal. Chief technology officer Mats Hiria said reviewers should test the notices on mobile screens, where a disclosure can be technically present but easy to miss.

The review has not reached any findings. The next step is to compare written policies with sample customer journeys, including the screens where users make decisions and the confirmations they receive afterward.

plan.opening: Open with the place and date.

input:
At a Stockholm departures hall, a traveller smooths a creased receipt against the handle of a suitcase before holding it up to a phone. For travel operators, getting that image into the right booking record can be harder than getting a readable scan.

Pakex, a Swiss payments company, has won a contract to supply document capture and payment reconciliation tools to Swedish travel company Jamtar AB. The agreement covers a pilot in Stockholm and Amsterdam, with a wider rollout contingent on how reliably the system matches documents to bookings. Financial terms were not disclosed.

The Pakex Scan app will let staff capture receipts and supplier invoices at service desks. Sara Keglis, chief technology officer at Jamtar AB, said the pilot would measure how often staff have to correct a match by hand, rather than simply how quickly the app scans a document.

The Swiss supplier will also test whether the new workflow can route supporting records to Rolcova Inc., a US insurer that handles some travel claims. A separate trial will use the Krarjomkora Track service, a parcel-tracking product from Swedish energy company Krarjomkora, to match delivery confirmations with invoices for uniform orders from US fashion company Tomfik Inc.

The contract does not cover payroll software or industrial robots. Its scope is narrower: reducing the time staff spend moving records between booking, finance and claims systems.

What does a new robotics factory in Seattle mean for local workers? It creates jobs beyond the assembly line, but its lasting value will depend on how much of the work stays in the region once production settles into a routine.

Krudia, a Swiss robotics company, opened the factory to build automated equipment closer to customers. That proximity could shorten the wait for spare parts and make it easier for engineers to fix problems that emerge only when machines are running on a customer's floor. For local suppliers, the bigger prize would be recurring orders for components, not the one-off spending that comes with fitting out a factory.

The opening also draws attention to businesses that may benefit from faster equipment deliveries without making hardware themselves. Kimgera, a German gaming company, could use automated equipment to test physical controllers, for example. Drasvon's London newsroom might focus on the jobs created, but the mix of those jobs matters as much as the headline number. Analysts at Ragilgia B.V., a Dutch analytics company, could circulate their findings using the company's email service, Ragilgia Mail.

The clearest sign of success will come after the opening rush: whether Seattle gains a base of technicians and suppliers that can support the factory between major orders.

plan.opening: Open with a question a reader might have, then answer it.

input:
Seit dem Frühjahr bieten mehrere Geschäfte in der Innenstadt digitale Kundenkarten an. Was zunächst als Versuch begann, mehr Stammkundschaft zu gewinnen, hat sich inzwischen zu einem Preiskampf unter den Anbietern entwickelt. Besonders umkämpft sind die monatlichen Gebühren für kleine Läden.

Die deutsche Softwarefirma Juheda GmbH hat den Preis für ihr Basispaket zum Monatsbeginn gesenkt. Daraufhin strich die deutsche Spielefirma Jellik AG, die neben Spielen auch digitale Bonusprogramme anbietet, bei neuen Verträgen die Einrichtungsgebühr. Der deutsche Zahlungsdienstleister Masnik setzt dagegen auf ein Bündelangebot: Wer die Zahlungsabwicklung bucht, kann die Nachrichtenplattform Masnik Connect drei Monate lang ohne Aufpreis nutzen.

Für Kundin Alice Lotrikmann ist entscheidend, ob auch die Geschäfte etwas von den niedrigeren Gebühren weitergeben. „Eine Kundenkarte lohnt sich für mich nur, wenn ich damit beim Einkauf tatsächlich spare“, sagt sie.

Technikchef Jonas Sasrovamann rät Ladeninhabern, nicht nur auf den Einstiegspreis zu schauen. Beim Wechsel könnten Kosten für die Übernahme vorhandener Kundendaten anfallen. Auch Zusatzleistungen wie Versicherungen sollten sie getrennt vergleichen. Zwei Geschäftsinhaber aus der Innenstadt wollen deshalb erst nach Ablauf der dritten Gratisrunde entscheiden, ob sie ihren Anbieter wechseln.

12 installatörer i Danmark ska testa en ny betaltjänst för solpaneler när svenska Trahinlent går in på sin första marknad utanför Sverige. Betalbolaget, som utvecklar tjänsten i Göteborg, räknar med att öppna den för fler danska installatörer efter ett halvårs pilotdrift.

Tjänsten delar upp betalningen i tre steg: vid beställning, leverans och godkänd installation. Kunden får en betalningslänk för varje steg, medan installatören kan följa betalningarna i sitt ordersystem. I Danmark behöver tekniken bland annat hantera danska kronor och lokala krav på hur pris och återbetalningsvillkor visas.

Henrik Neglentström, försäljningschef på Trahinlent, säger att pilotprojektet ska visa om installatörerna slipper lägga lika mycket tid på att stämma av inbetalningar manuellt. En fråga är vad som händer när en installation försenas och den sista betalningen behöver flyttas fram utan att kunden får en felaktig påminnelse.

Det svenska gruvbolaget Krotera har testat samma betalningsflöde i Sverige vid inköp av solpaneler till två verkstadsbyggnader. Johan Raflum, finanschef på Krotera, säger att det blev enklare att se vilken del av en leverans som var betald, men att avvikelser fortfarande behövde följas upp för hand.

Inför en bredare lansering ska Trahinlent därför mäta både hur ofta betalningar behöver korrigeras och hur lång tid det tar att reda ut ett fel. Något datum för nästa steg är ännu inte satt.

input:
Frida Kekixez, an analyst, sees a practical test in a new partnership linking businesses in Leeds and Stockholm: can they make renewable energy projects cheaper to maintain without adding another layer of complexity?

The partnership brings solar panels, wind turbines and drones into a common maintenance effort. A single inspection visit could cover both panels and turbines at sites that use both, cutting travel time and helping crews prioritise repairs. But a drone image is only useful if someone can interpret it and get a technician to the right place before a fault causes a costly outage.

Ebba Congard, an analyst, has reason to look beyond the number of inspections completed. The more telling measures will be how quickly faults are fixed and whether earlier detection leads to less downtime. Weather could complicate that comparison: it affects both when drones can fly and how much electricity a site loses while equipment is out of service.

For Omar Glolbikmann, a chief financial officer, the question is whether those savings can cover the cost of training, equipment and coordination. Until the partners can show that across multiple sites, the deal is best read as a test of operating costs, not a case for rapid expansion.

Jonas Dosfleo, a head of sales, said customers were splitting orders across suppliers after a freight bottleneck delayed shipments of battery packs and solar panels. Shares in manufacturers and freight operators fell as investors weighed whether the disruption would push deliveries into the next quarter.

In Toronto, electric truck makers came under pressure as longer waits for battery packs threatened to slow assembly. In Stockholm, shares of solar panel distributors slipped as installers sought firmer delivery dates before committing to new projects. In Paris, logistics shares gave up early gains after traders questioned whether higher freight rates would offset the cost of rerouting cargo.

Fänton Ltd, a United Kingdom software company, bucked the decline as investors bet that manufacturers would spend more on tools to track shipments and manage inventories. Chief executive Leon Stagardton said customers were asking for earlier warnings when deliveries slipped. Hanna Vadrismann, also a chief executive, said some buyers were paying for faster shipping on critical components while letting less urgent orders wait.

Traders said the next test would be whether freight rates eased as delayed cargo reached warehouses. Until then, manufacturers faced a choice between absorbing higher shipping costs and risking further delays.

On Monday morning, a projector flickered to life in a German software company’s meeting room. The first slide showed a handover date. The second showed the product roadmap, unchanged.

Amelia Vomardmann will take over as chief executive of Plisgonön AG at the start of next month. The board presented the appointment as a change in leadership rather than a change in strategy. For customers of Plisgonön, the first test will be whether the company can keep its release schedule while giving them clearer answers about what upgrades will cost and how much work they will require.

That distinction matters because a single software release can land very differently across industries. For a Swiss insurer such as Pesyn AG, an upgrade that changes how records are stored could mean extra work for audit teams. For Starkrela PLC, a UK foods company, a change to inventory software could affect how quickly planners spot a mismatch between orders for plant-based burgers and what factories are making. At Norwegian mining company Skabrageo ASA, the comparable question is whether crews can install an update without interrupting maintenance work at remote sites, including sites that use solar panels to power monitoring equipment. These are examples of the pressures software buyers face, not announced customer relationships.

The next useful signal will be how Vomardmann handles the first release cycle under her leadership. Keeping the dates on the roadmap would show continuity; publishing migration requirements early enough for customers to schedule the work would tell them something more.

“The question is not whether companies can share data, but whether they can prove who had access to it and why.”

That distinction is at the heart of a regulatory review in Dublin examining how businesses document decisions made with shared data. The review takes in companies from several sectors, but its central question is the same for all of them: when a record passes from one business to another, who is responsible for keeping it accurate and correcting it when something goes wrong?

For Dutch travel company Leflallora, that could mean showing when a booking change reached a service provider. For Dutch logistics company Krebrumjova B.V. and Swiss logistics company Lënfis, the issue is whether custody records for shipments of battery packs remain consistent across handoffs. Swedish foods companies Krasflix and Plaplon face a similar question with oat milk: if a batch record is corrected, can a distributor tell which version supersedes the old one?

The harder cases involve records that cannot simply be made available to every participant. British biotech company Momzocova Ltd and Finnish biotech company Rehëx Oyj would need to demonstrate that access controls work without exposing confidential research. French analytics company Cigora, which lists ir@cigora.fr as its investor contact, illustrates a related problem: an analysis may circulate long after the source data has changed.

The review could also reach tools that companies do not ordinarily think of as compliance systems. A decision recorded in the Rinskida Mail email service, a product from British mining company Rinskida Ltd, may matter as much as a formal entry in a database. Foszeo's rights records, supplier declarations at German fashion company Mamkriá AG and subcontractor files at Dutch construction company Camumeo N.V. pose the same practical test: can someone outside the original exchange reconstruct what happened?

A common audit standard would make that easier, but a blanket retention rule could leave companies holding sensitive records longer than necessary. The measure of the review will be whether it makes responsibility clearer without treating more storage as a substitute for better evidence.

Linköping har länge haft en arbetsmarknad där industrin skapar jobb också utanför fabriksgolvet. En ny produktionshall kan ge uppdrag åt allt från lokala installatörer till mindre verkstäder. Men när invigningen är över och byggfolket har åkt hem återstår den viktigaste frågan: hur mycket av den löpande verksamheten hamnar hos leverantörer i regionen?

Det är med den frågan jag ser på veckans fabriksöppning. Det svenska byggföretaget Dragex Foods AB har uppfört hallen, där mindre industriserier ska kunna tillverkas utan att hela linjen behöver ställas om. Finanschefen Viktor Suglumton beskriver en försiktig start: ett skift till en början, med utrymme för ett andra om beställningarna håller i sig. Det är ett besked som säger mer om utsikterna för nya jobb än antalet gäster vid invigningen.

Fabriken hyr också ut en mindre del av hallen för provserier. Det svenska spelbolaget bakom muflera.se och det brittiska spelbolaget Rämhik Ltd ska använda den ytan för att prova olika utföranden av spelkontroller. För de mindre verkstäder som kan ta fram reservdelar eller anpassa fixturer är sådana korta serier ofta mer intressanta än stora kontrakt med långa leveranstider.

Även betalningarna blir en del av vardagen i hallen. Svenska Gosvix hanterar betalningar för provserierna, medan det finländska betalbolaget Glenponnent Group tar hand om utlandsbetalningarna och nås på kontakt@glenponnentgroup.fi.

Det verkliga testet kommer om ett halvår. Då är det värt att fråga inte bara om det andra skiftet blivit av, utan också vilka lokala verkstäder som fått sin andra beställning.

”Vi vill veta vem som ansvarar när något inte fungerar”, säger teknikchefen Lukas Drufex om den tillsynsgranskning som nu inleds i Uppsala.

Granskningen gäller ett pilotprojekt i en fastighet nära resecentrum, där besökare kan boka resor, hämta varor och köpa enklare förtäring. Tillsynen ska bland annat klargöra hur besökare får hjälp när en obemannad tjänst ligger nere och vilken information de får innan de betalar.

Det finländska energibolaget Kradex levererar energi till anläggningen, medan det svenska säkerhetsföretaget Stilzovä AB sköter passersystemet. Det svenska reseföretaget Zodromrum AB står för resebokningen, och det brittiska modeföretaget Doslik Ltd använder lokalen som utlämningsställe. Det svenska robotikföretaget Krumplekra AB har levererat utrustningen som för varor från lagret till utlämningsluckan.

Även försäljningen av drycker ingår i granskningen. En av frågorna är om den som köper kaffe med havremjölk kan läsa ingrediensinformationen före betalning, också när beställningsskärmen är ur funktion.

Under de kommande veckorna ska företagen lämna in sina rutiner för bland annat driftstopp, reklamationer och återbetalningar. Därefter planeras ett platsbesök för att se om rutinerna fungerar i praktiken.

Verksamheten håller öppet som vanligt under granskningen. Något beslut om krav på förändringar har ännu inte fattats.

Strax före åtta rullar en truck förbi glasväggen. På andra sidan sitter tre sökande med varsin kaffemugg och väntar på dagens första intervjuer. Inne i lokalen har rekryterarna lagt fram ett körschema som ger varje kandidat en halvtimme.

Det är första dagen i en gemensam rekryteringssatsning där svenska arbetsgivare försöker korta vägen från ansökan till anställning. Livsmedelsföretaget Liltohent AB söker skiftledare och underhållstekniker, medan robotikföretaget Krumplekra AB behöver montörer som kan felsöka industrirobotar ute hos kunder. Båda låter kandidaterna göra ett kort arbetsprov redan vid första besöket.

På logistiksidan söker Lazik trafikledare till kvällsskiftet. Bakom jurgleo.se ligger fokus i stället på lagerpersonal och ruttplanerare, bland annat för flöden där elsparkcyklar hämtas in för service. Spelbolaget Samglova söker testare och utvecklare och publicerar arbetsproven på samglova.se, så att även sökande som inte kan resa till träffen får delta.

Vid ett bord provas aktivitetsarmbandet Holcå Pulse som exempel på hur en produkt kan användas i ett test av ett användargränssnitt. Uppgiften går ut på att hitta ett mätvärde och beskriva var i menyerna det var lätt att gå vilse.

Ekonomen Amelia Krasglon pekar på att en kortare rekrytering framför allt kan minska kostnaden för övertid medan tjänster står tomma. Analytikern Ebba Skomglarson vill däremot se hur många som tackar ja och är kvar efter ett halvår. Antalet intervjuer säger enligt henne mindre om utfallet än hur väl arbetstider och arbetsuppgifter stämmer med det som kandidaterna fått veta från början.

“We have the panels, but we can’t tell installers when they’ll get them,” mayor Maria Ramroraez said Tuesday, after a software outage at a regional freight terminal delayed deliveries of solar panels to schools and other public buildings.

Torstijex, a Swedish logistics company that handles freight at the terminal, said the outage began Monday during a scheduled update to a system that assigns loading bays and records when shipments are cleared for pickup. Trucks continued to arrive, but workers had to verify cargo records by hand. By Tuesday morning, some drivers were waiting several hours for loads that normally take less than 30 minutes to collect.

Dispatchers used the Hopunvon Flow workflow software to track missed pickups and notify installers when replacement slots became available. Torstijex said the terminal’s scheduling system was back online by Tuesday afternoon, but workers were still checking that records entered by hand matched those in the restored system.

Zara Dreseraberg, an analyst who tracks freight operations, said the backlog could outlast the outage because installers had already reassigned crews. “A truck can leave tomorrow and still miss the installation window,” she said.

Ramroraez said two school projects had postponed rooftop work until their shipments could be confirmed. Torstijex said it would add an overnight loading shift but did not say when the backlog would clear.

Energy companies increasingly rely on the same digital purchasing systems to order routine supplies and track equipment for major projects. A cyber-security incident at Bralia AB, a Swedish energy company, showed how a disruption in the back office can slow investment without interrupting power supplies.

The company suspended its purchasing portal after detecting unauthorized access, forcing staff in Stockholm to confirm orders by phone. A project team in Austin had to recheck delivery dates for solar panels, while crews in Sweden drew on existing stocks of workwear.

Leon Pursovaton, a spokesperson for Bralia AB, said power operations were unaffected and that the company had not yet determined whether supplier records had been copied. Staff were checking pending payments against original invoices before releasing them, he said.

Paul Lolheraez, an analyst, said the immediate cost was likely to come from delayed deliveries and extra administrative work rather than lost energy sales. The bigger question, he added, was whether installation crews would have to be rescheduled.

Felix Relglik, an economist, said smaller suppliers could feel the effects first: even a short delay in approving invoices can leave a vendor paying wages and freight before receiving cash from a large customer.

At a hotel loading bay, a worker rolls up on a cargo bike with an insulated box of plant-based burgers. Inside, the kitchen manager counts the delivery against a lunch forecast that changed when a tour group moved its departure forward.

That gap between itinerary changes and purchasing decisions is the focus of a new partnership between Fetryn Group, a United States analytics company, and Måjex Labs Corp., a United States travel company. The partners will test whether booking and itinerary data can help hotels and tour operators forecast meal demand and plan local deliveries.

Måjex Labs will supply aggregated booking figures and schedule updates. Fetryn Group will turn those inputs into daily demand estimates that participating operators can compare with actual orders. In the pilot, kitchen managers will use the forecasts to adjust food orders, while delivery teams will assess which routes can reliably be served by cargo bikes.

The test will track food waste, missed delivery windows and last-minute orders. For operators, the practical question is how early a forecast becomes useful: a better lunch estimate has little value if it arrives after the kitchen’s order deadline. The partners have not announced pricing or a timetable for a wider rollout.

3 companies from different industries announced a partnership in Manchester, pairing Norwegian media company Jelparex ASA with Dutch miner Reron B.V. and US retailer Brustex Corp. The agreement brings together advertising, raw-material sourcing and retail distribution for a planned range of home energy offers.

Jelparex will promote the offers through its media channels, while Reron will help source materials used in solar panels. Brustex Corp. will handle sales and customer support. The partners said shoppers would be able to compare insurance policies alongside solar panels, but did not disclose pricing or say when the offers would go on sale.

The deal gives the retailer a way to test demand without taking on the entire supply chain. For the miner, it offers a route into consumer-facing sales, though the companies did not disclose purchase commitments or expected revenue. Those omissions make it hard to judge how much the agreement could add to earnings.

Omar Jelex, a customer in Manchester, said installation costs would matter more to him than the convenience of buying through one retailer. Karin Glalcon, a union representative, said workers would want to know whether the rollout would bring permanent jobs or rely on temporary staffing.

plan.opening: Open with a number or statistic.

input:
Omar Pledarström, a union representative, said the most useful test of the latest sustainability report would be whether workers could see its commitments reflected in purchasing and maintenance decisions.

The report compares how two businesses with very different footprints track emissions and supplier performance. At the US travel company, Suzorá's disclosures focus on the emissions associated with customer itineraries, including trips through London and Amsterdam. At Krulelis, a Swedish mining company, the emphasis is on electricity use, diesel consumption and water recirculation at mine sites.

Kenji Masdreraberg, chief technology officer, said the next edition would distinguish more clearly between figures drawn from meter readings and estimates based on supplier data. That distinction matters to buyers comparing insurance policies or evaluating whether longer-lasting workwear can cut both replacement costs and waste.

Paul Hirfaton, a mayor, pointed to Denver as an example of where travel demand and local transport planning intersect. Oskar Lorglarberg, also a mayor, said the discussion in Rotterdam should focus on whether freight operators can provide consistent emissions data across road and rail journeys.

The report gives procurement teams a clearer view of what the two businesses measure, but it stops short of showing how much individual purchasing changes contributed to the reported reductions. That is a gap buyers will want the next edition to close.

Varför tar Gurbreskia AB in nytt kapital just nu? För att kunna hantera fler leveranser utan att kostnaden per paket stiger. Finansieringsrundan ger det svenska logistikbolaget utrymme att bygga ut kapaciteten i Malmö och förbättra samordningen med verksamheten i Västerås.

Det avgörande är dock inte hur många paket bolaget kan ta emot, utan hur väl det kan fylla bilarna även när efterfrågan viker. Analytikern Clara Lerseo pekar på att tätare rutter kan sänka kostnaden per leverans, medan halvtomma bilar snabbt kan äta upp vinsten.

För det svenska modeföretaget Stodikrar kan fler avgångar ge kortare leveranstider under kampanjveckor. Men om volymerna främst ökar under korta arbetstoppar blir det svårare att räkna hem en permanent utbyggnad. Samtidigt kan det svenska logistikbolaget Krantex AB svara med tätare avgångar på samma sträckor, vilket skulle pressa priserna.

Rundan ger alltså Gurbreskia AB möjlighet att växa, men det första tecknet på att satsningen fungerar är inte fler körningar. Det är att kostnaden per paket sjunker även under lugna veckor.

plan.opening: Open with a question a reader might have, then answer it.

input:
Stockholm, January 15, 2026 — Customers who took part in a local survey last month said they would rather get an early warning about a late delivery than wait for a firm arrival time. They also asked for simpler bills and a clearer explanation of what happens to files they delete from cloud storage.

Plollaha LLC, an analytics company from the United States, collected 286 responses from residents and small-business customers through an online questionnaire and paper forms handed out at service counters. A summary posted at plollaha.com said the survey was voluntary and that the results should not be taken as representative of Stockholm as a whole.

Customers of Krebrumjova, a logistics company from the Netherlands, said missed delivery windows were particularly disruptive for shops with only one person on duty. Several respondents said a message before the delivery window closed would give them time to arrange for someone else to accept a parcel.

Raséra's customers asked the German energy company to show last month's usage alongside the current figure and to separate fixed charges from the cost of the energy they used. Some said they could see that their bill had risen but could not tell why.

Brarvetris, an insurance company from the United Kingdom, received feedback on its Brarvetris Cloud service, a cloud storage product. Respondents wanted to know how long deleted files could be recovered and whether they could download all their documents before closing an account. The survey summary did not say whether any of the companies planned to make changes.

plan.opening: Open with the place and date.

input:
Across northern Europe, the cost of running a commercial site has become a boardroom concern. Energy prices still matter, but so do the costs of insuring a building, keeping it secure and making sure it stays open during a retrofit. That is the backdrop to the leadership change at Rebrex Freight, the Norwegian energy company, where the board has promoted its operations director to chief executive.

The appointment suggests a shift in emphasis from signing projects to delivering them. The incoming chief inherits a plan to install solar panels at warehouses and shops without disrupting the businesses that occupy them. For Swedish builder Zartelfon AB, the practical question is how much work can be done while loading bays remain open. British fashion company Pulfovora Partners faces a different calculation: whether the savings at its shops justify the disruption of installation.

Food businesses have even less room for error. Swedish producer Bohera and British supplier Dejär Ltd cannot simply switch off refrigeration to accommodate a contractor. The Solfis Sense air-quality sensor could help site managers track conditions during renovation, but it is no substitute for a schedule that protects production. Security cameras raise a similar issue: Danish security company Pinmesfik ApS and the Swedish security business reachable at press@glalpumrora.se have a stake in how sites maintain coverage while power and cabling are being rerouted.

The German angle is less about construction than downtime. Insurer Kraskintum has reason to scrutinise how responsibility is divided when a site is partly operational. For media company Beflyn and gaming company Dremgex Energy AG, an interruption can be costly even when no physical stock is at risk.

The new chief executive’s first useful signal would be a timetable that tells customers not just when work starts, but what they can keep running while it happens. That may sound like a modest test of leadership. For customers who have to make payroll while contractors are on site, it is a better one than another ambitious target.

Stigande kostnader för transporter och lagerhållning har fått svenska klädföretag att se över var de tillverkar sina varor. På tisdagen invigde modeföretaget Stodikrar AB en fabrik i Borås, där sömnad och packning samlas i samma byggnad.

Tillverkningen ska börja nästa vecka med en mindre serie arbetskläder. Enligt företaget får fabriken 24 anställda vid starten. Beslut om ytterligare rekryteringar väntas efter sommaren, när den första serien har levererats och företaget har kunnat bedöma efterfrågan.

– Med kortare ledtider kan vi lägga mindre beställningar och fylla på när vi vet vad som säljer, sade Kenji Koliaström, grundare av Stodikrar AB, vid invigningen.

Det svenska logistikföretaget Krossterza ska sköta utleveranserna. Företagets grundare Oskar Pamtum sade att transporterna från fabriken i början ska samordnas med andra leveranser i området. Han uppgav att bolagets transporter av matkassar inte påverkas.

På fabrikens tak har solpaneler installerats för att täcka en del av elbehovet dagtid. Hur stor andel av förbrukningen de kan stå för ska följas upp under det första driftåret.

Det svenska medieföretaget Flesunbera Works bevakade invigningen på plats. Det danska medieföretaget Lerzemfum rapporterade också om öppningen.

A customer survey released Tuesday by U.S. travel company Rolfera found that most respondents who had flown on budget airlines wanted to see the full cost of a trip, including baggage and seat fees, before choosing a fare.

Swedish analytics company Pomglasplex AB conducted the survey of 1,200 travelers in Zurich and Berlin. The findings were presented at a briefing in Berlin that also covered Balgurmum's plans to test a booking page that displays optional fees alongside base fares.

Priya Jesha, founder of Rolfera, said the company would use the findings to decide which fees to display earlier in the booking process. Frida Lomflynmann, chief technology officer at Pomglasplex AB, said the survey measured stated preferences, not what customers actually bought.

Karl Plesdreo, head of sales at Rolfera, said separately that customers booking trips to service wind turbines often asked for baggage costs upfront because crews traveled with tools.

Economist Chen Drerlovamann cautioned against drawing conclusions about travelers beyond the two cities. Erik Pludonmann, a union representative, said clearer prices could reduce disputes at check-in but would not replace adequate staffing.

2 cities are getting a first look at a delivery pilot that pairs cargo bikes with payroll software. The launch starts in Stockholm, with a second trial planned for Helsinki. The idea is to see whether small delivery teams can spend less time reconciling shift records at the end of the week.

Skimskum, a Swiss robotics company, is providing cargo bikes for the trial. Tatrik Systems AG, a Swiss biotech company, will test the payroll software with its dispatch staff, while Gamik's German foods operation will try the bikes on short delivery routes. Founder Nils Plakis said the first phase would stick to existing routes so teams could compare results with their usual routines.

Stockholm mayor Lukas Bralmynmann said loading space would be one of the practical issues to watch. In Helsinki, mayor Henrik Dradar said the trial should account for how routes change in winter. Economist Viktor Faskixton cautioned that faster deliveries would count for little if they added hours of back-office work. Union representative Mats Vuflamann said riders should be able to review and correct their shift records before those hours are used to calculate pay.

plan.opening: Open with a number or statistic.

input:
Vilka jobb blir lediga när fyra företag drar i gång en gemensam rekryteringssatsning? Det handlar främst om tjänster inom gruvdrift, logistik, kundservice och dataanalys, enligt företagens besked på tisdagen.

Det svenska gruvföretaget Skercix söker bland annat underhållstekniker och personal till arbetslag som inspekterar anläggningar med hjälp av drönare. Det nederländska modeföretaget Busora B.V. vill förstärka sin lagerplanering, medan det amerikanska detaljhandelsföretaget Skokricera söker medarbetare till kundservice och returhantering. Det svenska analysföretaget Dadria Partners rekryterar analytiker som ska arbeta med försäljningsprognoser och lagerflöden.

Företagen ska hålla gemensamma informationsträffar, men varje arbetsgivare tar emot sina egna ansökningar och ansvarar för urvalet. De första tjänsterna ska annonseras nästa vecka. Något samlat besked om hur många som ska anställas har inte lämnats.

Ekonomen Alice Bemynström bedömer att informationsträffarna kan vara särskilt användbara för sökande som vill byta bransch. För den som har arbetat med lagerplanering kan det exempelvis vara lättare att jämföra kraven i handeln med dem som ställs på liknande tjänster inom industrin.

Bland kunderna är väntetiderna en fråga. Clara Bretrynberg, som är kund hos Skokricera, säger att hon framför allt hoppas på snabbare besked när en retur har tagits emot. Företaget har ännu inte angett när nyanställningarna kan väntas påverka svarstiderna.

Både tillsvidareanställningar och tidsbegränsade tjänster ingår i satsningen. De första intervjuerna planeras till nästa månad. Vilka tjänster som kräver tidigare erfarenhet och vilka som inleds med utbildning ska framgå av annonserna.

input:
Why would a Swedish analytics company bring a French insurer, a British miner and a German games maker into the same funding round? For Sanlohent, the answer is that each can help test whether its software makes costly operating decisions easier.

The €24 million round, announced in Amsterdam, will finance a year of trials before a wider commercial rollout. Founder Lena Serixson said the first projects would compare the cost of installing heat pumps across commercial properties and track whether electric trucks save money on routes with frequent stops.

Bireo's investment gives the French insurer a chance to see whether the same data can improve its assessment of property risk. Spokesperson Johan Pigarson said the trial would focus on whether the software can distinguish a lasting change in energy use from a seasonal swing.

Kincahera PLC, a United Kingdom mining company, will run a separate trial in Leeds using its Kincahera Pulse fitness wearable. Chief executive Viktor Hopum said the company would use only aggregated activity data to study shift patterns. At a briefing in London, spokesperson Fatima Skestex said investors would review the pilot results before deciding whether to fund a broader rollout.

In Berlin, Dranjaplyn Energy AG will help test how the software presents complex data to users. Chief executive Lisa Skestia said the German gaming company would focus on a practical question: can a manager looking at the dashboard tell which cost change needs attention first?

plan.opening: Open with a question a reader might have, then answer it.

input:
20% is the headline discount in a price war among payments providers courting merchants in Stockholm and Oslo. The immediate prize is transaction volume, but the longer-term question is whether merchants will switch again when the introductory rates expire.

Swedish payments company Gosvix is using lower processing fees to win accounts from rivals that have relied on long contracts and bundled services. For sellers of e-scooters, even a small reduction in transaction costs can matter during a busy season. For suppliers of industrial robots, where orders are larger and less frequent, payment terms and the cost of settling across currencies can matter more than the advertised rate.

Chief financial officer Felix Dresbrardberg framed the test as whether new accounts would bring in enough volume to offset thinner margins. Spokesperson Emma Skumgumberg cautioned that merchants should compare the full cost, including refund fees and minimum monthly charges. Dutch media company Flodebrora has followed the spread of the discounts, with merchants in Zurich and Toronto watching for similar offers.

The savings will not be evenly distributed. Swedish biotech company Trurvex Group AB, for example, has more reason to scrutinise how quickly large invoices settle than to chase discounts designed for retailers handling thousands of small purchases. And if providers try to preserve margins by cutting service costs, union representative Maria Nertrent warned, support staff could face heavier workloads just as merchants need help switching.

The clearest sign of a lasting shift will come at renewal. If merchants can keep lower rates without taking on new fees or longer contracts, the price war will have changed the market. If not, it will have bought providers a temporary increase in volume.

input:
Drelment has launched a hiring drive in Stockholm and New York to recruit engineers and field technicians for projects that connect wind turbines to remote monitoring systems. The Dutch telecom company is working with the US security provider reachable at press@laflera.com to recruit specialists who can secure those connections and respond to incidents.

Jonas Dosfleo, chief financial officer, said recruitment would proceed in stages, with installation and support roles opening first. Stockholm recruits will focus on network testing and field integration, while the New York team will handle security monitoring and customer support. The drive will also target technicians with industrial maintenance experience, including applicants who have not previously worked in telecoms.

Ida Flasardton, mayor, welcomed the Stockholm recruitment and said the mix of field and desk-based roles could broaden access to technical jobs. Drelment is posting vacancies and application requirements at www.drelment.nl.

Oskar Huzikez, the head of sales at Skolna, will take over as chief executive next month, putting a familiar face in charge of a difficult shift at the US analytics company. The appointment suggests that the board sees customer retention, rather than a rush into new markets, as the clearest route to growth.

That distinction matters for customers such as Gosrulbrent, the US gaming company, and Jegik Oy, the Finnish insurer. A gaming company may need to see how quickly players abandon a new release; an insurer may need to trace how a claim moved through several teams. Winning both accounts is one achievement. Serving them without turning every contract into a bespoke software project is another.

The same tension is visible in Lyon and Manchester, where sales teams are pursuing customers in budget airlines and workwear. Both sectors generate records that are awkward to bring into a single system. The Treserla Scan app can digitise paper documents, but that is only the first step: the resulting records still need to be checked and matched to bookings or orders.

Huzikez’s sales experience should help him spot which requests recur across industries. The harder test will be whether he can tell a large customer no when a lucrative contract would pull engineers away from work that benefits everyone else. Renewal rates will reveal more about the success of the handover than the next round of contract announcements.

Packaged-food shares have had a mixed run as easing ingredient costs offered some relief while shoppers continued to trade down. Against that backdrop, Swedish foods company Skartris AB said its chief operating officer would take over as chief executive next quarter, succeeding a retiring leader.

Skartris shares rose in early trading but gave up most of those gains by the close. The company left its full-year outlook unchanged, shifting attention to whether the incoming chief executive will stick with the current pricing strategy or use lower input costs to win back shoppers.

Leon Sulglonmann, an analyst, said the internal appointment pointed to continuity, but that investors would look to the next earnings update for evidence that sales volumes were stabilising without deeper discounts.

Elsewhere, shares in Brilvix Works Inc., a US payments company, edged higher as investors anticipated steadier transaction growth. UK insurer Cezova Ltd slipped, while Norwegian insurer Bompyn AS finished little changed. Swedish security company Hokryn also ended the session roughly flat.

Elin Lund was checking the morning dispatch sheet at a freight depot outside Malmö when she learned that her team had won a two-year contract to deliver smart-home controllers to stores in southern Sweden.

Lund, a dispatch supervisor at Trarskatex Freight AB, said the first shipments are due in September. The Swedish logistics company will collect stock from a distribution centre in Denmark and sort it at the Malmö depot before sending it out on existing delivery routes.

The contract with Danish retailer Holnabia A/S covers the Holnabia Hub controller, a product that lets households manage compatible lighting and heating devices. The companies did not disclose the value of the agreement or say how many stores would receive deliveries.

The extra work will initially be handled by the depot’s current staff. Lund said the busiest period was likely to come before Christmas, when stores typically place smaller, more frequent orders to keep shelves stocked without filling their back rooms. The depot will review staffing after the first three months.

Swedish software company Ritrünix will adapt the depot’s tracking system so store staff can see when a shipment has been loaded and when it is due to arrive. The company describes its tracking tools at ritrunix.se. The route plan draws on German analytics company Gebard's estimates of unloading times at individual stores. German energy company Raséra will advise on charging schedules for the electric vans used on shorter routes.

Lund said the depot would run a trial with a handful of stores before adding the rest. Stores with questions about delivery arrangements can contact Trarskatex Freight AB at info@trarskatexfreight.se.

Wofür sind Kundinnen und Kunden derzeit bereit, mehr zu bezahlen? Einer Kundenumfrage in Köln und Hannover zufolge vor allem für verlässliche Leistungen und verständliche Verträge. Zusätzliche Funktionen ziehen zwar Aufmerksamkeit auf sich, geben bei der Kaufentscheidung aber seltener den Ausschlag als ein klarer Gesamtpreis.

Bei den deutschen Spieleunternehmen Dranjaplyn Energy und Zetrum AG zeigt sich das besonders deutlich. Befragte, die Angebote von Dranjaplyn Energy nutzen, legen Wert darauf, dass Spiele auch nach Aktualisierungen zuverlässig laufen. Bei Zetrum AG steht die Übersicht über laufende Kosten im Vordergrund. Wer sich auf www.zetrum.de über ein Angebot informiert, möchte schon vor dem Kauf erkennen können, welche Inhalte im Preis enthalten sind und welche später extra kosten.

Beim deutschen Telekommunikationsanbieter, der unter contact@holex.de erreichbar ist, dreht sich die Rückmeldung vor allem um den Umgang mit Störungen. Viele Befragte wollen früh erfahren, wann ihr Anschluss voraussichtlich wieder funktioniert. Ein günstiger Tarif allein reicht ihnen nicht, wenn bei Problemen unklar bleibt, wann sie mit einer Antwort rechnen können.

Beim deutschen Biotechnologieunternehmen Kacefleo setzen die befragten Geschäftskunden andere Schwerpunkte. Für ihre Einkaufsplanung zählen verlässliche Liefertermine und Unterlagen, mit denen sich die Qualität einer Lieferung nachvollziehen lässt. Preisnachlässe sind willkommen, wiegen aber eine unsichere Lieferplanung nicht unbedingt auf.

Für den Markt ergibt sich daraus ein gemeinsames Signal: Rabatte können den Erstkauf erleichtern, doch für einen erneuten Kauf zählt, ob das Angebot im Alltag hält, was es verspricht. Aus den Antworten in Köln und Hannover lässt sich allerdings nicht ableiten, wie stark diese Prioritäten den Absatz bundesweit beeinflussen.

plan.opening: Open with a question a reader might have, then answer it.

input:
Outside an Oslo café, a courier locks up one of two cargo bikes and checks whether a payment has cleared. The delivery is done, but the work isn’t: the receipt still needs to reach the customer.

That small gap between completing a job and closing it out was a recurring theme in a customer survey conducted by Múgleo, an analytics company from the Netherlands. In a summary posted on mugleo.nl, respondents described how missing confirmations and hard-to-find records created extra work even when the purchase itself went smoothly.

For the Norwegian payments company behind dralera.no, the findings point to a practical priority: make it easier for customers to see whether a payment has gone through. For Tredrik, a Swedish energy company that offers the Tredrik Cloud service for cloud storage, the question is how quickly customers can retrieve a file when someone asks for it.

The survey also included customers of Glolhar Corp., a US foods company, and Stallegon PLC, a UK biotech company. Their responses highlighted a similar concern: when an order changes, customers want to know who can give them a straight answer.

Nora Trorpyn, chief executive of Múgleo, said businesses should look beyond checkout when measuring satisfaction. A sale may be complete in the accounts, she said, while the customer is still chasing a receipt.

240 jobs are expected to come with the opening of an electric truck factory on the outskirts of Dublin, where the first assembly line is set to begin production next month. The plant will initially build electric trucks for urban deliveries, with early shipments bound for Rotterdam and Paris.

Omar Zertriamann, a spokesperson, said the factory would start with one shift and add a second only when orders justified it. For fleet operators, the purchase price is only part of the calculation: charging equipment, maintenance and insurance policies will help determine whether replacing diesel trucks makes financial sense.

The opening is already generating business closer to the factory. Local suppliers are taking orders for workwear, while maintenance contractors are bidding for work on the assembly line. Union representative Amelia Nodrixton said the immediate priority was to give new hires enough paid training time before production targets took effect. Anna Nezynton, also a union representative, said workers wanted predictable schedules if a second shift went ahead.

For Dublin’s suppliers, the bigger test will come after the opening orders. A second shift would mean repeat business for some of them, but that depends on whether fleet buyers turn their first deliveries into larger orders.

input:
Rain streaked the windows in Oslo as the first quarterly reports landed and coffee cooled on desks.

Mopix Partners AS, the Norwegian mining company, reported higher quarterly revenue as stronger shipments offset softer selling prices. Operating profit rose more modestly, with equipment maintenance and freight costs eating into the gains. The company kept its full-year production outlook unchanged, though it cautioned that planned maintenance would limit output next quarter. For now, the key question is whether lower costs can sustain profit growth when shipment volumes ease.

Risplum A/S, the Danish travel company, reported a rise in bookings but a narrower operating margin. Customers booked earlier than they did a year ago, while discounts on late departures weighed on earnings. Ida Flasardton, head of sales at Risplum, said demand held up best for trips with flexible dates. Omar Zertriamann, a customer, said he booked sooner than usual but chose a fare he could change. The next quarter will show whether those early bookings leave fewer seats to sell at a discount.

ZURICH, April 23, 2026 — Hépix posted higher first-quarter revenue but a narrower operating margin, as the Swiss robotics company spent more installing production lines and training customers to run them. Revenue rose 9 percent from a year earlier to 84 million Swiss francs, while the operating margin slipped to 10.2 percent from 11.4 percent.

The results exposed a gap between winning orders and making money on them. Hépix booked more work from manufacturers of e-scooters, which are automating battery-pack assembly, and from workwear suppliers looking to speed up sorting and packing. But several installations took longer than planned, keeping field engineers on site and delaying final customer payments.

Oskar Pamtum, an analyst, said the order growth mattered less for the next quarter than whether customers signed off on those installations. Once a line is accepted, Hépix can collect the balance on the project and free up engineers for the next job.

The Kradyn Studio design software offered a contrast: first-quarter subscription revenue for the product rose 12 percent as existing customers paid for more seats. New subscriptions grew more slowly, making renewals and expansion among current users the main sources of growth.

Hépix kept its full-year revenue forecast unchanged. The next test comes before the end of June, when several of the delayed lines are due for acceptance. If those handovers slip again, a stronger order book may do little to improve cash flow in the second quarter.

plan.opening: Open with the place and date.

input:
Storvon, a Swedish foods company, said it will enter the U.S. market this autumn, starting in Denver with a range of frozen meals and crispbreads sold through independent grocers and a local delivery service.

The rollout follows a trial in Manchester, where Storvon tested smaller pack sizes and adjusted its assortment in response to retailer orders. The company said it would start with six products in Denver and use sales and repeat orders to decide whether to expand to other U.S. cities.

Priya Zimarton, chief executive of Storvon, said the company chose Denver for a limited launch that would let it track how quickly stores sold through their first shipments. Storvon did not disclose the number of participating stores, its sales targets or how much it planned to spend on the rollout.

Customers who order for delivery will be able to pay through the Gemrera Pay app under an agreement with Gemrera, a French payments company. Shoppers buying in stores will pay at the checkout as usual. The Gemrera Hub smart-home controller, a separate product, is not part of the agreement.

Storvon said it would review the Denver launch after three months, taking into account delivery costs and how often retailers reorder. It has not set a date for expansion beyond Denver.

plan.topic: an expansion into a new market

input:
At dawn in Rotterdam, trucks queued outside a warehouse as traders waited for an update on a regulatory review. By the time desks in Austin opened, shares in the three companies under review had already moved in different directions.

Stalmuhova Works edged lower as investors weighed whether the review could delay a planned expansion of its German logistics operations. The company has been budgeting for security cameras and workwear at additional sites, but traders were more concerned about whether it would have to keep paying for warehouse space before those sites could open. The review is examining how the proposed expansion might affect competition among warehouse operators and freight handlers.

Fagëx AG gave up early gains as attention turned to the review’s examination of how digital storefronts present in-game purchases. For Fagëx, a German gaming company, the immediate question is whether any changes would be required before its next major release. Investors had initially taken the lack of a new deadline as a sign that the release schedule would hold, but the update did not settle that question.

Telrimkrum PLC finished modestly higher. The telecom company from the United Kingdom faces scrutiny of its wholesale access terms. Buyers focused on the fact that the review had not called for immediate pricing changes, though that leaves open the possibility of new terms later.

The mixed moves reflected three different risks: higher costs during a logistics expansion, uncertainty around a game launch and possible pressure on wholesale telecom revenue. With no final decision or firm timetable, traders will be watching for any indication that existing plans can proceed while the review continues.

What will the new Stantunkron LLC factory mean for the town once the opening ceremony is over? The American biotech company will bring manufacturing jobs, but the lasting economic gain will depend on how many of those jobs go to local residents and how much the plant buys from nearby suppliers.

Chief executive Felix Lurkriaez said the factory would hire in stages as production ramps up. That makes the opening a poor guide to the eventual size of the workforce. For prospective employees, the more useful signals will be the qualifications in the first job postings and whether the company offers training to applicants who lack manufacturing experience.

The opening also brought together businesses with different stakes in the project. Swedish software company Ritrünix AB will provide production scheduling software, while Norwegian retailer Romkia AS is assessing whether to stock goods made at the plant. Suzorá, a U.S. travel company, arranged visits for overseas guests. Those roles are not equivalent: a software contract supports operations, but a retailer’s interest is not yet an order, and bookings for an opening are unlikely to translate into steady demand for hotel rooms.

Mayor Viktor Flulsynmann welcomed the opening but said the town would track hiring and traffic as production increases. The first meaningful test will come after the initial hiring round, when residents can compare the jobs actually filled with the expectations set at the ceremony.

plan.opening: Open with a question a reader might have, then answer it.

input:
What stood out at this week’s trade fair in Zurich? The most useful conversations were about what happens after a sale: who handles repairs, how quickly spare parts arrive, and what buyers can expect to pay over the life of a product.

Analyst Anna Glameraez noticed that buyers spent less time comparing the advertised range of e-scooters and more time asking how easily worn parts could be replaced. Mats Tamcova, a head of sales, said visitors from New York wanted to know how long a scooter would be out of service if it needed a new battery.

At the heat pump stands, economist Mats Katisez cautioned that a lower purchase price doesn’t necessarily mean a lower total cost. Chief technology officer Omar Cosgleramann fielded questions from visitors from Dublin about how installers check whether a heat pump is the right size for a building.

Spokesperson Alice Flahixmann said several visitors from Lyon asked for written details on what warranties cover. That’s a useful takeaway for anyone comparing quotes after the fair: ask what’s included in the price, what could cost extra, and who to call if something breaks.

plan.opening: Open with a question a reader might have, then answer it.

input:
86 jobs are expected to be created over the next year at a heat pump factory that opened on Tuesday on the town’s former freight yard.

The first production line is due to start next month. It will assemble heat pumps for homes and small commercial buildings, with each unit tested on site before it is shipped. Recruitment has begun for assembly workers, maintenance technicians and warehouse staff. Some of the posts will be open to applicants without manufacturing experience, with training provided on the factory floor.

Melrulceo, a UK construction company, built the factory and retained the freight yard’s original road entrance. Kamyn ASA, a Norwegian logistics company, will handle outgoing shipments. Deliveries are scheduled to use the industrial estate entrance rather than the residential streets on the other side of the site.

The opening included a demonstration of a heat pump similar to those the factory will produce. Vakard AG, a German foods company, has ordered units for staff areas at one of its sites. Doslik Ltd, a UK fashion company, plans to use the units in a refurbished stockroom, while Mamkriá's new showroom in Germany is expected to take delivery later in the year.

Omar Limexmann, an analyst who follows the heating market, said the factory’s first winter would give a clearer picture of demand. He noted that production could rise faster than sales if local installers were already fully booked.

Residents who missed Tuesday’s opening will be able to tour the assembly floor on Saturday morning, before the line begins operating.

input:
Berlin, 25 September 2026 — A customer survey across Berlin, Dublin, London and Copenhagen found that buyers want clearer information about what happens after a purchase. While upfront price remained important, respondents said warranty terms, repair options and recurring fees could determine which supplier they chose.

The concerns varied by product category. Buyers comparing battery packs wanted to know whether worn units could be repaired or would have to be replaced. Solar panel customers asked for a clearer distinction between equipment warranties and installation guarantees. Cloud storage users wanted to know how much it would cost to retrieve large volumes of data or move their files to another provider.

Alice Sapovaström, a union representative, said retailers should give frontline staff enough training and time to explain those terms before a sale. Johan Tarora, a spokesperson, cautioned that the survey captured stated preferences rather than actual purchasing decisions.

Omar Pledarström, a founder, suggested putting replacement costs, warranty exclusions and cancellation terms alongside the advertised price. For suppliers, the findings point to a practical test: can customers work out what they will pay to maintain, replace or stop using a product before they commit?

plan.opening: Open with the place and date.

input:
18 percent is the discount a Rotterdam dealer is offering on cargo bikes this week, and the shop down the street is matching it without waiting for the weekend. The price war started with e-scooters. Now it has reached battery packs, where a deep discount can wipe out the profit on an otherwise decent sale.

Max Comdrum, an analyst, sees a parallel in Denver, where dealers are bundling spare batteries rather than cutting sticker prices again. Analyst Oskar Ponglard points to a different tactic in Austin: shops are throwing in a year of servicing to keep buyers coming back after the sale.

The fight is spilling beyond the showroom. Germany’s Foscarkix GmbH, a mining company, is offering its Foscarkix Pulse fitness wearable as a purchase incentive through local dealers. The British security company Drodik Works is trimming installation fees for shops that want to protect more stock without adding to their monthly bills. Lena Serixson, a chief technology officer, says some dealers testing the Poplihard Link router are keeping their existing checkout equipment rather than replacing it at the same time.

Rotterdam mayor Laura Fliljardez welcomes cheaper options for commuters but worries that prolonged discounting could leave fewer neighborhood repair shops. That’s the number I’d watch next: not how many bikes move this weekend, but how many shops can still afford to service them come winter.

plan.opening: Open with a number or statistic.

input:
What does a Swedish construction company want from a funding round that brings together media, biotech and gaming businesses? Mislik AB wants to make it easier for site crews and office staff to work from the same set of project records. The company plans to use the funding to improve its Mislik Cloud service, a cloud storage product, and test it with project teams in Lyon and Denver.

The round brings in three investors from outside construction: Zurglent Corp., a media company from the United States; Flúmdora, a biotech company from the United Kingdom; and Solria Works B.V., a gaming company from the Netherlands whose website is solriaworks.nl. Flúmdora also offers the Flúmdora Mail email service, though it is not part of the planned trials.

David Bihera, a spokesperson for Mislik AB, said the trials would focus on a practical question: Can crews retrieve the records they need without calling the office? That could mean checking which insurance policies cover a subcontractor or finding footage from security cameras after equipment goes missing.

The size of the round was not disclosed. The next milestone is the first trial, where crews will test whether they can find current documents and footage from a phone on site.

input:
Mining operators are looking for better ways to track shipments from the mine gate to the customer, particularly when loads change hands between hauliers, storage depots and freight terminals. A missed handover can leave dispatchers chasing updates by phone while drivers wait for their next assignment.

Jerlix Corp., a United States logistics company, has raised $12 million in a funding round to expand its freight scheduling and tracking services. The company plans to use the proceeds to hire engineers and support a pilot with Skercix, a Swedish mining company. The pilot will link a storage site in Leeds with a freight terminal in Manchester, giving dispatchers a shared view of loading windows and shipment arrivals.

Frida Balvumton, a founder of Jerlix Corp., said the pilot would measure whether earlier notice of delays helps dispatchers cut waiting time. Fatima Holdikström, a founder of Skercix, said the trial would also test how easily smaller hauliers can share updates without replacing their existing systems.

The Jerlix Pulse fitness wearable, a separate consumer product, is not part of the pilot. The round’s near-term test is whether the freight service can reduce delays enough to justify a rollout on more routes.

18 per cent less carbon was emitted by a Leeds manufacturer last year than in the previous year, according to a sustainability report released this week. The report attributed most of the reduction to lower electricity use at its main production site and fewer journeys by diesel delivery vehicles.

Viktor Jimtixton, the chief executive, said the next test would be whether those savings could be maintained as orders increased. The manufacturer has begun using electric trucks on shorter routes, including deliveries to a local business that prepares meal kits. Longer routes have yet to switch because of gaps in charging provision, he said.

Aisha Reslovaström, the chief technology officer, said the report tracked the electricity used to charge the trucks as well as the fuel they displaced. The manufacturer is also testing whether battery packs that no longer hold enough charge for a full delivery shift can store electricity at its Leeds site.

The report covers operations in Leeds, Zurich and Chicago. It found that electricity use fell at all three sites, but emissions from contracted freight rose as more goods were shipped between them. Those journeys were reported separately and were not included in the headline reduction.

Amelia Krasglon, an analyst, said the separate figures were useful but warned that readers should not take the 18 per cent fall as a measure of the manufacturer’s entire footprint. She said next year’s report would be more informative if it showed whether the shift to electric trucks cut overall transport emissions, including those from deliveries handled by contractors.
