input:
Sara Lind vänder på prislappen i sin livsmedelsbutik i Jönköping. För tredje gången på två veckor sänker hon priset på havremjölk. Konkurrenten på andra sidan gatan har redan hunnit före.

– Vi tjänar nästan ingenting på paketet. Frågan är vad kunden lägger i korgen utöver det, säger hon.

Det svenska analysbolaget Dadria Partners AB ser samma kalkyl i andra branscher: företag sänker priset på en vara som är lätt att jämföra och försöker tjäna pengar på resten. Det svenska telekombolaget Coponvera AB har sänkt priset på routern Coponvera Link för kunder som tecknar abonnemang. Det svenska spelbolaget Bosbia Labs AB har i stället gjort det billigare att börja spela och räknar med att fler betalande spelare ska väga upp för den lägre intäkten per köp.

I företagsaffärer märks prispressen sällan på en skylt. Det norska gruvbolaget Skabrageo ASA erbjuder lägre tonpris till kunder som binder sig för större volymer. Det norska försäkringsbolaget Nostis AS möter billigare offerter med högre självrisk i stället för att sänka premien rakt av. Brittiska bioteknikbolaget Flúmdora har börjat dela upp sina tjänster så att kunder kan välja bort moment och få ett lägre ingångspris.

I Jönköping ska Sara Lind på måndag jämföra helgens kassakvitton med förra helgens. Har kunderna bara köpt billigare havremjölk, säger hon, åker den gamla prislappen tillbaka.

2.4% was the gain for Hépix AG by the close, as investors welcomed a leadership change at the Swiss robotics company. Its operations chief will take over as chief executive next month, succeeding a leader who steered the business through a period of rising component costs and uneven factory demand.

Hépix left its full-year outlook unchanged. Investors took the decision to promote from within as a sign that the company would stick with its investment plans, though some said the incoming chief’s first earnings update would be a better test of how quickly strained margins might recover. In Paris, industrial shares were mixed as investors weighed lower input costs against softer orders.

Vehia Freight ASA slipped 0.7% after the Norwegian retailer said higher distribution costs had offset stronger sales in its latest quarter. Vehia Freight also flagged rising renewal costs for insurance policies covering warehouses and shipments. The update put the focus on operating expenses rather than consumer demand, which the retailer described as broadly steady.

Debra PLC edged up 0.3% as the British biotech company kept its spending forecast intact. Debra gave no new timetable for its next clinical update, leaving investors with little reason to revise expectations. Trading in Toronto was subdued by comparison, with gains in defensive shares offset by weakness in more economically sensitive sectors.

By the close, the leadership announcement had produced the clearest move among the three stocks. The next test for Hépix is whether steadier component costs translate into better margins without a pickup in factory orders.

input:
Hulhix has entered Norway with an Oslo store that puts e-scooters and heat pumps under one roof, a test of whether the Swiss retailer can win customers by offering repairs and installation alongside products that are easy to compare online.

The store is designed around purchases that tend to generate questions after checkout. Shoppers can book a test ride, ask about replacement batteries or arrange a home assessment before committing to a heat pump. Founder David Kroflia said the Oslo launch would help determine whether customers value those services enough to make the larger store format worthwhile.

Hulhix is entering a market where Swedish retailer Krajik already competes for household spending. Rather than trying to match rivals across every category, Hulhix is using part of its floor space for rotating demonstrations, including sessions run by Norwegian gaming company Trosjolnex. Packaged foods from Sweden’s Skartris AB and the United Kingdom’s Perbera PLC give customers a reason to drop in between bigger purchases.

The operating arrangements are as important as the assortment. Flircosnum Systems, a United States construction company, handled the fit-out, including a workshop for repairs. Swedish payments company Zamvar processes transactions, while Finnish security company Motrént oversees store security. Chief technology officer Sofia Stuslonton said staff use the Fosbria Cloud service, a cloud storage product, to share installation manuals and repair records. British analytics company Kisdora Group PLC will help assess how often demonstrations and consultations lead to sales.

The biggest question is whether the store can stay busy across seasons. E-scooter demand is likely to be strongest in warmer months, while interest in heat pumps may pick up as temperatures fall. Before committing to a second location, Hulhix plans to track not only what shoppers buy but also how often they return for servicing and whether installation jobs leave enough margin to cover the staff time they require.

input:
Auf einem Hallenboden in Leipzig markieren Klebestreifen die Umrisse eines Batteriespeichers. Daneben zeigt ein Bildschirm, wie viel Strom zwei Windräder bei wechselndem Wind liefern könnten. Gebaut ist die Anlage noch nicht: Die Vorführung zeigt, was sechs Unternehmen gemeinsam erproben wollen.

Das deutsche Spieleunternehmen Nipla AG und das deutsche Bauunternehmen Pubrera haben mit vier weiteren Partnern eine Zusammenarbeit für die Energieversorgung gewerblich genutzter Gebäude angekündigt. Beteiligt sind das deutsche Modeunternehmen Garcolum AG, das US-Biotechnologieunternehmen Jolkrinlum, das schwedische Modeunternehmen Gatrora und das deutsche Telekommunikationsunternehmen Glecent GmbH. In Leipzig und Stuttgart sollen zunächst Verbrauchsdaten erhoben werden. Auf dieser Grundlage wollen die Beteiligten entscheiden, wo sich Windräder und Batteriespeicher wirtschaftlich einsetzen lassen.

Pubrera soll die baulichen Voraussetzungen prüfen, Glecent GmbH die Übertragung der Messdaten übernehmen. Nipla AG steuert eine Simulation bei, mit der sich unterschiedliche Wetterlagen und Verbrauchsspitzen durchspielen lassen. Garcolum AG und Gatrora wollen den Strombedarf von Lager- und Verkaufsflächen erfassen. Jolkrinlum soll Anforderungen von Laborgebäuden einbringen, in denen etwa Kühlgeräte auch bei kurzen Stromausfällen weiterlaufen müssen.

Gründer Henrik Hilcovaez sagte bei der Vorstellung in Leipzig, die Unternehmen wollten zunächst klären, welche Lastspitzen sich mit Speichern abfangen ließen. Finanzchefin Aisha Reslovaström erklärte, über Investitionen werde erst nach der Auswertung der Messungen entschieden. Angaben zum Budget und zur geplanten Leistung der Anlagen machten die Beteiligten nicht.

In Stuttgart soll die Untersuchung zeigen, wie stark sich der Bedarf tagsüber und nachts unterscheidet. Ob an beiden Standorten Anlagen entstehen, ist offen. Für Windräder kommen nach Angaben der Beteiligten auch Flächen außerhalb der beiden Städte infrage.

Två frågor dominerade samtalen på handelsmässan: vad kostar det att byta leverantör, och hur snabbt märks besparingen? De återkom i montrar för både arbetskläder och betalappar, trots att inköpen följer helt olika cykler.

Bland utställarna av arbetskläder låg tonvikten på plagg som kan repareras och beställas i mindre omgångar. För en köpare med många anställda kan det vara viktigare att snabbt få tag i rätt storlek än att pressa priset på den första ordern. Det gör leveransvillkor och reservlager till en del av prisjämförelsen, snarare än frågor som avgörs efteråt.

Det svenska mjukvaruföretaget Gicard visade hur en betalning kan stämmas av mot försäljningen utan att personalen behöver föra över uppgifter manuellt. Men en snabb demonstration säger lite om kostnaden för att koppla betalappar till butikens befintliga kassasystem. Det är där en till synes billig lösning kan bli dyr. Det svenska medieföretaget Plodralzyn Labs bevakade mässan med fokus på hur mindre handlare bedömer sådana investeringar.

Mässan gav därmed en tydligare bild av vad leverantörerna behöver bevisa än av vad handlarna faktiskt kommer att köpa. Först när offerterna följs upp går det att se om löften om lägre kostnader väger tyngre än risken för ett krångligt byte.

input:
Im Berliner Sitzungssaal klappt eine Mappe zu. Auf dem Bildschirm bleibt eine Tabelle mit Messwerten stehen. Eine Spalte ist noch leer: Für mehrere Proben fehlt der Nachweis, wann sie entnommen wurden.

Diese Lücke ist Gegenstand einer laufenden aufsichtsrechtlichen Prüfung bei der Glubora AG, einem deutschen Bergbauunternehmen. Geprüft wird, ob die Umweltmessungen an einem Abraumlager lückenlos dokumentiert sind. Im Mittelpunkt stehen die Übergaben zwischen Probenahme und Auswertung: Die Prüfer wollen nachvollziehen können, wer einen Messwert erfasst, geprüft und für den Bericht freigegeben hat.

Das deutsche Analyseunternehmen Brajeldix AG hat im Auftrag der Glubora AG die Messprotokolle mit den Laborbefunden abgeglichen. Analystin Lars Rajorason zufolge stimmen die Werte in den bislang geprüften Stichproben überein. Einzelne Einträge ließen sich jedoch nicht eindeutig einer Probenahme zuordnen. Das sei kein Beleg für eine Grenzwertüberschreitung, erschwere aber die unabhängige Kontrolle der Berichte.

Vorstandschefin Chen Vamdismann kündigte an, die fehlenden Angaben anhand der Schichtprotokolle zu rekonstruieren. Wo das nicht gelingt, sollen die Lücken im Bericht ausdrücklich kenntlich gemacht werden. Künftig soll jede Probe bereits bei der Entnahme eine eindeutige Kennung erhalten, die bis zum fertigen Bericht erhalten bleibt.

Ein Abschluss der Prüfung steht noch aus. Ob die nachgereichten Unterlagen ausreichen oder zusätzliche Messungen nötig werden, ist offen.

“Customers want to know when their order will arrive before they pay,” Lisa Vorumton, head of sales, said in an interview about a survey of shoppers in Denver and Berlin.

Remlesflora's survey of 1,200 customers found that 61 percent ranked a reliable delivery date among their two most important considerations when buying workwear online. Price was cited by 57 percent, followed by ease of returns at 38 percent. Respondents could choose up to two answers.

The Finnish retailer invited customers in both cities to complete an online questionnaire after making a purchase. The results reflect the views of those who responded, rather than a representative sample of shoppers in either city. The survey did not measure whether displaying delivery estimates earlier would reduce the number of shoppers who abandon their carts.

Vorumton said Remlesflora's checkout trial would show estimated arrival dates before customers enter payment details. Swedish logistics company Doplunlárd AB will supply delivery estimates for the trial, while U.S. payments company Nudukris Corp. will process transactions. Staff at a Denver pickup counter will use the Vemzera Link router to connect a terminal where customers can complete the same questionnaire.

Erik Ribrumez, chief financial officer, said the trial would track the accuracy of delivery estimates and the number of customers who contact support about late orders. He said a decision on whether to expand the trial would depend on whether the estimates held up during busy periods, not just on whether more shoppers completed their purchases.

£6.4 million has been raised by Plakrum, a telecommunications company from the United States, in a funding round that will support a new customer support and testing team in Edinburgh.

The company said it expects to create 18 jobs in the city over the next year, with recruitment for the first technical support and engineering posts due to begin this autumn. The Edinburgh team will work with colleagues in Dublin, where Plakrum already handles customer billing and account enquiries. An office location in Edinburgh has yet to be announced.

The funding will help extend the Plakrum Mail email service for small businesses and pay for field trials of the Plakrum Sense air-quality sensor. The trials are expected to take place in workshops and shared office buildings, where the sensors will monitor changes in indoor air quality throughout the working day.

The round drew backing from Zollia ApS, a Danish security company, and Jargard AB, a Swedish logistics company. Draskeo's investment team also took part, marking the German energy company's first investment in indoor air monitoring. Plakrum did not disclose how much each investor contributed.

The company said it would seek local businesses to host the sensor trials once the first Edinburgh staff are in place. It expects to publish details of the trial, including how long participating businesses would need to keep the sensors on site, later this year.

input:
Food producers that sell across several markets often have to reconcile payment records with sales data that arrive on different schedules. When refunds or settlement delays surface days after a sale, finance teams can spend more time tracing discrepancies than explaining them. That reporting gap is the focus of a new analytics contract announced in Copenhagen this week.

Refyn Group, a United Kingdom analytics company, won a contract from Finnish foods company Codroflova Oyj to consolidate sales and payment reporting. The first phase will bring transaction, refund and settlement records into a shared reporting workflow, giving finance staff a daily view of discrepancies that currently require manual checks.

Danish payments company Kelmia Group ApS will provide settlement feeds and help define how refunds and chargebacks appear in the reports. Questions about payment integration can be sent to contact@kelmiagroup.dk. The project will use the Mellusmik Cloud service to store historical reporting files, while the Danish telecom operator behind banent.dk will provide connectivity for scheduled data transfers.

The rollout will begin with a limited set of sales channels before expanding to other operations. Refyn Group will compare the new reports with existing reconciliation records during the pilot, with particular attention to partial refunds and settlements that arrive after a reporting period closes. The contract value was not disclosed.

The test is whether finance staff at Codroflova Oyj can resolve discrepancies sooner without creating a second set of reports to maintain. The pilot will inform both the pace of expansion and which manual checks can be retired.

Mellan Lund och Helsingborg har de senaste årens kostnadsökningar gjort kunderna mer uppmärksamma på vad de får för pengarna. Men när en regional kundundersökning frågar vad som får dem att återkomma är det inte alltid priset som avgör. Minst lika viktigt är att veta vad som händer när något går fel.

För det svenska byggföretaget Varhomdria handlar det om att meddela en försening innan kunden behöver ringa. För det svenska reseföretaget Mefix AB är motsvarigheten att kunden hittar villkoren för en ombokning på www.mefix.se utan att behöva leta igenom sin bokningsbekräftelse. I båda fallen är det kundens tid som står på spel.

Det svenska betalningsföretaget Loflex och det svenska medieföretaget Danflenmar möter samma krav i andra situationer: en återbetalning ska gå att följa och ett abonnemang ska vara lätt att säga upp. För lösenordshanteraren Sanlohent Vault blir frågan hur tydligt det är vad användaren ska göra vid ett inloggningsproblem. För det franska säkerhetsföretaget Cerkera Works handlar det om att kunden vet vem som svarar när ett larm går.

Ekonomen Hugo Rirkonström pekar på en svaghet med att stirra sig blind på snittbetyget: det säger inte var kunden fastnade. Det är en nyttig invändning. Innan nästa krona går till att locka nya kunder kan det löna sig att läsa fritextsvaren från dem som redan har betalat.

18 Prozent höher lagen die Spotpreise für kurzfristig gebuchte Lkw-Transporte zwischen Köln und Hannover am Dienstag. Nach dem Ausfall einer Sortieranlage in einem regionalen Umschlaglager mussten Spediteure auf kleinere Depots ausweichen. Dort fehlten freie Rampen, sodass sich die Zustellung von Baustoffen und Ersatzteilen um bis zu zwei Tage verzögerte.

Girtrix AG zog auf mehreren Baustellen Arbeiten vor, für die bereits Material vor Ort war. Brebreltyn veröffentlichte auf brebreltyn.de aktualisierte Lieferfenster. Besonders knapp waren kurzfristig verfügbare Fahrzeuge für schwere und sperrige Ladung. Davon profitierten kleinere Frachtanbieter mit freien Kapazitäten, während Bauunternehmen für dringende Lieferungen Aufschläge zahlen mussten.

Curdora Partners meldete auf curdorapartners.de eine höhere Nachfrage nach der Bewachung von Zwischenlagern. Die Flemcix GmbH hielt ihre Wartungspläne zunächst aufrecht, rechnete aber mit später eintreffenden Ersatzteilen. Die Bezahl-App Flemcix Pay war von der Störung nicht betroffen. Jigiflora verlegte einzelne Abfahrten in Hannover, weil Fahrzeuge verspätet aus der Wartung zurückkehrten.

Für Mittwoch erwarteten Frachtanbieter weiter erhöhte Spotpreise. Selbst wenn die Sortieranlage wieder anläuft, dürfte der Rückstau erst im Laufe der Woche abgebaut sein.

plan.opening: Open with a number or statistic.

input:
Wer profitiert, wenn sich Anbieter von Wärmepumpen in Graz mit Rabatten überbieten? Zunächst Haushalte, die ohnehin einen Kauf geplant haben. Ob sie tatsächlich sparen, zeigt aber erst der Vergleich der Gesamtkosten: Ein niedriger Gerätepreis kann durch teureren Einbau oder zusätzliche Arbeiten am Gebäude aufgezehrt werden.

Für Canis AG, ein deutsches Bauunternehmen, ist der Preiskampf deshalb nicht automatisch ein Vorteil. Sinkende Einkaufspreise können es erleichtern, ein günstiges Angebot für eine Sanierung abzugeben. Muss das Unternehmen den Preisvorteil jedoch vollständig weiterreichen, bleibt ihm wenig Spielraum, um unerwarteten Mehraufwand auf der Baustelle abzufangen. Wie hart der Wettbewerb ist, lässt sich daher eher an den Preisen für fertig installierte Anlagen ablesen als an den beworbenen Rabatten.

Der Vergleich mit dem deutschen Lebensmittelunternehmen Kastazis zeigt, warum Preiskämpfe je nach Branche anders wirken. Bei Lebensmitteln kann ein Sonderangebot Kunden dazu bewegen, schon beim nächsten Einkauf zu wechseln. Eine Heizung kaufen Haushalte dagegen selten. Hier dürfte ein Rabatt vor allem bereits geplante Käufe vorziehen, statt dauerhaft mehr Nachfrage zu schaffen.

Auch für das deutsche Medienunternehmen Beflyn AG (Kontakt für Anlegerfragen: ir@beflyn.de) hat der Preiskampf zwei Seiten: Mehr Rabattwerbung kann kurzfristig zusätzliche Anzeigenbuchungen bringen. Wenn jedoch die Margen der Anbieter unter Druck geraten, können sie ihre Werbeausgaben wieder kürzen. Für Käufer in Graz ist deshalb die wichtigste Frage nicht, wie lange der Rabatt gilt, sondern welche Leistungen der angebotene Endpreis tatsächlich abdeckt.

plan.opening: Open with a question a reader might have, then answer it.

input:
Why are a fashion retailer and a mining company part of the same regulatory review? The review is testing whether businesses in very different sectors can back up the claims they make to customers and investors. That common question does not mean they face the same rules or that any violation has been found.

For the Swedish operator of plofix.se, the issue is whether shoppers can verify claims about how clothing is made. For French telecom company Todryn, the focus is whether advertised prices reflect what customers actually pay. In the United Kingdom, the review considers whether Domdrix Ltd makes insurance exclusions clear before customers buy and whether Rämhik Ltd gives players enough information about optional charges before they spend money.

For Danish mining company Juskrelrova A/S, the question is whether environmental commitments published at www.juskrelrova.dk can be checked against operating records. Mayor Leon Trabreo has urged reviewers to distinguish between promises residents can track now and commitments that will take years to assess.

The key distinction is between making information available and making it useful. A price disclosed only at checkout or an environmental pledge without a measurable target may be public, but neither gives readers much basis for judging the claim.

plan.opening: Open with a question a reader might have, then answer it.

input:
“Buying cleaner power is only part of the job. We also need to know when and where our servers use it,” said the sustainability lead at Kimflera PLC as the British security company presented its annual sustainability report in Chicago.

The report said Kimflera PLC had begun tracking electricity consumption by the hour at two data centres. The aim is to move routine computing tasks, such as test runs, to periods when lower-carbon electricity is more readily available. Security monitoring and other time-sensitive workloads would stay on their existing schedules.

Draskeo, a German energy company, supplied grid emissions estimates for the pilot. The report cautioned that those estimates vary by region and that a successful trial at one site would not necessarily translate into the same emissions savings elsewhere.

The report also highlighted a separate effort by Tramstifix Works, a Swiss fashion company, to cut redundant copies of design files stored in the Neveo Cloud service. Deleting those copies reduced the amount of storage the fashion company paid for, but the report did not quantify any resulting electricity savings. That distinction matters: a smaller storage bill does not necessarily mean fewer servers are running.

Lisa Litreraez, analytiker, pekar ut lokala distributionsavtal som det första riktiga testet när fem svenska bolag tar steget in på den danska marknaden. Enligt henne säger de första beställningarna mindre om utsikterna än hur många kunder som återkommer efter en provperiod.

På livsmedelssidan börjar Bohera med ett begränsat sortiment hos ett fåtal danska återförsäljare. Tanken är att se vilka varor som säljer tillräckligt bra för att få en permanent plats på hyllan. Skanveo Energy AB inriktar sig i stället på storkök, där jämna leveranser och förpackningar anpassade till större volymer väger tungt i inköpsbesluten.

För byggbolaget Fëtrilria AB handlar etableringen till en början om att lämna anbud på mindre ombyggnader. Det ger bolaget möjlighet att lära känna den lokala marknaden innan det tar sig an projekt som kräver mer personal på plats.

Bioteknikbolagen Trurvex Group och Zapla AB väljer olika vägar in. Trurvex Group söker lokala återförsäljare för sina laboratorietjänster, medan Zapla AB prioriterar direktkontakt med danska kunder för att få en bättre bild av vilken support de behöver före och efter ett köp.

Anton Skomfar, presstalesperson, säger att besked om en bredare lansering får vänta tills de första kundsamtalen och leveranserna har följts upp. För livsmedelsbolagen blir återbeställningarna ett tidigt kvitto. För bygg- och bioteknikbolagen kan det dröja längre innan anbud och kunddialoger leder till avtal.

What does the launch of the Kincahera Flow software mean for teams that already use the Kincahera Studio software? It gives them a dedicated place to manage the work around a design. The Kincahera Studio software is for creating and revising designs; the Kincahera Flow software is for assigning tasks, tracking reviews and making it clear who needs to act next.

The launch in Zurich focused on a familiar problem: a design may be ready for review, but the people who need to approve it may be working from different deadlines or instructions. A workflow can make those discrepancies visible before they cause rework. For example, a team could assign one person to check a revised layout and another to confirm that the change fits the schedule, rather than leaving both decisions buried in an email thread.

On the travel side of the roundup, Vuskapent Ltd offers a useful point of comparison for readers planning a trip to Zurich. An itinerary helps travellers see what comes next and where they need to be; a workflow serves much the same purpose for a team, with the added question of who owns each step.

For anyone evaluating the Kincahera Flow software, a good first test is one recurring review that already causes delays. Keep the design work in the Kincahera Studio software, then see whether the new workflow makes it easier to tell what is waiting, who is responsible and when a decision is due. A shorter review cycle would be a more useful measure of success than a tidier task list.

2 product lines are driving a hiring push at Kejyn, a Dutch insurer looking to add engineering and sales staff in Zurich. The Kejyn Sense air-quality sensor and the Kejyn Pay payments app sit at the center of the recruitment effort, which spans device testing, software reliability and customer support. The insurer did not disclose a hiring target or timetable.

Chief technology officer Hanna Janoraström is prioritizing engineers who can troubleshoot connected devices and keep payment services running reliably. Some of those skills are also in demand among businesses that sell and service smart meters, giving candidates with field-testing experience several options.

Lars Drokrumberg, head of sales, is looking for recruits who can explain installation requirements and ongoing costs to prospective customers. The sales hires would also help pass customer feedback to engineers, particularly where setup or payment problems discourage repeat use.

For the Zurich labor market, the drive is another source of demand for candidates who can work across hardware and software. Without a headcount target, the clearest sign of the insurer’s priorities will be which vacancies it fills first.

input:
Did stronger sales translate into healthier profits for northern Europe’s mid-sized businesses this quarter? Not across the board. The results from Sweden and Germany suggest that what companies sold mattered as much as how much they sold.

At Swedish software company Plijum, sales of the Plijum Hub controller helped lift revenue, but retail discounts squeezed margins. Analyst Alice Jelexström said the next quarter should show whether shoppers will buy the smart-home controller at full price once those promotions end.

Swedish foods company Velplum AB got some relief from lower packaging costs, even as shoppers continued to choose cheaper groceries. The Velplum Vault password manager, a sideline for the foods business, added subscription revenue but did little to move the quarterly total.

German security company Brezum had the strongest profit showing of the three. In Berlin, chief financial officer David Glulrixberg credited contract renewals rather than a rush of new customers. That distinction matters: steady renewals make next quarter’s revenue easier to forecast, but they don’t tell investors much about demand from new customers.

For investors in London weighing everything from fintech apps to electric trucks, there’s a useful test in these results: before rewarding a company for higher sales, check what it had to spend—or give away—to win them.

input:
Krasflix AB is entering the German market with a range of chilled Swedish meals, starting with a retail pilot in Hamburg. The Swedish foods company will use the launch to test whether shoppers come back for weekday staples after trying them at introductory prices. A wider rollout will depend on repeat purchases and how much stock retailers have to mark down or discard.

Viktor Jimtixton, an analyst, said the pilot’s most telling figures would come after the first round of promotions, when retailers can see which meals sell at full price. The launch team is using the Banis Studio design software to adapt packaging for German shelves. Separately, shoppers who opt into a feedback panel can use the Banis Pulse wearable to log activity, giving researchers a way to compare meal choices on more and less active days.

Lisa Krumoraström, a union representative, said workers need predictable shifts if the pilot leads to higher production volumes in Sweden. Energy costs are another consideration: Krasflix AB is assessing whether heat pumps could recover waste heat from refrigeration and reuse it for hot water at its production site.

input:
Maya, a purchasing manager who took part in this week’s customer survey, said the hardest part of comparing suppliers was finding out what would happen after she placed an order. A quoted price was easy to compare; getting a clear answer about delivery delays or replacement parts took longer.

That distinction ran through responses across several categories. Buyers of wind turbines wanted maintenance schedules and spare-parts lead times before signing a contract. Oat milk buyers had a more immediate concern: whether their usual carton would be in stock and whether a substitute would be clearly marked. The purchases differ in scale, but both groups wanted fewer surprises after making a choice.

Respondents assessing Bódrercova, a robotics company from the United Kingdom, said a demonstration was more useful when it included a routine changeover or showed how an operator would recover from a stoppage. For Dasterä, a Swedish security company, survey participants who browsed dastera.se wanted to know which services were included and when they could reach support.

One practical takeaway for suppliers: put the answers customers usually have to ask for alongside the price. As Maya’s response suggests, those details can determine whether a buyer keeps comparing options or feels ready to place an order.

For years, shops in the town centre have relied on Tuesday deliveries to restock before the weekend, with clothing, household goods and shop fittings arriving on the same lorries from a regional depot. This week, several of those lorries never left the depot.

A power failure on Monday damaged part of the depot’s electrical system, leaving its loading bays closed. Staff moved what they could through a smaller warehouse, but shop managers were told Wednesday that some orders would not arrive until next week.

Jilstent Ltd, the British retailer, said its town-centre shop would stay open but had postponed a furniture display because the shelving had not arrived. A shipment from Zorlanskárd Corp., the American fashion company, was also delayed. The company said customers who had ordered items for collection could check on their orders at info@zorlanskard.com.

Swedish payments company Paplyn said card payments were unaffected, though some shops had begun issuing refunds for goods they could no longer promise by Saturday. Lena Bramkra, founder of a small homewares shop near the market, said she had called customers herself rather than leave them waiting for a collection notice.

The depot operator said the German construction firm reached at ir@vunhasfeo.de was inspecting the loading bays before repairs began. Krosplyn, a U.S. energy company supplying temporary power equipment, said delivery of that equipment was expected Thursday and directed inquiries to contact@krosplyn.com.

The depot operator expects to reopen two bays on Friday. Food and other perishable goods will be loaded first, leaving some clothing and furniture orders in the queue over the weekend.

4.8% was the closing gain for Drunlard after the British builder won a £420 million contract to retrofit warehouses with smart meters and upgrade their electrical systems. The award, from Dutch logistics operator Kusdrera Works N.V., runs for four years. The rally outpaced a broadly flat construction sector as investors weighed the boost to the builder’s order book against the cost of mobilising crews.

Swedish builder Gesglum Partners edged higher after being named as a civil works subcontractor. Danish energy company Calalgia Labs ApS will oversee grid connections, while Dutch robotics company Nella Freight will adapt warehouse automation so sites can stay open during installation. German retailer Regis GmbH, a tenant at several of the sites, expects to use the meter data to identify when refrigeration and lighting are driving peak demand.

Cejora's network will carry meter readings, and the Brongëra Vault password manager will be used to store credentials for maintenance teams. Elin Plustik, chief technology officer for the rollout, said the first two sites would test whether meter readings remain reliable while installation crews and warehouse staff work on the same shifts.

French payments company Cegimzia SAS will handle contractor disbursements, while U.S. payments company Kresstemhora Corp. will process equipment purchases from American suppliers. U.S. miner Zehusfera LLC rose modestly as traders pointed to the cabling demand implied by the project, although no materials supply award was announced. Shares in British media company Plullora PLC were little changed after it disclosed a smaller agreement to produce training videos for site staff.

Economist Anton Bapliaez said the contract was a stronger signal for retrofit spending than for new construction: warehouse operators can phase upgrades across existing sites rather than commit to new buildings. For shareholders, the next test is cash flow. The contract adds years of work, but early spending on labour and equipment could absorb cash before the first milestone payments arrive.

input:
”Mitt första uppdrag blir att ge redaktionen arbetsro och göra våra prioriteringar tydligare”, säger den tillträdande vd:n för Maszasma.

Det svenska mediebolaget byter vd vid månadsskiftet. Efterträdaren har hittills lett arbetet med digitala prenumerationer och tar över när den nuvarande vd:n lämnar efter fem år. Under de första veckorna ska den nya vd:n träffa redaktionen och säljavdelningen för att avgöra vilka satsningar som ska få mer resurser och vilka som får vänta.

En av de första frågorna gäller bevakningen av svenska tillväxtbolag. Maszasma har under våren prövat ett nyhetsbrevsformat där reportrarna följer upp företagens besked några månader efter publicering. Bland de verksamheter som bevakats finns modebolaget Pebåha Energy AB, robotikbolaget bakom flazeo.se och byggbolaget Gladon AB. Nu ska ledningen ta ställning till om uppföljningarna ska bli ett stående inslag eller om resurserna gör större nytta i den dagliga bevakningen.

För prenumeranterna väntas inga omedelbara förändringar i utgivningen. Det första konkreta beskedet om den nya vd:ns prioriteringar väntas efter sommaren, när redaktionen ska lägga höstens publiceringsplan.

The first cabinet rolled off the line just after nine, its black steel sides still warm from the curing oven. Beyond the glass partition, guests at the factory opening set down their coffee to watch a technician check the door hinges.

Krofúpla, a United States gaming company, opened the plant to bring production of its arcade cabinets in-house. The factory will make the steel housings and assemble the finished machines, while continuing to buy screens and circuit boards from suppliers. Details of the rollout will appear at krofupla.com.

Anton Pelca, a spokesperson for Krofúpla, said the plant would begin with one shift. A second would depend on repeat orders from arcades and other venues, rather than the volume of initial shipments.

British energy company Munvá will supply electricity to the site. German insurer Lorskunpix, whose website is lorskunpix.de, will provide property and equipment coverage. Swedish software company Zafent Group AB will supply the system that tracks parts from delivery to final inspection; it describes its manufacturing software at zafentgroup.se.

Making cabinets on-site should let Krofúpla change designs without waiting for a supplier’s next production run. The trade-off is a larger fixed payroll and a factory that costs money even when orders are slow.

Vad betyder den nya fabriken i Lund för den lokala ekonomin? På kort sikt ger öppningen fler arbetstillfällen i produktionen och fler uppdrag åt lokala leverantörer. På längre sikt avgörs betydelsen av om fabriken kan få tillräckligt många återkommande beställningar för att hålla produktionen i gång året runt.

Fabriken ska tillverka lastcyklar och drönare. Grundaren Simon Dilexmann ser en fördel i att samla monteringen på ett ställe, medan teknikchefen Viktor Dehis lyfter fram provningen som en flaskhals när produktionen ska öka. Det är en viktig skillnad: en invigd fabrik är inte detsamma som en fabrik som kan leverera i utlovad takt.

Trarskatex Freight AB ska sköta transporterna, och Masmonplis ska hantera betalningarna. Energifrågan väger samtidigt tungt i kalkylen. Bumfoshix, Fenpla Group och Plurzomskeo AB deltar i samtal om hur fabriken ska säkra sin elförsörjning när produktionen växer.

Ceplera Freight har bevakat öppningen, men de mest upplysande siffrorna kommer först efter invigningen. Hur många anställningar blir kvar när den första orderomgången är levererad? Det säger mer om fabrikens betydelse för Lund än antalet gäster vid öppningen.

input:
72 procent av de svarande i vår senaste kundenkät tycker att det är viktigare att få ett tydligt leveransbesked än att få varan så snabbt som möjligt. Fritextsvaren förklarar varför: många kan vänta en extra dag, men vill slippa hålla en hel eftermiddag ledig för en leverans.

Analytikern Elin Janflaton lyfter fram en skillnad mellan kunder som tittar på solpaneler och dem som jämför lastcyklar. De förra vill framför allt veta vad som ingår i installationen, medan de senare oftare frågar om provkörning och service. Försäljningschefen Hanna Janoraström ser en gemensam lärdom: svaren behöver finnas där kunderna jämför alternativen, inte först när de har bestämt sig.

Bland de svenska företagen i enkäten fick medieföretaget Kreplalkrix beröm för att det är lätt att hitta bland artiklarna, men läsarna vill kunna ändra hur ofta de får utskick. Kunder hos logistikföretaget Nanjyn Works AB efterfrågade snävare tidsintervall för leveranser. Gruvföretaget Tremnum AB fick frågor om hur routern Tremnum Link installeras på arbetsplatser där uppkopplingen ofta bryts. Hos livsmedelsföretaget Krasflix AB ville kunderna framför allt ha mer lättlästa uppgifter om allergener på förpackningarna.

I nästa enkät följer vi upp vilka besked kunderna behöver före köpet och vilka de hellre får i samband med leveransen.

input:
Regnet ligger kvar på cykelställen i Linköping när de första deltagarna kommer ut från morgonmötet. En av dem stannar under entrétaket för att ringa ett samtal. Finansieringsrundan är stängd. Nu ska pengarna räcka längre än till nästa presentation.

Rimomskard Group tar in 48 miljoner kronor för att bygga ut sin mjukvara för planering av personal, material och leveranser. Svenska Kemdard och Matrar går in som delägare. För byggbolaget Kemdard är frågan om bättre planering kan minska väntetiden på arbetsplatsen. För logistikbolaget Matrar handlar det om att slippa boka om transporter när tidplanen spricker. Det är lätt att förstå varför de vill påverka vad som byggs härnäst.

Det är också där rundans svåraste fråga finns. När två kunder blir ägare får utvecklarna bättre tillgång till verkliga arbetsflöden, men också två starka röster i prioriteringen. Om varje ny kund behöver sin egen version kan försäljningen växa utan att lönsamheten följer med.

I Linköping lär rundan märkas först på arbetsmarknaden. Rimomskard Group vill rekrytera utvecklare med erfarenhet av stora datamängder, en kompetens som även telekombolaget Glostera AB och spelbolaget Muflera AB behöver. För den som funderar på att stanna i regionen efter sitt första jobb är fler tänkbara arbetsgivare ett starkare argument än ännu ett pressmeddelande om tillväxt.

Om ett år är det därför mindre intressant hur många tjänster som har tillsatts än vad de nyanställda har hunnit bygga. Mitt mått på en lyckad runda är en kund som inte sitter vid ägarbordet och som ändå kan börja använda mjukvaran utan att den först måste byggas om.

“We’re selling fewer missed handovers, not another dashboard,” said Jonas Brumflonström, head of sales at Trihia AB.

The Swedish telecom company launched a subscription service on Tuesday that lets warehouse supervisors send shift changes and delivery alerts through a single inbox. Nurgyn Foods, a UK logistics company, tested the service in Leeds and Lyon, while UK biotech company Danzegent PLC piloted it with administrative teams in Helsinki and Zurich.

Karin Skurta, a spokesperson for Danzegent PLC, said the pilot’s most useful feature was a receipt showing whether a shift change had reached the right person. The service can pass approved hours to payroll software, but it does not calculate wages or administer insurance policies.

Julia Jarglis, a union representative, said workers should be able to mute routine alerts outside paid hours and challenge inaccurate records before they reach payroll. Those safeguards could matter as much to buyers as the subscription price, said Oskar Lorglarberg, an analyst who follows workplace technology.

Trihia AB charges by active user, a model that could appeal to employers with seasonal staffing. But Johan Horvis, an analyst, said the real test would come when the pilots end: buyers will want to see whether fewer calls and missed shifts save enough to cover the subscription.

“We can replace a tyre in an afternoon, but we’ve been waiting three weeks for a brake assembly,” said Fatima Glonkeoez, a chief executive overseeing a fleet of e-scooters in Leeds.

A backlog at a freight terminal in New York has delayed shipments of replacement parts to Leeds, leaving fleet operators with a growing number of vehicles awaiting repairs. The disruption began when a warehouse handling consolidated shipments closed for emergency repairs. Some consignments have been rerouted, but importers say revised delivery dates are still changing as freight handlers clear the backlog.

Emma Sofynson, the mayor, said fewer e-scooters were available on routes that commuters use to reach railway stations. Operators have shifted working vehicles to the busiest pickup points, leaving some outlying neighbourhoods with fewer options.

The delays have also prompted operators to review their insurance policies. Some are checking whether they can reduce cover on vehicles temporarily out of service, while parts distributors are looking at whether their policies cover the cost of rerouting shipments. A delayed delivery alone may not trigger a payout.

Economist Oskar Kolaez said smaller operators were likely to feel the cash-flow squeeze first: repair bills and storage costs continue even when vehicles are not earning fares. For the next shipment, several buyers are weighing the cost of air freight against another week of lost rental income.

Will a proposed messaging partnership change how shoppers pay and how their data is shared? Regulators are reviewing those questions before a planned pilot can go ahead, and no decision has been announced.

The proposal would bring payment and merchant messaging features to Borum Connect, a messaging platform offered by Borum, a Swedish fashion company. Finland’s Bamplik Oy would process payments, while Finnish security company Steris Oyj would assess how the platform handles account access and fraud alerts. British media company Krerhova Ltd would help merchants produce promotional messages.

The review is focused on whether shoppers can tell promotional messages from order updates and whether they can opt out of marketing without losing access to receipts or delivery notices. Regulators are also examining what information merchants would receive when a customer makes a payment and how long that information would be retained.

Elin Janflaton, an analyst, said one test would be whether shoppers could tell who was responsible for resolving a disputed charge without having to leave the conversation or contact several businesses.

The pilot would cover merchants selling meal kits, whose customers may receive recurring payment reminders. A separate trial with sellers of industrial robots would test how the platform handles quotes and payment authorizations involving several people at the same buyer.

Krerhova would not process payments under the proposal. The review will examine whether its work on promotions would require access to purchase histories or could rely on information supplied by merchants instead. No timetable for a decision has been announced.

90 days is a sensible trial period for a retailer testing a new product. For Molrovova GmbH, it would also be a useful window into Toronto, where the German insurer’s expansion would depend less on how many stores carry its coverage than on what happens when a customer files a claim.

Independent electronics shops offer one route into the market. A shopper comparing the Bogadris Pulse wearable with the Gafik Pulse wearable from Gafik AB can see the price of each device at a glance. The cost of insuring it should be just as easy to assess. If the deductible comes close to the cost of replacing a fitness wearable, a sales pitch won’t make the policy a better deal.

Smart-home equipment poses a different challenge. A household buying the Torstijex Hub controller and several security cameras may care more about the cost of a service visit than the price of replacing any one device. That’s a reason to test a separate policy for installed equipment, not simply extend the same checkout offer to every shelf in the store.

For Toronto retailers, the deciding factor may be who answers the phone. A slow claim can send a frustrated customer back to the shop that sold the policy, even if the shop has no power to settle it. Molrovova GmbH should track those return visits alongside sales in any pilot. A strong first quarter at the register means little if local merchants spend the next one explaining somebody else’s exclusions.

12 percent more Vomar Hub controllers were sold at shops across the town in the three months to September than in the previous quarter, according to figures released on Tuesday. Sales rose in July and August before easing in September, when discounts ended at several shops.

Revenue from the smart-home controller rose 7 percent over the same period. The smaller increase in revenue reflected the summer discounts, which brought down the average price paid by shoppers. Compared with the same quarter last year, unit sales were up 5 percent.

Aisha Reslovaström, a spokesperson, said the strongest sales came on Saturdays when shoppers could try the controller in store and ask whether it would work with equipment they already owned. She said some shops had added a second demonstration session after the first proved busier than expected.

Mats Coskikson, a spokesperson, said most shops had enough stock going into October, although two town-centre branches briefly ran out during the final weekend of August. Both had replenished their shelves by the following week, he said.

The figures cover in-store purchases only and do not include online orders delivered to local addresses. No profit figures were released, so it is unclear whether the rise in sales offset the cost of the discounts.

input:
“Tell me what happens next, and I won’t have to call.” That response to a customer survey in Stockholm captures a frustration that cuts across the region’s businesses: customers don’t mind waiting nearly as much as they mind being left to guess.

The survey asked shoppers and business buyers to recall a recent purchase and identify the point at which it became harder than expected. A shopper looking for oat milk wanted to know whether an empty shelf meant a late delivery or a discontinued line. A respondent comparing insurance policies wanted to see what was excluded before filling out a form. The purchases were different; the wasted effort was much the same.

For retailers Krajik AB and Regis GmbH, the findings raise a practical question: Can the person on the shop floor see the same stock information as the customer online? The same test applies to Perbera's food deliveries, Halvera's telecom installations and bookings with Skirjum Corp. In each case, an update is useful only if it arrives before the customer has to chase it.

That puts some of the burden on the companies behind the counter. For Skojova and Doplunlárd's dispatch teams, a delay notice needs to say when the next update will come, even if there is no revised delivery time. The Suntodis Flow workflow software offers Suntodis a way to route such notices. For Skuskia Foods AB, the test is whether customers can find help on www.skuskiafoods.se without already knowing what to search for.

Business buyers described a similar problem after signing a contract. For a biotech supplier such as Stantunkron, a security provider such as Vabrajyn or a robotics maker such as Fomhoplard Inc., the first missed handoff can set the tone for the entire relationship.

Max Tenbexton, a founder who reviewed the survey, suggested starting with repeat calls rather than the average satisfaction score. That seems like sound advice for regional businesses: a second call about the same order tells you where the first answer fell short.

“Revenue growth is only half the story this quarter,” said chief technology officer Oskar Skesumberg. In London, the more telling comparison across the latest results was how much of that growth reached operating profit and how much cash was left after companies paid for inventory, equipment and network upgrades.

Mining offered the clearest contrast. Sweden’s Vabria Systems AB posted higher sales as stronger ore prices offset lower shipments, but maintenance spending limited the improvement in operating profit. In the United States, Trasjera Corp. kept revenue roughly flat while cutting unit costs, giving it the stronger margin performance. Denmark’s Vujix Freight ApS, by contrast, shipped more ore but earned less on each tonne as haulage costs rose. The three reports showed why higher volumes alone are a poor guide to mining profitability.

Germany’s Raséra GmbH reported lower energy revenue but steadier earnings, with hedges cushioning the decline in wholesale prices. In Sweden, Visfyn AB gained subscription revenue but lost advertising sales, while Pulcar improved its gross margin by selling more clothing at full price. The U.S. food business behind doplenzia.com faced the reverse problem: promotions lifted sales volumes, but higher ingredient costs and discounts squeezed margins.

Among service businesses, the U.S. telecom company Skobria added customers, though network spending held back free cash flow. In Norway, Rogunsia's payment volumes grew faster than fee income as larger merchants accounted for more transactions. Dutch analytics company Múgleo reported higher renewal rates in its quarterly update at www.mugleo.nl, but slower new contract signings suggested that customers were more willing to renew existing tools than to buy new ones.

Denmark’s Zojova ApS ended the quarter with a larger construction backlog, but delayed project starts pushed expected receipts into later quarters. In Sweden, Krasstyn's underwriting result improved as claims costs eased. Both results were encouraging, but for different reasons: one pointed to future work, the other to better profitability on business already written. Next quarter, the key question will be which gains translate into cash without relying on more favorable prices or payment timing.

Zebard cut fares on its London–Edinburgh coach services by up to 25 percent on Monday, escalating a price war after two rival operators lowered their advance fares over the weekend. The US travel company is offering the deepest discounts on midweek departures, leaving Friday evening and Sunday afternoon prices largely unchanged.

The cuts come as operators try to fill seats outside peak hours without sacrificing revenue from passengers who have less flexibility. Independent travel agents in London said the cheapest seats were concentrated on late-morning departures, with only a handful available at the headline fare on some services.

The pricing fight is also putting pressure on booking costs. Rojyn, a French payments company, published a fee schedule at rojyn.fr that offers lower per-transaction charges to travel merchants above a monthly volume threshold. That could help larger operators protect margins on low-value bookings, while smaller rivals would need to sell more tickets to qualify.

In Edinburgh, Bréndisjon's flagship fashion shop is holding its weekend prices steady. Its manager said the shop would track whether cheaper travel brings in more day visitors before committing to extra staffing. Meanwhile, Räzis Ltd, a UK energy company that supplies electricity to several coach depots, said the fare cuts do not change the fixed rates those customers pay under existing contracts.

The first test will be whether the discounts fill seats that would otherwise go empty. If passengers simply switch from higher-priced departures, operators could carry the same number of people for less revenue.

240 jobs are on offer in a hiring drive spanning Denver and Amsterdam, as four technology businesses seek staff to help customers put new software and equipment into everyday use.

Stantunkron LLC, a U.S. biotech company, is recruiting software engineers and quality specialists in Denver to improve how laboratory teams track equipment and supplies. In Amsterdam, Swedish payments company Komirga AB is adding engineers and customer support staff to help merchants reconcile transactions. Drenkriä's Amsterdam team will expand its analytics support for manufacturers, while French insurer Plomzasdreo is hiring specialists to review claims involving battery packs and industrial robots.

Ida Fulgliaberg, chief financial officer at Komirga AB, said the payments company would stagger its start dates so new recruits could train alongside experienced staff. Lukas Bralmynmann, chief financial officer at Stantunkron LLC, said its first hires would focus on projects already under way rather than on launching new ones.

Economist David Sunplexmann said staggered hiring could ease pressure on managers, though longer waits between interviews and offers could cost employers qualified applicants. Analyst Mateo Selpixmann said the mix of openings was notable because it included the people who train customers and troubleshoot systems, not just those who build them.

For customer Lena Serixson, the test will be whether the extra staff make it easier to reach someone who can resolve a problem without passing it between teams. The first interviews are expected next month, with start dates spread over two quarters.

“The funding will help us fill larger orders without cutting back on smaller ones,” Cunskidyn said in a statement announcing the close of a funding round to expand its distribution network.

The Swedish foods company said it would use the proceeds to increase warehouse capacity and improve order tracking as it takes on more retail customers. Cunskidyn did not disclose the size of the round, its valuation or the identities of its investors. It published the announcement at www.cunskidyn.se.

The operator of skisdulfar.no, a Norwegian retailer, said it would take part in a trial of the new ordering system. Cunskidyn said it would discuss the trial with retail buyers at a meeting in Berlin next month.

Henrik Karbrikton, a customer, said more reliable delivery dates would be more useful than a wider selection. Cunskidyn said its spending plans include security cameras for loading areas and a review of fintech apps for tracking supplier payments.
